description:
The BS program in accountancy provides a broad-based education in business and a comprehensive education in accounting. The W. P. Carey School of Business accountancy programs are widely recognized for their high-quality instruction and the excellence of their graduates. The programs focus on understanding the role of accounting in society as well as the underlying concepts of accounting. Students are encouraged to develop a sense of inquiry, a desire for lifelong learning and the ability to adapt to a changing professional environment.

Students learn how to provide services that assure the reliability of information and how to design and implement information systems used to generate data for decision-making. Students gain a deeper understanding of areas such as taxation, auditing, financial reporting and management accounting. Because the school attracts many students who have had international experiences, a strong emphasis is placed on preparing students for global business opportunities.

Graduates often begin their careers with professional services firms, in business or in government. Graduates are well prepared to advance quickly in their chosen fields. The BS program in accountancy may be appropriate for students who are not planning to seek professional certification as a CPA. Most states, including Arizona, require 150 semester hours of education for CPA certification. This program requires 120 credit hours.
Accreditation status: The accountancy BS program at ASU is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB). The W. P. Carey School of Business is one of the original 16 schools to have both its business and accounting programs accredited by AACSB International. This represents the highest standard of achievement for business schools worldwide. Programs that earn accreditation confirm their commitment to quality and continuous improvement through a rigorous and comprehensive peer review. Less than five percent of the more than 16,000 business schools worldwide have been accredited.

description:
The BS program in actuarial science provides a strong foundation in mathematics, statistics and business for students interested in a career as an actuarial professional. The program prepares students to pass the initial actuarial exams administered by the Society of Actuaries and the Casualty Actuarial Society.

In addition to fulfilling the mathematics and statistics requirements of the program, students take courses in computer science, economics, finance, accounting and other business areas.

The Society of Actuaries has recognized this program for its quality curriculum, and it is on the society's list of Universities and Colleges with Actuarial Programs.

The aeronautical management technology program at ASU provides a technical foundation in the aviation field with a management focus. The air traffic management concentration prepares students for a career in air traffic control. The curriculum meets the Federal Aviation Administration requirements for graduates of an approved program to be recommended for the Air Traffic-Collegiate Training Initiative. Upon graduation, students may be eligible to bypass the first five weeks of initial qualification training at the FAA Academy. Graduates also may be eligible to take the air traffic selection and training exam earlier than the general public. This is a competitive program; space is limited. Students will spend an average of 15 to 20 hours a week in specialized air traffic control labs.
Accreditation status: This program is accredited by the Aviation Accreditation Board International.
Program name: Aeronautical Management Technology (Air Traffic Management), BS

description:
The aeronautical management technology program is a management-oriented degree program designed to prepare graduates for a variety of careers in the aviation industry. The program provides students with a strong foundation of aviation knowledge and skills through a multidisciplinary program with a choice of one of three concentrations: air traffic management, air transportation management or professional flight.

The air transportation management concentration curriculum provides a broad perspective of aviation management and operations. The coursework provides a strong business and management foundation applicable to all facets of the aviation industry, from general aviation to commercial air transportation and from civilian to military aviation. The program is specifically designed to prepare graduates for a wide variety of professional careers in the air transportation industry, including airline management and operations, air cargo management and logistics, airport management and operations, corporate aviation management, and government and non-government aviation and aerospace organizations.

Graduates of the air transportation management concentration have a broad understanding of the airline and corporate aviation industries as well as the airport's role within the national airspace system. They are trained in aviation safety, security, operations and management and are prepared for a variety of career paths. Students learn to implement and manage systems that are key to a safe and efficient air transportation system and that move people and goods safely around the world.

The aeronautical management technology program is accredited by the Aviation Accreditation Board International.
Accreditation status: The aeronautical management technology program is accredited by the Aviation Accreditation Board International.
Program name: Aeronautical Management Technology (Air Transportation Management), BS

description:
The aeronautical management technology program prepares students for a variety of leadership and management positions in the aviation industry. This concentration provides students with the required aeronautical knowledge and skills to earn a commercial pilot certificate with multiengine and instrument ratings.

In addition to general education requirements, students take courses in aviation weather, safety, security, human factors, air traffic control and airport management. The program culminates with two capstone courses in which students solve real-world aviation problems.

Professional flight students can complete their private pilot certificate at a flight provider of their choice before entering the program. Students complete the instrument, commercial, multiengine and certified flight instructor courses with ATP Flight School, ASU's affiliate for flight training. Graduates of the program are eligible for a R-ATP certificate at 1,000 flight hours, per FAA regulations.
Accreditation status: The Aeronautical Management Technology (Professional Flight) BS is accredited by the Aviation Accreditation Board International.

description:
The aeronautical management technology program is a management- and business-focused degree for students interested in a broad range of careers in the aerospace industry, both in the flight and in the ground support areas. This program provides students with a strong foundation in technical areas, including:

aircraft flight systems
aircraft propulsion
air traffic control
aviation safety
unmanned aerial systems

The program also develops students' skills in:

aviation law
financial accounting
human factors
leadership
management
marketing

This unique combination of technical and business knowledge prepares graduates for a wide range of leadership roles in the aviation industry.

The unmanned aerial systems concentration provides students with knowledge in all aspects of unmanned aerial systems, including:

design
operations
policy
systems
uses
Accreditation status: The aeronautical management technology (unmanned aerial systems) program is accredited by the Aviation Accreditation Board International.
Program name: Aeronautical Management Technology (Unmanned Aerial Systems), BS

description:
The aerospace engineering BSE program with a concentration in aeronautics provides a broad and challenging, high-quality education that prepares students for the practice of engineering at a professional level. The program develops graduates with the technical and critical-thinking skills needed to design aircraft and propulsion systems for commercial and military use.

Students learn from leading experts in aerospace engineering, including five National Academy of Engineering members and 11 fellows of the American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics. Students can gain a competitive edge through participation in a number of student organizations and research labs.

Aerospace engineers learn the fundamentals of aerodynamics, stability and control, propulsion and structures to design flight vehicles that meet specified performance and safety requirements. The concentration in aeronautics focuses on the design of vehicles that fly within the Earth's atmosphere, such as airplanes, helicopters and unmanned aerial vehicles.
Accreditation status: The aerospace engineering BSE program with a concentration in aeronautics is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Program Criteria for Aerospace and Similarly Named Engineering Programs.

description:
The BSE program in aerospace engineering with a concentration in astronautics provides students with an education in the fundamental principles of aerospace engineering as well as specialized knowledge in the analysis and design of space vehicles and their subsystems. Graduates are well prepared for careers in the aerospace industry or for graduate study.

Aerospace engineering is the branch of engineering that focuses on the design, construction, testing and operation of vehicles that operate in the Earth's atmosphere and in space. Aerospace engineers are employed by the aerospace and defense industries, research and development laboratories and government agencies, and some graduates become astronauts.

Aerospace engineers develop new technologies for use in space exploration, commercial aviation, national defense systems and climate monitoring. They often specialize in one or more areas of aerospace engineering, including:

aerodynamics, the study of how air flows over and around aerospace vehicles and the forces the flow produces

flight mechanics, which is the study of the trajectory and rotational motion of vehicles in the air or in space

flight software and controls, which focuses on the design of the control systems to ensure the desired vehicle performance

propulsion, which is the design of engines and other devices to propel the vehicles in the atmosphere or in space

structural design and analysis, which focuses on the design of the physical configuration of the vehicle to withstand the aerodynamic and other forces to which it is subjected

Students receive a broad education in the fundamental principles of aerospace engineering as well as specialized knowledge in the analysis and design of space vehicles and their subsystems.

The program culminates in a senior-year capstone design experience in which students work in teams to design a complete aerospace vehicle, from initial concept to final design.
Accreditation status: The aerospace engineering (astronautics), BSE is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Aerospace and Similarly Named Engineering Programs Program Criteria.

description:
The aerospace engineering BSE program provides students with an education in the fundamental principles of aerospace engineering. The program focuses on developing the knowledge and skills necessary for the design and development of aerospace vehicles and systems. The curriculum offers a balance of theoretical and practical hands-on experiences and addresses the design of aircraft, spacecraft and related systems.

The autonomous vehicle systems concentration provides students the ability to apply fundamental aerospace engineering knowledge to autonomous vehicle systems. In addition to a set of core aerospace engineering courses that provide a strong foundation, the students are required to take a set of courses that offer hands-on experience in autonomous vehicles. Graduates with this concentration are well equipped to work in this fast-growing sector of the economy.

The aerospace engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.
Accreditation status: The aerospace engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

description: The BA program in African and African American studies is an interdisciplinary degree program in The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences that provides a comprehensive, holistic and rigorous introduction to the study of Africa and people of African descent throughout the world. The program aims to expose students to a full range of social, political, cultural and historical subjects, centered on the experiences of people of African descent. Students learn the histories and contemporary experiences of African Americans and other people in the African diaspora, as well as those living on the African continent. Students develop the skills necessary to analyze and evaluate information from a variety of sources and in various forms. They learn to critically examine complex social and historical issues, construct cogent arguments, and communicate their ideas effectively in both writing and speech. The program helps students develop a critical consciousness of the national and global connections relevant to people of African descent. It facilitates an understanding of how race and other socially constructed categories have shaped the lives and experiences of African-descended people. Students learn how to analyze the concepts of race and racism from an interdisciplinary perspective. This includes studying the social and historical contexts in which these ideas have been created and reproduced, how racial identities are constructed and how race continues to be a factor in contemporary society. The program provides students with a general education in the arts, humanities and social sciences. This ensures they acquire a solid foundation in the research and analytical methods used in these broad disciplines and are able to apply them to specific questions and issues. Students leave the program with highly marketable and transferable skills that prepare them for a wide range of careers in both the private and public sectors.
Program name: African and African American Studies, BA

description:
The BS program in aging is a comprehensive, multidisciplinary program designed to equip students with a deep understanding of the aging process from various perspectives, including social, psychological, biological and policy-related aspects. It focuses on the challenges and opportunities associated with an aging population.

The curriculum covers a wide range of topics, such as gerontology, health and aging, cognitive changes in later life, social policies affecting older adults, and ethical considerations in elder care.

The program provides students with the knowledge and skills necessary for careers in fields that serve older adults, such as health care, social services, policy-making and research. Graduates are prepared to contribute to the well-being of the aging population, addressing its diverse needs and promoting healthy and active aging.

This program provides students with a strong foundation in understanding aging. It includes a series of core courses with a variety of electives to choose from and a for-credit internship to gain real-world experience.

The agribusiness industry is a dynamic sector of the global economy. It is composed of a diverse set of private, public and nonprofit firms and organizations that provide inputs to production agriculture; produce, process, distribute and sell food, fiber and bio-energy products and services at the wholesale and retail levels; and provide financial and information services to the sector. The agribusiness program provides students with strong academic preparation in business, management and finance principles and in applied economics. The quantitative and analytical skills that students develop are highly valuable and readily transferrable to other sectors of the economy.

The BS program in agricultural business prepares students for careers in the dynamic and complex global food and agriculture industry. The curriculum provides a solid foundation in business management and economic principles for a successful career in the management, marketing and financing of ag-related businesses. In the rapidly evolving global and technological environment of the 21st century, the BS program in agricultural business provides students with the entrepreneurial and leadership skills to make complex business decisions. Students learn to apply economic principles and business management skills to solve problems in the food and agricultural industry.

The BS program in air traffic management provides students with a strong foundation in aviation studies along with an understanding of all facets of the air traffic control system. Students take courses in air traffic control, aviation meteorology, flight operations, aviation safety and human factors.

Graduates are prepared for careers in air traffic control and a variety of other aviation management roles.

The air traffic management program is an FAA-approved Collegiate Training Initiative program, which allows graduates to be recommended to the FAA for hire into air traffic controller positions.

In addition, students have the option to complete flight training requirements to become professional pilots. Flight training courses are offered via a partnership with a local FAA-approved flight provider. Students are responsible for the costs of flight training, which are in addition to and separate from ASU tuition and fees.
Accreditation status: The air traffic management program is an FAA-approved Collegiate Training Initiative program.

description:
The Bachelor of Science in American Indian studies is a multidisciplinary program focusing on the historical and contemporary experiences, perspectives and life ways of the Indigenous peoples of North America. The curriculum challenges students to consider new perspectives and worldviews.

Students learn how to analyze complex issues within a framework of Indigenous-centered knowledge, with an emphasis on tribally-driven, community-engaged research and partnerships that seek to advance tribal sovereignty and self-determination.

This program is based in American Indian studies, one of the leading Indigenous studies programs in the nation. It provides students with a strong foundation in a wide range of fields, including:

*   American Indian law and federal policy
*   community development
*   economic and political development
*   education
*   environmental justice
*   history
*   language and cultural revitalization
*   philosophy
*   religion

The curriculum's strong methodological emphasis prepares students for careers in tribal leadership, law, policy and administration as well as a range of public and private sector jobs in business, education, government and health care.

The program provides excellent preparation for graduate studies in American Indian studies and other social sciences, such as:

*   anthropology
*   history
*   political science
*   sociology

It also offers a solid foundation for professional schools in business, education, law, medicine and social work.

The BA program in American studies gives students the opportunity to explore the complex interplay of race, gender, class and other forms of social difference that have shaped American culture, both past and present.

Students investigate the ways in which various forms of culture and expression, from film and popular music to political rhetoric and legal documents, reflect, reinforce and sometimes challenge prevailing ideas about American identity.

Core courses provide students with foundational knowledge in American studies and critical training in cultural analysis. Students then go on to tailor their degrees by choosing from a rich menu of cross-listed courses offered by American studies and a host of other programs across the university.

Students are trained to analyze cultural texts of all kinds, to become more sophisticated readers and writers and to understand the historical contexts of American culture and experience. This training offers excellent preparation for graduate programs in the humanities and social sciences and for professional programs in law and education. The critical thinking, writing and research skills students develop can be adapted to a variety of careers in business, journalism, education, public service, politics and more.

The BS program in animal behavior prepares students for careers working with animals in a variety of settings such as conservation, research and animal welfare, as well as for graduate school in animal behavior or related disciplines (e.g., ecology, evolution, psychology, biology, etc.) and professional schools (e.g., veterinary medicine).

Students in this program are provided an interdisciplinary perspective on animal behavior, learning from faculty experts across multiple ASU academic units (School of Life Sciences, Department of Psychology, School of Social and Behavioral Sciences). Students gain a broad background in the sciences, with core classes on the mechanisms and evolution of animal behavior and electives in specialized topics in animal behavior (e.g., animal communication, social behavior, behavioral endocrinology, canine behavior, primatology). Students also are provided with hands-on experience by completing at least one animal behavior research experience, either in the field or in a laboratory setting. This offers students the opportunity to work in research laboratories with faculty experts in animal behavior.

The animal health, BS program is designed to meet all the prerequisites for application to a Doctor of Veterinary Medicine program. It differs from other preveterinary majors by including animal nutrition, animal physiology, anatomy and diseases in the curriculum. The program provides the general background in biological and physical sciences needed for advanced study in animal physiology, animal science and veterinary medicine.

The animal health curriculum gives students the opportunity to learn about many species, from livestock and poultry to companion animals and even some exotics. Students are encouraged to use electives to broaden their experience with animals.

Students who are interested in a preveterinary course of study should consider this major and are encouraged to visit the Preprofessional Advising Office website for more information regarding entrance to a veterinary program.

The Bachelor of Arts program in anthropology provides a broad-based approach to the study of humanity and human culture. It is designed to provide students with a multifaceted approach to the evolution of human biology and culture, to past civilizations and to human diversity around the globe.

Anthropology is holistic in its perspective, drawing from biological and social sciences and from humanities in its research and theory. This allows students to develop an understanding of different cultures and to better understand their own. Students learn about the human experience through classroom studies and research and through work in the field and laboratories.

Students are introduced to the principal subfields of the discipline: archaeology, sociocultural anthropology and physical anthropology.

The Bachelor of Science degree program in anthropology offers students a holistic study of the human condition from a variety of perspectives. It provides students with a strong theoretical background and research skills in anthropology and prepares them for further graduate study as well as careers in the public or private sectors.

Students focus on the scientific dimensions of the discipline through training in the theory and methods of biological anthropology and archaeology as well as through in-depth study of areas such as primatology, human evolution, human osteology, bioarchaeology, dental anthropology, medical anthropology, nutritional anthropology, paleopathology, archaeological method and theory, geoarchaeology, zooarchaeology and lithic analysis. The program also emphasizes advanced statistical methods and laboratory-based research. The BS option is particularly well-suited for those who wish to pursue a pre-health track or careers in forensic science or conservation archaeology.

Students in the BS degree program may elect to pursue a general anthropology track or a more specialized concentration in either anthropological sciences, environmental and social sustainability or medical anthropology.

The school offers unique opportunities for students to work with a range of world-renowned faculty at its research centers, including the Center for Bioarchaeological Research, the Center for Digital Antiquity, the Institute of Human Origins, and the Teotihuacan Research Laboratory. Students can also participate in one of its many summer study abroad programs or archaeological field schools and gain firsthand experience working in the field with leading experts in the discipline. The school also provides a range of laboratory-based opportunities for students to engage in research during the academic year.

The School of Human Evolution and Social Change is a leader in finding innovative solutions to the complex problems challenging the human world. The school's transdisciplinary approach helps its students and faculty understand the human story and provide a unique perspective on the human side of global challenges.

The Associate of Arts in apparel technical design is an intensive two-year program focused on the technical skills of apparel design and construction. The program provides the foundational knowledge required in technical aspects of the apparel industry and prepares students to become skilled professionals in various positions, including technical designer, patternmaker and product developer. Students will gain an understanding of apparel production, from concept to finished product, for the global fashion marketplace. Students will learn the following skills:

- industrial sewing
- patternmaking
- digital patternmaking
- garment construction
- production management
- technical design
- technical flat sketching
- Adobe Creative Suite

The BS program in applied biological sciences with a concentration in natural resource ecology provides a solid foundation in the biological sciences and teaches students to apply this knowledge to the management of natural resources.

The applied curriculum has a strong foundation in biological and physical sciences, with an emphasis on plant and animal ecology, conservation biology, wildlife management, fisheries management, restoration ecology, and landscape ecology. Students learn both in the classroom and in the field at the Polytechnic campus arboretum, in nearby natural areas such as the Sonoran Desert and the Superstition and San Tan mountains, and on regional field trips.

Graduates of the program work for government agencies, consulting firms, nonprofit organizations and in environmental education and research. The natural resource ecology concentration provides a strong background for students wishing to pursue graduate studies in natural resource management, ecology or conservation biology.
Program name: Applied Biological Sciences (Natural Resource Ecology), BS

description:
The applied biological sciences degree program with a concentration in pre-dental studies is a fast-paced, rigorous, relevant preprofessional program designed for students who want a strong foundation in the biological sciences in preparation for dental school.

The curriculum combines a broad-based approach to the various disciplines in the biological sciences with hands-on, research-based laboratory experiences and an emphasis on the critical-thinking skills needed for success in graduate school and in the dental profession.

Students in this program will complete most prerequisites for dental school as part of their major requirements.

Students complete challenging coursework in topics such as:

anatomy and physiology
biochemistry
cell and molecular biology
genetics

Students also gain in-depth experience in scientific laboratories.

The program features an accelerated block format for its biology courses. Students are immersed in a single subject for three-and-a-half weeks, which facilitates mastery of the material before moving to the next subject. Small class sizes (24 to 48 students per class) offer a personalized and supportive learning environment that encourages high academic achievement.

Students have access to a new, state-of-the-art facility featuring high-tech instrumentation that is unavailable on other ASU campuses.

This program provides excellent preparation for students interested in attending dental school as well as for those who wish to pursue a career in biological sciences or other preprofessional programs, such as pharmacy and optometry.

The BS program in applied biological sciences with a concentration in preveterinary medicine is a comprehensive, interdisciplinary program of study that allows students to focus on the biological sciences as they relate to animal health. The curriculum provides a strong scientific foundation that includes biology, chemistry, mathematics and physics.

The concentration in preveterinary medicine is tailored to meet the entrance requirements for veterinary school and to provide students with the scientific skills and knowledge required to be a competitive applicant to veterinary school and for a successful career in veterinary medicine or a related animal health field.

In addition to rigorous coursework, the preveterinary medicine concentration requires experiential learning in the form of an internship or undergraduate research. The program also provides opportunities for students to conduct research alongside faculty and to take part in study abroad programs.

The BS program in applied biological sciences with a concentration in secondary education in biology offers an interdisciplinary curriculum that allows students to focus on biology education at the secondary level. Students are provided with extensive training in biological sciences, including ecology, genetics, cellular and molecular biology and evolution, in addition to pedagogical coursework focused on training students for teaching in a formal secondary school setting.

Students learn how to teach biology through a combination of traditional coursework and hands-on experience in a variety of settings. Through the program's partnership with the Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College, students engage in a final semester of full-time student teaching in a secondary classroom. Upon completion of the degree, students are recommended for secondary certification in biology from the Arizona Department of Education.
Accreditation status: The Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College is accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation.
Program name: Applied Biological Sciences (Secondary Education in Biology), BS

description:
The BS program in applied biological sciences with a concentration in sustainable horticulture prepares students for a wide range of careers in horticulture through a solid foundation in plant biology and hands-on training in plant production. Graduates are well prepared to work in a variety of horticultural enterprises, such as plant nurseries, flower and vegetable production facilities, landscaping companies, and botanical gardens and arboreta, or to seek advanced degrees in horticulture, plant biology, plant science and related fields.

The curriculum is focused on the knowledge and skills required for careers in plant production and management, including plant identification and propagation, cultivation of horticultural crops, landscape management, and plant pest and disease management.

Students in this program benefit from the outstanding resources for horticulture at ASU's Polytechnic campus, including a modern greenhouse complex with automated environmental controls; extensive teaching gardens featuring a wide array of plants, including a collection of date palms and other desert-adapted species; and a research farm with facilities for plant production and plant science research.

description: The Bachelor of Science in applied biological sciences provides a strong foundation in the life sciences, chemistry, mathematics and physics. A solid understanding of these principles is critical to all areas of biology, whether related to medicine, veterinary science or research. The core of the program addresses cell and molecular biology, ecology and evolution and provides students with skills in critical thinking, writing and problem-solving. This core is supported by extensive hands-on learning experiences in laboratories and field settings, and with independent research opportunities available through faculty research laboratories. Students learn the scientific method and how to interpret and analyze data, making them proficient in using data to create solutions for the changing world. This degree program offers students a choice of several concentrations, allowing them to focus their studies in areas such as pre-veterinary medicine, sustainable horticulture, or applied biological data analytics.

Concentration name: Food Industry Management, Graphic Information Technology, Information Technology, Operations Management
description:
The Bachelor of Arts in applied business and technology solutions is a fully online program that addresses growing employer demand for a workforce with a broad set of business skills combined with the ability to apply technology in practical, problem-solving ways across a wide variety of industries.

The program's core business courses provide a foundational understanding of data analysis, finance and accounting, marketing and management in the contemporary workplace. In addition to a grounding in business principles, students develop practical technology skills through courses in information technology, graphic design and web development.

The program culminates in a senior-level capstone that applies business and technology knowledge and skills to a specific workplace challenge.
Program name: Applied Business and Technology Solutions, BA

description:
The BS program in applied computing with a concentration in cybersecurity focuses on the skills needed to design, implement and manage secure computer networks. Students learn how to build firewalls and other types of network security, and they practice skills for identifying network vulnerabilities and cybersecurity threats.

The curriculum provides a solid foundation in the principles of computing, including data structures, algorithms, computer architecture and object-oriented programming. Coursework provides students with the advanced knowledge they need in information security and data and information management.
Accreditation status: The applied computing, BS program is accredited by the Computing Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org. Student enrollment and graduation data are available at engineering.asu.edu/factbook/data.

Concentration name: ['Cybersecurity', 'Internet and Web Development', 'Network and Security Administration', 'Project Management']
description:
The BS program in applied computing provides a solid foundation in the core concepts of computing and information technology. Students learn how to apply problem-solving and critical-thinking skills and knowledge of computing and information technology in a variety of contexts and environments. The program emphasizes the importance of communication, ethics and professionalism, and it addresses a broad range of topics, including networking, security, databases, web systems and project management. Students learn how to configure, integrate and administer computing and information technology systems.

Students develop the skills necessary to work effectively as team members and leaders and gain comprehensive, hands-on experience by completing at least one substantial team-based project.

The curriculum allows students to choose a focus area to further develop their professional interests, such as cybersecurity, internet and web development, or network and security administration.

The Bachelor of Applied Science in applied leadership provides a dynamic, high-quality, accessible degree program that capitalizes on a student's technical education and experience by focusing on the supervision, management and leadership skills needed in a variety of industries. The program builds on a student's foundation of specialized knowledge with advanced coursework in leadership, management and supervision. Students learn to facilitate teamwork, lead projects, resolve workplace conflict, manage change, communicate effectively and supervise diverse teams. The program is designed for students who have earned an Associate of Applied Science degree from a regionally accredited institution. Students who do not possess an AAS degree may be considered for admission if they have significant and extensive work experience in one area of expertise.

The BS program in applied mathematics for the life and social sciences provides a deep understanding of mathematical concepts and methods that are used to explain and model phenomena in the life and social sciences.

Students develop rigorous skills in mathematical reasoning and advanced problem-solving through a wide range of topics that include:
-calculus
-differential equations
-discrete and continuous modeling techniques
-linear algebra
-numerical analysis
-probability and statistics

Through a flexible curriculum, students have the opportunity to study a variety of related subject areas to fit their specific interests, including:
-animal behavior
-biomedical research
-computational life sciences
-ecology
-epidemiology
-finance
-neuroscience
-social dynamics
-sustainability

The curriculum offers the necessary mathematical and computational tools to model and solve real-world problems. The program integrates coursework in mathematics and life and social sciences to give students the background needed for a successful career in a variety of fields and for advanced graduate studies.

A student pursuing a BS in applied mathematics for the life and social sciences is not allowed to also pursue a BS in:
-actuarial science
-computational life sciences
-mathematics
-mathematics (statistics)
-secondary education (mathematics)
Program name: Applied Mathematics for Life and Social Sciences, BS
