description:
The BS program in applied mathematics provides a strong foundation in the core areas of mathematics while also exploring connections to other fields. Students learn to use mathematics to solve practical problems in the physical, biological and social sciences as well as in engineering.

A distinctive feature of this program is the required area of concentration, a sequence of courses in a related field chosen in consultation with an academic advisor. This provides students with in-depth experience applying mathematics to another area.

This program offers extensive training in mathematical modeling and computation. Because this is a BS degree program, it has a higher science requirement than the BA program.

Graduates are prepared to pursue advanced degrees in mathematics or in another related field or to find employment in industry, technology or government.

The BA program in applied military and veterans studies focuses on the specific historical, cultural, institutional, political, and social issues attendant to the military and veteran communities. The major's curriculum provides an in-depth understanding of the central issues associated with military service and veteran status, especially with regard to health and wellness, social and institutional integration, and family and community. The program's core and related coursework prepares students to become more effective leaders and problem-solvers in the various sectors that interact with service members, veterans and their families. Students gain career-relevant training in leadership, community building and problem-solving, along with the development of the following valuable and transferable skills: communication, information literacy, critical thinking and analysis, social perceptiveness and systems evaluation. Students develop these skills in applied learning environments and research opportunities. Through interdisciplinary coursework and training, the program teaches students about the historical contexts of U.S. and international military conflicts, the psychological consequences of combat and military service, military family dynamics, veteran health issues, and veteran transition and reintegration challenges. Graduates will be prepared to assist service members, veterans and their families through professional roles in government, nonprofit and private sectors, and to pursue a wide variety of graduate and professional degrees.
Program name: Applied Military and Veterans Studies, BA

description: The BS program in applied nutrition and health prepares students with knowledge of the principles of human nutrition and health to pursue careers in a variety of settings. The program helps students understand the vital role that nutrition plays in promoting health and preventing disease throughout the life cycle. Students gain a solid foundation in the biological and chemical sciences in order to better understand the physiological and biochemical functions of nutrients. The curriculum focuses on the practical application of nutrition knowledge to promote positive health outcomes for individuals and communities. Graduates are well prepared to advance their education through graduate study in nutrition or health-related fields, or to enter the workforce in areas such as community and public health, corporate wellness, government agencies, and the food industry.

Concentration name: Business, Computational Physics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Materials Science and Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Physics Teaching
description:
The applied physics BS program combines a professional physics curriculum with substantial experiences in a related field such as engineering, computational science or finance. This program provides an excellent background for a career in a wide variety of engineering and technology-related fields.

The applied physics degree program is appropriate for students wishing to pursue careers in industry or government as well as for those contemplating graduate studies in engineering, computer science, data science, medical physics or other related fields.

Students select a concentration from the list below, with one concentration focused on computational physics.

The Bachelor of Science in applied psychology provides a broad-based liberal arts education focused on understanding human behavior from a variety of perspectives. It provides students with opportunities to acquire research and other critical thinking skills valued by employers, including in human resources, management, marketing, sales, and in human services and other related settings.

The curriculum features a research sequence culminating in an advanced research lab in which students conduct an original research project, from idea generation through data collection, data analysis and final presentation. The program also offers an internship experience in which students apply their knowledge in a community setting.

Graduates are well prepared for the workforce or for graduate-level work in a variety of fields, such as social work and law.

The BS program in applied quantitative science provides students with a solid foundation in mathematics and statistics and the skills to apply this knowledge to solve problems in science and technology. Students develop problem-solving, critical-thinking, modeling, and communication skills to answer real-world questions with data and statistics, including in-depth consulting and research experiences that help students develop the skills they need to lead data-driven projects after graduation. The curriculum provides excellent preparation for students interested in careers using mathematics and statistics in business, industry and government, or in further graduate studies in mathematics, statistics and other related fields. With a choice of focus areas, students are able to tailor their degree to their interests and career goals.

The Bachelor of Applied Science degree with a concentration in applied leadership is a degree program for students who have earned an associate of applied science degree from a regionally accredited institution. AAS degree programs are generally not designed for transfer to a four-year institution, but this BAS program allows students to apply their AAS credits to a bachelor's degree.

The BAS program with a concentration in applied leadership builds upon students' technical expertise obtained through their AAS degrees to enhance their professional careers by providing them with additional opportunities in higher education. This degree is designed to develop skills in leadership and management that can be directly applied to multiple business sectors. Coursework focuses on providing a fundamental knowledge of management, project management, organizational behavior and leadership.

The degree program offers a large number of elective hours, allowing students to select a path of study best suited to their individual career aspirations.

The Bachelor of Applied Science in project management provides an interdisciplinary program of study for students with an AAS degree from a regionally accredited institution. The program builds upon a strong technical foundation to provide the knowledge and skills necessary for success in a supervisory or managerial role in a project-driven organization.

The applied science degree with a concentration in project management requires 90 credit hours for the AAS degree and a minimum of 30 credit hours of upper-division coursework at ASU. Specific coursework requirements are determined by the student's AAS degree and the ASU academic unit that offers the concentration.
Accreditation status: The project management concentration in the BAS program is accredited by the PMI Global Accreditation Center for Project Management Education Programs (GAC). The GAC is the world's leading specialized accrediting body for project management and related degree programs, and GAC accreditation is a testament that a program has been rigorously assessed and that its scale, scope and quality meet comprehensive, global standards.

Concentration name: ['Applied Leadership', 'Food and Nutrition Management', 'Graphic Information Technology', 'Internet and Web Development', 'Logistics', 'Operations Management', 'Project Management']
description:
The Bachelor of Applied Science degree program in applied science is a degree completion program for students with an Associate of Applied Science degree from a regionally accredited institution. The program provides students with the opportunity to pursue a bachelor's degree, and it emphasizes the skills of communication, leadership and critical thinking necessary for career advancement.

Students complete one of seven concentrations, depending on their interests, background and career goals. Concentrations are available in: applied leadership, food and nutrition management, graphic information technology, internet and web development, logistics, operations management, or project management.

The curriculum is designed to help students transition from the role of technician to that of a professional in business and industry.

This program is not intended for students who have never attended college or who have fewer than 30 transferable credit hours. Students with fewer than 60 transfer credit hours may take ASU general studies coursework while enrolled in the program.

The bachelor's degree program in architectural studies is a preprofessional degree program that provides a foundation in the field of architecture. It prepares students for a variety of career paths or for a two-year Master of Architecture program, which is the accredited professional degree required for licensure. The program provides a broad liberal education along with a foundation of architectural knowledge. The curriculum includes a strong base in sustainability, social and community engagement, and urban design principles in the context of the desert region of the American Southwest. The program also has a strong emphasis on hands-on design and fabrication skills, with access to state-of-the-art facilities and technology. This preprofessional degree is useful for students who want a solid foundation in architecture to work in related fields such as construction management, landscape architecture, interior design and urban planning. With a focus on sustainable and resilient design, students are equipped to tackle the pressing environmental and social challenges of the 21st century. The four-year bachelor's degree in architectural studies at ASU is a preprofessional program and is not accredited by the National Architectural Accrediting Board. The professional, NAAB-accredited Master of Architecture is also offered by The Design School. Graduates of the BSD program may apply to the two-year MArch program. Other students may apply to the 3+ MArch program.
Accreditation status: The four-year bachelor's degree in architectural studies at ASU is a preprofessional program and is not accredited by the National Architectural Accrediting Board.

description:
The BFA program in art with a concentration in art education prepares students for careers as art teachers in K-12 schools and for a variety of other roles as artists, teachers and community leaders.
The curriculum is studio-based and prepares students to become confident, knowledgeable and skilled artist-teachers. Students develop their artistic voice through intensive studio work and an independent exploration of materials, concepts and processes in a variety of media.
Through their art education coursework, students also develop a professional teaching portfolio that is aligned to state and national standards, including a teaching philosophy and resume, standards-based lesson plans, a classroom management plan, and other resources to use in their future classrooms. Students gain teaching experience through a variety of field placements, including a semester-long student teaching residency.
In addition to the art education concentration, the school also offers a BFA program in art with a concentration in digital photography. Students interested in that area of study should apply to that program directly.

The Bachelor of Arts in art with a concentration in art history offers a broad humanistic education that focuses on the study of artworks and architecture from a variety of cultures and historical periods. Students develop skills in critical and visual analysis as well as scholarly research and writing.

Students in the art history program work closely with a renowned faculty of scholars whose teaching and research cover a wide range of fields, including:

*    the ancient Mediterranean
*    Asia
*    colonial to contemporary Latin America
*    early modern and modern Europe
*    the history of photography
*    the Islamic world
*    modern and contemporary U.S.

The curriculum is designed to give students a strong foundation in the art of a wide variety of time periods and cultures while also providing opportunities to focus on specific areas of interest. The art history program places emphasis on the theoretical and methodological diversity that comprises the study of art and visual culture today. Students may complement their art history studies with course work in studio art, and they are strongly encouraged to pursue a foreign language and to study abroad. Students are also encouraged to complement the major with a minor, a certificate program or a second major.

The School of Art's extensive programming, including the visiting artists and scholars lecture series, provides a stimulating environment for the study of art history. The ASU Art Museum and other area museums, including the Phoenix Art Museum, Heard Museum and Scottsdale Museum of Contemporary Art, offer students valuable opportunities for research and museum experience, including internships. An active art history student organization, the Art History Society, also organizes special events and brings in guest speakers.

Graduates find rewarding careers in a range of art-related professions, such as in museums, galleries, arts administration, publishing and education. The BA in art history also provides excellent preparation for graduate studies.
Accreditation status: The Herberger Institute for Design and the Arts is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Art and Design.

description:
The BFA in art with a concentration in art studies is a transdisciplinary, research-focused degree. The program is specifically designed to accommodate the needs of transfer students who have an associate degree.

The program gives students the opportunity to learn in an environment where they have access to outstanding faculty, facilities and an internationally recognized art museum.

The curriculum is flexible and can be customized to the student's area of interest, whether that is continuing in a single medium, working across a variety of media or exploring a research topic through a variety of methods.

During their final semester, students in the art studies program develop and present a final body of work that can be research- or studio-based. Students complete their experience with a capstone exhibition or presentation and a professional practices course that prepares them for a career in the arts.
Accreditation status: The School of Art is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Art and Design.

description:
The BFA in art with a concentration in ceramics focuses on contemporary and traditional art practices. Students develop technical skills and historical knowledge while developing their personal artistic voice. The curriculum is conceptually driven, process-oriented and technically rigorous.

The curriculum covers a broad range of ceramic processes, including hand building, wheel throwing, glaze calculation, clay formulation, and kiln firing and design. Students use a variety of firing techniques including gas, electric, soda, salt, raku and wood. The curriculum is enhanced with visiting artists, student exhibitions and field trips.

The program emphasizes the development of professional skills in preparation for a career as a studio artist, artist-in-residence, educator or designer for industry or as preparation for graduate studies.
Accreditation status: The School of Art is a part of the Herberger Institute for Design and the Arts at Arizona State University. The school is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Art and Design. The teacher certification program is accredited by the National Council for Accreditation of Teacher Education.

description:
The BFA program in art with a concentration in digital photography provides students with a broad understanding of the important role of photography in art and culture. The program is designed to develop students' practical and conceptual skills through an innovative curriculum and state-of-the-art facilities.

Students are encouraged to develop a personal aesthetic in a collaborative environment through a variety of elective courses, including:
- analog photography
- bookmaking
- color photography
- intermedia
- photo history
- video art

Students have access to darkrooms and a wide array of digital technology, enabling a broad range of personal expression. The photography program in the School of Art is renowned and is consistently ranked among the top 10 in the country.

Students in this program may not declare a concurrent major in the School of Art. All BFA students in art are required to complete an exit portfolio of their work prior to graduation.
Accreditation status: The ASU School of Art is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD).

description:
The bachelor's degree program in art with a concentration in drawing offers an intensive studio art experience.

The curriculum is focused on contemporary and traditional approaches to drawing and is designed for students who want to establish a professional practice in art. Students receive a broad foundation in studio arts and a focused education in drawing. Students are encouraged to develop an individual and unique voice.

The BFA is a pre-professional degree that helps students develop a strong portfolio of work in preparation for a career as a practicing artist. Additionally, graduates who go on to advanced degree programs are well prepared for the rigors of graduate study.
Accreditation status: The School of Art is a member of the National Association of Schools of Art and Design. The BFA program in art with a concentration in drawing is an accredited, professional degree for students who intend to become professional artists.

description:
The BFA program in art with a concentration in fibers provides a strong foundation in the concepts, techniques and processes of the fiber arts while encouraging a broad, interdisciplinary and experimental approach to materials and ideas.

The curriculum is broad and diverse. Students explore a range of contemporary and historical concepts and processes, including:

- weaving, surface design (dyeing and printing)
- stitching
- felting
- basketry
- sculptural and conceptual approaches
- new technologies

The program encourages students to investigate the rich history of fibers, both as a fine art and in its relationship to material culture and to develop their own critical and aesthetic direction.

In their final year, BFA students focus on the development of a strong, cohesive and professional body of studio work. This studio work culminates in the BFA thesis exhibition in the spring.

The BFA program in art with a concentration in intermedia offers a course of study that focuses on emerging and innovative forms of expression. The intermedia concentration provides students with access to a wide variety of tools and methods, from traditional skills to new media. This approach reflects contemporary art practice where artists combine and choose the skills, ideas and media that best suit their practice.

Students are encouraged to develop a course of study that provides them with an understanding of a variety of different approaches to making art, leading to a personal, focused studio practice. The concentration includes a sequence of courses in digital processes that provide grounding in new media, as well as a selection of required studio courses from different areas. Students are expected to complete a wide range of elective courses to satisfy the remaining credit hours for the degree. These electives may be from any of the studio areas, including: animation, ceramics, drawing and painting, fibers, metals, photography, printmaking, sculpture, and video and digital art.

The BFA program in art with a concentration in metals prepares students for a successful career as a studio artist.

The curriculum is designed to provide students with a deep understanding of the historical and contemporary context of the metalsmithing and jewelry field, along with a mastery of a wide variety of techniques and processes.

Students in the metals program learn to use metal as a medium for artistic expression. They have the opportunity to study a range of metals techniques and concepts including:

body adornment
fabrication
forming
functional objects
jewelry
sculpture
small-scale casting

The curriculum fosters critical thinking and the development of a personal aesthetic, which guides students toward a focused and independent body of creative work. It prepares students for a variety of pursuits after graduation, including a career as a professional studio artist and for graduate study in a Master of Fine Arts program.

The BFA program in art with a concentration in painting provides students with a strong foundation in contemporary and traditional painting practices. Students develop technical and conceptual skills to realize their individual artistic vision.

The program curriculum includes a range of studio art, art history and theory classes. Students may take electives from other disciplines, fostering a dynamic and diverse range of influence and interdisciplinary inquiry.

The program fosters a vibrant and inclusive community of student artists. They are mentored by a faculty of distinguished artists who are active nationally and internationally.

The School of Art's state-of-the-art facilities include spacious, well-lit painting studios with natural light as well as individual BFA student studios. Students can access a well-equipped woodshop, digital lab and other facilities.

Students have access to renowned museums on campus and in the Phoenix metropolitan area as well as a dynamic local art scene and many galleries and alternative spaces. The ASU Art Museum has a significant collection and an exciting, contemporary exhibition program, and the school's galleries feature student, faculty and visiting artist exhibitions. Visiting artist and scholar lectures and studio visits enhance the curriculum and provide a glimpse into the professional art world.

The program culminates in a senior exhibition.
Accreditation status: The School of Art is a part of the Herberger Institute for Design and the Arts, which is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Art and Design.

description:
The BFA program in art with a concentration in printmaking offers a comprehensive curriculum that prepares students to be practicing artists and skilled printmakers. The program balances the development of technique with the cultivation of critical thinking skills, historical knowledge, visual literacy and a strong personal voice. The printmaking concentration fosters experimentation and innovation within a broad range of traditional and contemporary printmaking media, including:

intaglio
lithography
relief
screen printing
monotype
book arts
digital printmaking

Students in the program work toward a professional body of work, culminating in a BFA thesis exhibition. This body of work is developed in an atmosphere of critical dialogue with other students and faculty.

The goal of the BFA program in art with a concentration in printmaking is to prepare students to leave the university as professional artists and creative thinkers with a strong personal vision, prepared for careers in the arts or for graduate study.
Accreditation status: The School of Art is a part of the Herberger Institute for Design and the Arts, which is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Art and Design.

description:
The BFA program in art with a concentration in sculpture provides students with a broad range of technical and conceptual skills that equip them for a professional career as an artist. A strong emphasis is placed on experimentation with materials, techniques and ideas.

Students have the opportunity to participate in a diverse curriculum that addresses contemporary art issues, art theory and art history. The curriculum promotes critical thinking, and the program's faculty of artists, critics and art historians provide a context for rigorous intellectual and artistic inquiry.

Students are offered a diverse, hands-on learning experience that addresses current creative research practices, as well as the history of the medium.
Accreditation status: The School of Art is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Art and Design.

description:
The bachelor's degree program in art history offers students a humanistic course of study. Students develop visual literacy, critical thinking and writing skills that allow them to analyze and interpret visual culture.
The study of art history prepares students for a wide range of careers in diverse fields, including art conservation, art law, business, communication, cultural affairs, education and fashion, as well as work in galleries and museums. The program provides the intellectual foundation for advanced graduate study in art history and related disciplines.

The BA program in art with a concentration in art studies provides students with a comprehensive liberal arts education with a focus in art history, museum studies and art-making studio practices. The degree promotes critical and creative thinking and provides students with skills to address complex social problems.

The art studies program prepares students to meet the challenges of the 21st century by providing them with a broad understanding of art history and museum studies and the skills of visual analysis within social, historical, cultural and political contexts. Students receive an in-depth education in the history of art and research methods and an introduction to museum studies.

Students also develop a foundation in studio art by taking courses in areas such as:
animation
ceramics
drawing
fibers
intermedia
metals
painting
photography
printmaking
sculpture
woods

The diverse curriculum prepares graduates for work in the creative industries or to pursue graduate studies in art history, museum studies, art education or studio art. This program is available for students at ASU Local.

The BA program in Asia studies provides students with interdisciplinary training to pursue careers related to Asia in education, government and the private sector. The program offers two tracks: East Asia and South/Southeast Asia.

Students develop proficiency in at least one Asian language (Chinese, Indonesian, Japanese, Korean, Sanskrit or Vietnamese) and gain in-depth knowledge of the histories, cultures, politics and economies of the region of their choice.

This program is designed for students interested in:

ancient and modern history
art and literature
culture and film
globalization
language studies
political and economic systems
religious traditions

A study abroad program in Asia is strongly recommended to further language proficiency and understanding of other cultures. Students also can combine their study of Asia with other programs such as global studies, history, political science or religious studies, or with a professional degree, such as in business, journalism or law.

The Bachelor of Science in astronomy provides a strong background in the fundamentals of astronomy and astrophysics to prepare students for graduate study. This program provides a complete introduction to the concepts and methods of modern astronomy and astrophysics. Students complete a sequence of courses in physics and mathematics to achieve a robust understanding of the physical principles underlying astronomy and astrophysics. Students also complete courses in astronomy, astrophysics and cosmology, and they learn observational techniques using the university's telescopes. The School of Earth and Space Exploration's location in the desert Southwest provides an excellent environment for astronomical observations. The school has a number of telescopes on campus that are used for both teaching and research. The school is also involved in many space missions, including the Hubble Space Telescope, the James Webb Space Telescope, the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter and the Psyche mission. This involvement provides many opportunities for undergraduate students to get involved in research.

Astrophysics is the discipline of physics that studies the universe. It applies the laws of physics to understand the birth, life and death of stars, planets, galaxies, nebulae and other objects in the universe. The Bachelor of Science in astrophysics provides a strong foundation in physics and mathematics, in-depth coursework in astrophysics and hands-on research experience. Astrophysics majors have opportunities to participate in research with faculty in cosmology, extragalactic astronomy, galactic astronomy, stellar astrophysics, astrobiology, planetary science, and instrumentation. Faculty also actively participate in research programs with NASA and the National Science Foundation, such as the Hubble Space Telescope, the James Webb Space Telescope, the Spitzer Space Telescope, the Chandra X-ray Observatory, the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, the Mars Science Laboratory, the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter and the Psyche mission. Students learn from faculty experts in the School of Earth and Space Exploration, one of the leading research centers in the country for earth and space sciences, and have access to unique state-of-the-art facilities and instruments.

The BS program in biochemistry with a concentration in medicinal chemistry gives students a strong background in biology and chemistry and prepares them for a career in the pharmaceutical and biotechnology industries or for entry into professional schools for medicine, dentistry or pharmacy.

The medicinal chemistry concentration provides a strong background in chemistry, with a particular emphasis on the theory and practice of organic chemistry, and includes sufficient biological sciences course work to provide the context for medicinal applications. This major is less quantitative than the BS in chemistry with a concentration in medicinal chemistry, as it does not require calculus-based physics.

This program is available for students enrolled at ASU's Tempe campus.

The School of Molecular Sciences has received an above-average ranking for its graduate programs in chemistry and biochemistry from the National Research Council. The school's award-winning faculty is recognized internationally, with a majority having received the highest honors in their fields.
Accreditation status: This program in biochemistry is accredited by the American Society for Biochemistry and Molecular Biology.

description:
The Bachelor of Arts degree program in biochemistry provides a strong foundation in chemistry and biology and an introduction to biochemistry. It is an appropriate course of study for students who wish to pursue careers in the health professions, such as medicine, dentistry or pharmacy; in biotechnology; in related fields in education, law and business; and for students who plan to pursue advanced degrees in these areas. The program does not offer the depth of training required for a career as a professional biochemist. For that, students are advised to enroll in the Bachelor of Science program in biochemistry.

This major is eligible for the Western Undergraduate Exchange program at a reduced tuition rate. For more information on WUE, see https://www.asu.edu/wue.

Biochemists explore the chemical structure of living things. They seek to understand the molecular basis for processes such as development, disease, evolution and heredity. An understanding of biochemistry is essential for the development of new treatments for disease, the creation of new biotechnologies and a deeper understanding of the natural world.

The BS in biochemistry provides students with a strong background in chemistry, with an emphasis on the chemistry of biological systems. Coursework is rigorous in chemistry, biology and mathematics and provides a great foundation for further study in the medical sciences.

Students can enter the workforce with this degree or they can continue to graduate school or professional programs.

The Bachelor of Science in biodiversity and conservation prepares students for careers in which they can understand, protect and sustain the diversity of life on Earth. The degree provides an interdisciplinary approach to the science of biodiversity and the practice of conservation. Students in this program benefit from the strengths of two ASU units: the School of Life Sciences in The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences and the College of Integrative Sciences and Arts' School of Applied Sciences and Arts. Students on the Tempe campus enroll in The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences and are taught by faculty from the School of Life Sciences. Students at the Polytechnic campus enroll in the College of Integrative Sciences and Arts and are taught by faculty from the School of Applied Sciences and Arts. The curriculum requires a combination of classroom, laboratory and field experiences. Students are also encouraged to develop an independent research project and to obtain real-world experience through an internship. This program provides students with a solid foundation in the principles of ecology, evolution, genetics and organismal biology, which are central to understanding biodiversity and its conservation. Students learn about the patterns of biological diversity, the processes that create and maintain it, and the strategies and policies that can be employed to conserve it. Students gain skills in data analysis, scientific communication and critical thinking. They are well-prepared for a variety of careers in government agencies, nongovernmental organizations and the private sector as well as for graduate studies in conservation biology, environmental science, and related fields. ASU's location in the Sonoran Desert provides a unique opportunity for students to study biodiversity and conservation in a region with high levels of endemism and a long history of human-environment interactions. The university's strong ties to local, national and international conservation organizations also provide students with a wealth of opportunities for hands-on learning and professional development.

Concentration name: ['Biomedical Devices', 'Imaging and Sensing', 'Molecular, Cellular and Tissue Engineering']
description:
The bachelor's degree program in bioengineering, also known as biomedical engineering, is based on a solid foundation in mathematics, physics, chemistry and the engineering sciences. The curriculum provides a broad education in the fundamentals of bioengineering while allowing students to select a particular area of emphasis through the choice of track electives.

The required courses cover key areas of biomedical engineering, including:

biomechanics (the study of the mechanical properties of biological systems)
biomaterials (the study of materials used in biomedical applications)
biosignals and systems (the study of biological signals and the systems that process them)
biotransport (the study of the transport of molecules in biological systems)
instrumentation (the design of devices for diagnosis, treatment and exploration of physiological systems)
Students learn to apply engineering principles to understand, modify or control biological systems; design and develop devices to monitor and measure physiological parameters; and develop new therapeutic procedures, such as the design and development of artificial organs and other implants. Students also become familiar with the ethical issues that biomedical engineers face.

The biomedical engineering curriculum provides excellent preparation for graduate study in biomedical engineering, medicine or other health-related disciplines. Graduates are also well prepared for employment in industries focused on medicine and health care, including pharmaceutical development, medical device manufacturing, health care delivery and biotechnology.
Accreditation status: The bioengineering BSE program at the Tempe campus is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

description:
The BS program in bioinformatics combines foundational knowledge in life sciences with computational skills and data science methods. The curriculum provides an excellent background for students who are interested in research careers in academia or industry, or in professional careers in health care or biotechnology.

The study of bioinformatics applies computer technology to the management and analysis of biological data. The result is that vast and complex data sets can be deciphered and used for discovering new knowledge in medicine and biology. Rapid advances in science and technology mean there is a high demand for professionals who are trained in this interdisciplinary field.

Students learn to:
* access and use major public domain biological and biomedical databases for research and development
* formulate and test biological and biomedical hypotheses by analyzing large-scale datasets, including those from genomics, proteomics and transcriptomics
* retrieve, analyze and synthesize complex information from a variety of sources as part of a research or development project
* use basic programming and scripting tools to automate data processing and analytical tasks
* use state-of-the-art computational and data science software to analyze and interpret data

The BS program in biological sciences with a concentration in biology and society is focused on the life sciences and their interaction with society. The concentration in biology and society offers students an opportunity to join faculty in a cross-disciplinary exploration of the role of biology in society and of the social, political and ethical issues that these studies of biology raise. Graduates of the program are well prepared for careers in a wide range of fields, including health care and health policy, biological research and education, conservation and environmental policy, law and science journalism.

The BS program in biological sciences with a concentration in biomedical sciences is designed for students interested in careers in medicine and other health-related professions. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in biological principles and processes, ranging from the molecular and cellular levels to the organismal and population levels. The concentration in biomedical sciences also incorporates a solid foundation in chemistry, physics and mathematics.

Students gain skills in scientific methodology, critical thinking, written and oral communication, collaboration, and quantitative and data analysis.

This concentration fulfills all requirements for application to medical, dental and other health professional schools.

The diverse research interests of the faculty in the School of Life Sciences offer a wide selection of research opportunities for undergraduate students, and faculty members actively encourage student participation in research.

The BS program in biological sciences with a concentration in conservation biology and ecology is an opportunity for students to learn about the diversity of life on Earth and the science of conserving it for generations to come. Students explore the principles of ecology, evolution, genetics and physiology to learn how to apply them to solving conservation problems.

Students learn the basic components of biological diversity, from genes to species to ecosystems, and about the patterns and processes of life on Earth. Through an exploration of the causes and consequences of biodiversity loss, students learn techniques for restoring and managing populations, communities and ecosystems and for managing human activities to promote biodiversity conservation and sustainability.

The program emphasizes hands-on learning through laboratory courses and field experiences. Students can work directly with faculty on research projects in the field or in the lab.
Program name: Biological Sciences (Conservation Biology and Ecology), BS

description:
The BS program in biological sciences with a concentration in genetics, cell and developmental biology is focused on the study of the molecular basis of life. This concentration provides a strong foundation in genetics, cell biology, developmental biology and molecular biology. Students learn the structure and function of cells, the genetic and molecular processes that control the growth and development of organisms, and the molecular basis of human disease.

Students in this concentration learn valuable research skills through innovative, inquiry-based laboratory courses.

Graduates are well prepared for careers in the biotechnology and health care industries, academic research and for entry into graduate schools and a variety of professional schools, including medical, dental, optometry and pharmacy school.
Program name: Biological Sciences (Genetics, Cell and Developmental Biology), BS

description: The BS program in biological sciences with a concentration in neurobiology, physiology and behavior is an interdisciplinary program that leads to a deep understanding of the structure and function of the nervous system, from molecules to the complex behaviors of organisms. The program is specifically designed to meet the growing need for neuroscientists in the clinical, academic and industrial workforce. The study of neuroscience includes many fields, from molecular biology to psychology, and represents a unique combination of traditional disciplines. This program offers extensive and exceptional research opportunities that train students in the conduct and communication of scientific research. Graduates of the program are well prepared for medical school and graduate school as well as for careers in biomedical research, for positions in the biotechnology and pharmaceutical industries and in science-related fields such as science writing, policy and patent law.
Program name: Biological Sciences (Neurobiology, Physiology and Behavior), BS

description:
The BS program in biological sciences provides a comprehensive background in biology. The curriculum offers an extensive selection of courses in all areas of biology, allowing students to tailor their education to their specific interests.

From molecules to ecosystems, biology is a broad and diverse science. The biological sciences program provides students with skills essential for a variety of careers. The curriculum provides a strong foundation for further study in graduate or professional school.

Students participate in hands-on learning in laboratory and field courses. They are encouraged to become involved in research with faculty in the School of Life Sciences. These research experiences can be life-changing for students, who often go on to publish their work in peer-reviewed journals. Students gain research skills, critical thinking skills and technical experience that improve their marketability for jobs and make them competitive applicants for graduate school and professional programs.

The School of Life Sciences also hosts a number of study abroad opportunities, including programs in Australia, the Galapagos Islands and Ecuador, and Panama.

Many students who graduate with a BS in biological sciences are prepared to enter medical school, dental school, veterinary medicine programs and other allied health programs.

Students in this program may also be interested in the 4+1 accelerated BS/MS program in biology, which allows them to earn a bachelor's and a master's degree in just five years.

Concentration name: Biological Devices, Biological Signals and Systems, Biomaterials and Tissue Engineering, Biomechanics
description:
The Bachelor of Science in Engineering program in biomedical engineering is an interdisciplinary program that integrates engineering and the life sciences. Students receive rigorous training in engineering fundamentals (e.g., mathematics, physics, chemistry and engineering) while becoming well-versed in the life sciences (e.g., biology, biochemistry, physiology) so that they can apply engineering principles to solve problems in medicine and biology.

Graduates of the biomedical engineering program have a broad knowledge of traditional engineering disciplines, allowing them to work and communicate effectively with engineers in all fields. Additionally, they have a strong understanding of the chemical, electrical and mechanical properties of biological systems.

Biomedical engineers apply their expertise in many ways, including:

* designing instruments, devices and software to diagnose and treat medical problems
* developing new procedures using knowledge from many technical sources
* creating artificial organs
* making biomaterials
* developing pharmaceuticals
Accreditation status: The biomedical engineering, BSE program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Bioengineering and Biomedical and Similarly Named Engineering Programs Program Criteria.

description:
The BS program in biomedical informatics focuses on the development of methods to better use data, information and knowledge in all areas of the biomedical sciences.

Students in the program learn to apply and create computational tools to manage and analyze biomedical data. They learn about the latest trends in the field and have opportunities to conduct cutting-edge research with renowned faculty in ASU's Department of Biomedical Informatics. Students gain skills in data mining, software engineering, systems biology, machine learning, clinical informatics, public health informatics and imaging informatics.

The degree program is unique as it's offered through the College of Health Solutions. This allows students to receive hands-on experience and training with faculty at the forefront of biomedical informatics research, a factor that sets this program apart from other undergraduate bioinformatics or computational biology degrees. Students are also afforded the opportunity to interact directly with clinicians and researchers from the program's many partner institutions, such as the Mayo Clinic, Banner Health, the Translational Genomics Research Institute, the Phoenix Children's Hospital and the Barrow Neurological Institute. These opportunities enhance and enrich their academic experience as well as provide an excellent base for future career opportunities in all areas of the biomedical sciences.

The BS program in biophysics provides an interdisciplinary education in physics, biology and chemistry, preparing students for careers in biotechnology and medicine as well as for graduate studies in biophysics, medical physics, physics, biology and medicine.

Biophysics lies at the intersection of the physical and life sciences. The methods of physics, and the related sciences of chemistry, mathematics and computer science, are used to study biological systems at the molecular, cellular and systems levels.

Graduates are equipped with the critical thinking skills of a physicist and a fundamental knowledge of biology at the molecular and cellular levels. With this training, graduates are able to identify and solve complex problems across a broad range of biological systems using an interdisciplinary approach that applies quantitative reasoning to biological problems.

Concentration name: Biomanufacturing and Bioprocessing, Molecular Biotechnology for Health
description:
Biotechnology is a field of applied biology that involves the use of living organisms and bioprocesses to create or modify products for a specific use. For thousands of years, humankind has used biotechnology in agriculture, food production and medicine. Today, modern biotechnology is a cutting-edge field with a wide range of applications, including the development of disease-resistant crops, new biofuels and life-saving treatments for human diseases.

The Bachelor of Science program in biotechnology prepares students for careers at the forefront of this dynamic field.

The curriculum provides a strong foundation in the basic sciences, an understanding of the underlying life sciences and an in-depth knowledge of a variety of biotechnologies and their real-world applications. Students gain hands-on training using state-of-the-art laboratory instrumentation, and they conduct research side-by-side with world-class faculty.

To better prepare students for the full range of career opportunities in biotechnology, the program offers two concentrations that allow students to align their degree with their specific interests:

The concentration in biomanufacturing and bioprocessing focuses on the production of biological products, from biofuels to therapeutics.

The concentration in molecular biotechnology for health focuses on the applications of biotechnology for improving human health, including diagnostics, therapeutics and forensics.

The BA program in business with a concentration in accountancy is a non-professional degree program offered by the W. P. Carey School of Business. It does not contain enough accounting credits for CPA licensure and is designed for students who are interested in careers in the business world but are not seeking to become professional accountants. Students who want to pursue a career in accounting should apply to the BS program in accountancy.

Students develop a strong foundation in business anas well as leadership, critical thinking and communication skills. Coursework in the concentration provides a general introduction to the theories and practices of financial and managerial accounting, taxation and auditing.
Accreditation status: The W. P. Carey School of Business is accredited by AACSB International, the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.

description: The BA program in business with a concentration in business administration provides a broad and general business education designed to prepare students for a wide variety of careers on the business side of any industry. The program provides students a solid grounding in business knowledge with courses in accounting, economics, finance, information systems, management, marketing and supply chain management. The business administration curriculum is designed for students who want a broad background in business with the flexibility to work in a variety of industries and functions. Business administration students receive a rich educational experience that allows them to interact with peers from a variety of backgrounds and experiences. Students learn how all business functions work together and become well-rounded and well-educated managers. Graduates of this program are skilled at leading teams, thinking critically and strategically, and effectively managing resources to meet organizational goals in both domestic and global contexts.
Accreditation status: The W. P. Carey School of Business at Arizona State University is accredited by AACSB International, the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business. All of our business and accounting degree programs are included in this accreditation.

description:
The Bachelor of Arts in business with a concentration in communication is an innovative, interdisciplinary program offered by the highly ranked W. P. Carey School of Business and The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences' Hugh Downs School of Human Communication. The program, with classes offered at ASU's Tempe campus, provides students with a strong foundation in business and an extensive understanding of the role of communication in the business environment.

Communication is essential for success in business. Students in this program will study a variety of communication topics, including persuasion and social influence, intercultural communication and public speaking, in conjunction with business courses in accounting, economics, finance, management, marketing and supply chain management. The business communication program gives students the skills and knowledge necessary to develop effective communication strategies for a variety of business-related situations and contexts.
Accreditation status: The W. P. Carey School is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.

description:
The Bachelor of Arts in business with a concentration in computer information systems provides students with a strong foundation in information technology and business. The curriculum is designed to provide students with broad knowledge of business, together with the specific tools needed to design and develop modern information systems. The program helps prepare students for roles such as a systems analyst, business applications developer, and information technology consultant. 

The program teaches students the principles of business information systems, systems analysis and design, database management, and business analytics. Computer information systems professionals are in demand by businesses of all sizes in all sectors of the economy. 

Students who enjoy technology and want a career that allows them to solve problems will find this program a good fit. This program allows students to combine their interest in business with a solid technical foundation that provides them with the background to analyze, design and manage information systems.
Accreditation status: All programs in the W. P. Carey School of Business are accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB International).

description:
The Bachelor of Arts in business with a concentration in corporate accounting provides knowledge of the functional areas of business with an emphasis on the accounting concepts and practices used in corporations.

The curriculum is designed to help prepare students for a successful career in a corporate setting in accounting. This program does not meet the requirements for students to sit for the CPA exam in Arizona.
Accreditation status: The W. P. Carey School of Business is accredited by AACSB International, the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business. AACSB International is the world's largest and longest-serving accrediting body for business schools, and its accreditation is the hallmark of excellence in business education.

description:
The Bachelor of Arts in business with a concentration in data analytics prepares students with the skills needed to succeed in a world where data is the most valuable asset. The ability to extract, interpret and communicate meaningful information from large, complex data sets is one of the most in-demand skills in the modern business world.

This program combines a strong business core curriculum with the advanced data analytics coursework required for success in the rapidly expanding data science and analytics fields. Students learn cutting-edge data mining and modeling techniques using industry-standard software and programming languages such as Python, R and SQL. Graduates are prepared for careers in fields such as business and market intelligence, financial and risk analysis, and operations and supply chain management.

This program is offered by the W. P. Carey School of Business, which is one of the top-ranked business schools in the country. W. P. Carey School of Business is a community of scholars, researchers and expert faculty focused on transforming the future of business. With smaller class sizes and a supportive learning environment, students get the individual attention they need to thrive.
Accreditation status: All undergraduate programs offered by the W. P. Carey School of Business are accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB International).

description:
The Bachelor of Arts in business with a concentration in financial planning helps students develop the qualitative and quantitative skills necessary to provide professional financial planning services to individuals and families.

The curriculum addresses the major areas of financial planning:
- employee benefits
- estate planning
- income tax planning
- insurance
- investments
- retirement planning

The W. P. Carey School of Business financial planning program is registered with the Certified Financial Planner Board of Standards. Graduates of the program are eligible to take the CFP® certification examination, one of the premier certifications in the financial planning profession. The program is designed so that students will have satisfied the educational coursework requirements to sit for the CFP exam upon graduation.
Accreditation status: The W. P. Carey School of Business financial planning program is registered with the Certified Financial Planner Board of Standards.

description:
The BA program in business with a concentration in food industry management is designed to develop business leaders for the nation's food industry.

Agribusiness is the study of the business of agricultural production. It includes the manufacturing and distribution of farm supplies; production and processing on farms and ranches; and the storage, processing and distribution of farm commodities and items made from them.

Food industry management is a specialized area of agribusiness that deals with the management of the food supply chain, from producer to consumer.

The program integrates the study of food systems with a solid foundation in business management. The curriculum covers a wide variety of topics, including agricultural finance, economics, food advertising and promotion, and food supply networks, and it provides an understanding of how food companies and farms operate.

Graduates are prepared for a variety of careers in the food industry, including food distribution, food marketing and food processing.
Accreditation status: The W. P. Carey School of Business is accredited by AACSB International, the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business. This is the oldest and most prestigious international accrediting agency for business and accounting degree programs.

description:
The BA program in business with a concentration in global agribusiness prepares students for management careers in the food and agriculture sector. The agribusiness industry is a large and complex global system, with opportunities for students in all business disciplines.

ASU's global agribusiness program is one of very few undergraduate agribusiness programs in the nation that is housed in a business school. The W. P. Carey School of Business provides a solid business core curriculum for students to be successful in this diverse industry.

Students learn about the entire agribusiness value chain, from the farm to the consumer's plate, while mastering business concepts and principles in accounting, finance, marketing and management, as well as supply chain management. Experiential learning in the form of internships, research and consulting projects is an important component of the program.

Students gain an understanding of the challenges and opportunities of the rapidly changing global food system. They acquire knowledge of business disciplines applied to agribusiness and develop an appreciation of the social, cultural and economic diversity of the global food business.
Accreditation status: The undergraduate and graduate programs and the School of Accountancy are all accredited by AACSB International.

description:
The BA program in business with a concentration in global leadership provides students with a broad business background applicable to for-profit, nonprofit and public sector organizations. Students learn from a curriculum with an emphasis on global business, and they choose a required area of study in a specific international region. The program requires intermediate-level proficiency in a non-English language.

In this program, students develop an understanding of the complexities of the global economy as well as global and regional business practices. In-depth study in a specific region of the world helps students develop an understanding of a specific area and business practices for that area.

Students acquire knowledge and skills for effective intercultural communication, including language skills, which are essential for success in the business world's multicultural context.
Accreditation status: The W. P. Carey School of Business is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB International).

description: The BA program in business with a concentration in global logistics management prepares students for a career in logistics and supply chain management. This program is a transdisciplinary program that leverages the expertise of faculty in the W. P. Carey School of Business and the College of Global Futures. The curriculum offers an integrated perspective on global logistics, with courses in sustainability, business and global supply chains. Topics of study include: accounting, computer information systems, economics, finance, management, marketing, sustainability. In their final year of study, students have the opportunity to participate in a senior project that allows them to apply their knowledge and skills in logistics and supply chain management to a real-world project with a local company.
Accreditation status: The W. P. Carey School of Business is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB International).

description:
The Bachelor of Arts in business with a concentration in global politics offers students foundational business knowledge and skills as well as a specific focus on global politics. This program is a collaboration between the W. P. Carey School of Business and the Thunderbird School of Global Management.
Students develop an understanding of the global political landscape and a strong skill set in business functional areas. They also gain a general understanding of business concepts and practices and a deeper understanding of the global political context in which businesses operate. The curriculum includes courses in accounting, economics, finance, management, marketing and supply chain management as well as courses in international relations, global political economy and international security.
Graduates with this business degree are prepared for positions in a variety of industries, including consulting, finance and international business, as well as in government and nonprofit organizations. This program is an excellent choice for those interested in careers that require a deep understanding of both business and global affairs.
The curriculum is rigorous, and the program is highly competitive. Students who are successful in this program are typically well-rounded, with strong analytical and communication skills. They also are often globally minded and have a passion for learning about other cultures.
Accreditation status: The business degrees offered by the W. P. Carey School of Business are accredited by AACSB International, the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.

description:
The business (human resources) program combines a broad-based business curriculum with a specialization in the human resource function. Students learn about business fundamentals, and in their concentration courses, they study topics such as:

compensation and benefits
employee and labor relations
employment law
performance management
staffing
training and development
This program provides students with the critical skills and knowledge they need to pursue a career in human resource management in business, government and nonprofit organizations. Human resource specialists are vital to an organization's success and are in high demand across a range of industries. Graduates often go on to careers as human resources managers, labor relations specialists and compensation managers.
Accreditation status: The W. P. Carey School of Business is accredited by AACSB International, the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business. The W. P. Carey School of Business is one of the top-ranked business schools in the country, with undergraduate and graduate programs, as well as a wide variety of nondegree programs, for students and executives.

description: The Bachelor of Arts program in business with a concentration in law provides a strong business foundation in accounting, economics, finance, management, marketing and supply chain management. This liberal arts degree also emphasizes the interrelationships between law, business and society and allows for significant flexibility to explore nonbusiness coursework. The law concentration provides prelaw students with a significant competitive advantage when applying to law school and other graduate programs. This program is offered by the W. P. Carey School of Business, which has a worldwide reputation for excellence and is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.
Accreditation status: W. P. Carey School of Business ... is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.

description:
The BA program in business with a concentration in marketing teaches students the skills and knowledge they need to be successful in the fast-paced world of marketing. The curriculum covers a wide range of topics, including:
- consumer behavior
- marketing research
- product management
- promotion
Students also have the opportunity to gain hands-on experience through internships and other experiential learning opportunities.
The W. P. Carey School ofBusiness marketing program is consistently ranked among the top in the nation. It provides students with a solid foundation in the principles of marketing and prepares them for a variety of careers in the field. Graduates are prepared for marketing-related careers in a variety of industries, including advertising, brand management, market research and sales.
Accreditation status: All W. P. Carey School of Business programs are accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB International).

description:
The Bachelor of Arts program in business with a concentration in public service and public policy provides students with a broad business background and a strong foundation in public administration and policy. The program introduces students to the challenges and opportunities of working in or with federal, state and local government. The program prepares students for careers in which business and government intersect, in areas such as public finance, urban economics, real estate and regulation. Students are well-prepared for law school and graduate programs in business, public administration and public policy.

The public service and public policy concentration combines the development of general business knowledge with a specific focus on the public sector. The program provides a strong curriculum that develops the skills valued by employers in both the private and public sectors. The curriculum is designed to help students understand how organizations in different sectors --- public, private and nonprofit --- can work together to address some of the most challenging issues in society.

This is a transdisciplinary program that requires coursework from the School of Public Affairs and the W. P. Carey School of Business. It provides the skills and knowledge to analyze social, economic and political issues, to develop creative, evidence-based solutions, and to lead with integrity, all in preparation for careers aimed at producing graduates who create public value.
Accreditation status: The W. P. Carey School of Business is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB).
Program name: Business (Public Service and Public Policy), BA

description:
The Bachelor of Arts in business with a concentration in retail management provides a solid business core, which includes accounting, economics, finance, management, marketing and statistics. The concentration courses offer students in-depth knowledge of retailing principles and practices, including buying and planning, leadership, retail strategy and operations.

Students who enjoy working with people in an exciting and constantly changing environment may enjoy a career in retailing. Opportunities for advancement are greater in this field than in most others and can include management positions with department stores, specialty stores and mass merchandisers or buying and planning positions with company corporate offices.

Students pursuing this program are required to complete a concurrent degree in a nonbusiness field. Examples include but are not limited to:

*   communication
*   fashion
*   film
*   food and nutrition
*   graphic information technology
*   interior design
*   journalism and mass communication
*   tourism

For more information, students should visit the W. P. Carey School of Business website.
Accreditation status: W. P. Carey School of Business is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB International).

description:
The Bachelor of Arts in business with a concentration in Spanish language and culture provides a strong foundation in business and liberal arts and a functional knowledge of Spanish language and culture, allowing students to integrate their language skills and cultural knowledge with an understanding of global business practices. The program is specifically designed to provide students with the business and cross-cultural skills to successfully engage with a Spanish-speaking global audience.
The language classes in this program focus on the functional use of Spanish for the business professional. The classes combine face-to-face instruction, cutting-edge language learning technology and professional development opportunities. In addition, the program encourages students to complete an internship or to study abroad in a Spanish-speaking country.
Students learn the fundamentals of business, including accounting, economics, finance, management, marketing and supply chain management. In addition to the functional knowledge, students learn about international business and the global business environment.
Students may be able to accelerate their degree program.
Accreditation status: All programs in the W. P. Carey School of Business are accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB International).

description:
The bachelor's degree program in business with a concentration in sport and media studies provides students with a broad background in business while preparing them for a career in the dynamic sport industry.

Students take a common business core that provides a strong foundation in business fundamentals. The curriculum offers a variety of courses in sport, including sport law, sport marketing, and sport and society, and it also covers current topics such as sport analytics, name, image and likeness, college athletics, professional sports, and media relations.

Students gain practical experience through an internship program and develop their skills through projects with local and national sport organizations. Students are supported and encouraged to secure meaningful industry experience while in the program.

The W. P. Carey School of Business has a dedicated sport business career specialist who assists students with resume building, internship searches and career opportunities. ASU's sport business programs are closely aligned with Sun Devil Athletics, a NCAA Division I program that includes 26 varsity-level sports.
Accreditation status: The W. P. Carey School of Business is one of the top-ranked business schools in the country. Our undergraduate, graduate and doctoral programs are all highly regarded and are accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.

description:
The Bachelor of Arts in business with a concentration in sports business, offered by the W. P. Carey School of Business, provides students with a solid foundation in business and an understanding of the context of the sports industry. Students have opportunities to focus on aspects of sports business that are of particular interest to them. In addition to general studies requirements and a solid foundation of business knowledge, the curriculum includes sports-specific coursework that provides an overview of the business of sports and gives students the chance to investigate specific areas of interest by selecting from a variety of electives.

The sports business concentration offers an innovative curriculum and a variety of internship opportunities. Students benefit from the school's extensive network of relationships with sports-related organizations at all levels (professional, collegiate and amateur) and in all sectors (public and private).

Career opportunities in the sports industry include positions in collegiate athletics, corporate sponsorship, event management, facility management, marketing and promotions, media and communication, and professional sports. The curriculum and opportunities provided in the program prepare students to be competitive candidates for a variety of roles in the highly competitive sports industry.
Accreditation status: AACSB International

description:
The Bachelor of Arts in business with a concentration in sustainability is an innovative, transdisciplinary program that gives students a strong foundation in business functional areas and expertise in sustainability.

The W. P. Carey School of Business and the School of Sustainability have partnered to offer this program. It integrates business with a global perspective and an understanding of social and environmental responsibility, while also providing a solid background in the liberal arts.

The curriculum includes core courses from both disciplines and culminates in a senior-year capstone course. Students develop critical thinking skills necessary for a world in which business success is inextricably linked to sustainable practices. They are prepared to become the next generation of business leaders who will create and capture new opportunities by solving some of the world's most pressing challenges.
Accreditation status: The W. P. Carey School of Business is one of the top business schools in the country. The school is internationally recognized for its leadership in business education and is highly regarded for its groundbreaking research and student outcomes. Its business and accountancy programs are accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.

description:
The business BA program with a concentration in technology is offered by the W. P. Carey School of Business. This program combines a solid business foundation with specialized coursework in technology, preparing students to be leaders in the fast-paced, dynamic world of business and technology.

In a business world increasingly driven by data and technology, this business degree, with a concentration in technology, provides the skills and knowledge to keep organizations on the leading edge.

The curriculum blends key aspects of technology, including computer information systems and supply chain management, with a strong foundation in every functional area of business. The program also delivers a first-rate general education curriculum, including courses in mathematics, English, humanities and social sciences.

Graduates are prepared to use data and technology to solve business problems and to manage processes, people and projects in a technology-driven workplace.
Accreditation status: The W. P. Carey School of Business is one of the top business schools in the country. The undergraduate and graduate business programs are accredited by AACSB International, the highest recognition for a business school in the world.

description:
The business (tourism) BA program, offered by the W. P. Carey School of Business, provides students with a business-oriented approach to the tourism industry. The curriculum prepares students for positions in destination management and marketing, tourism planning and development, resort and hotel operations, and tourism research.

The program addresses the economic, social and environmental aspects of tourism, one of the world's largest industries. It examines topics such as destination development, sustainable tourism, special event and festival planning and management, destination marketing and sales, and international tourism.

A combination of classroom instruction, field trips and domestic and international travel study opportunities provide students a thorough understanding of the challenges and opportunities of the tourism industry.

The program requires 45 hours of business core courses, 21 hours of tourism development and management courses, 15 hours of business electives, 35 hours of general studies and four hours of electives.
Accreditation status: The W. P. Carey School of Business is one of the top business schools in the country, and is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB International).

description: The BA program in business administration provides students with a broad and general background in business. It has a strong international orientation and is designed to develop business acumen, financial literacy, and an entrepreneurial mindset in students. Students gain a solid foundation of business knowledge in accounting, economics, finance, information systems, management, marketing and supply chain management. This well-rounded education also covers business communication, law and ethics, international business, and small business and entrepreneurship. The curriculum provides the foundation necessary for careers in a wide array of business fields, including: financial analysis, human resource management, international trade, marketing, new venture development, public relations and research.
Accreditation status: The undergraduate and graduate business programs are accredited by AACSB International.

description:
Chemical engineering is a broad and versatile discipline that combines the principles of chemistry, mathematics, physics and biology with engineering to solve a wide range of problems. Chemical engineers are involved in the research, design, development and operation of processes for the production of a wide range of products, including commodity and specialty chemicals, pharmaceuticals, semiconductors, alternative fuels and biomaterials.

The ASU bachelor's degree program in chemical engineering provides students with a high-quality, contemporary and comprehensive education. The curriculum includes a fundamental core of mathematics, chemistry, physics and biology, a range of core chemical engineering courses that provide the basic tools of the discipline and a selection of technical electives that allow students to explore specialized areas of chemical engineering.
