Students may choose from a wide range of specialized areas, such as energy and sustainability, biomolecular engineering, semiconductor materials processing, advanced materials and process engineering.

Students develop strong analytical and problem-solving skills and a solid foundation in the principles of chemical engineering, which prepares them for a successful career in a variety of industries or for graduate study.
Accreditation status: The chemical engineering, BSE program at the Tempe campus is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

description:
The Bachelor of Arts in chemistry provides a strong background in chemistry while allowing for more curriculum flexibility than is possible with the Bachelor of Science degree. The program provides the necessary foundation for students who wish to pursue careers in a variety of fields, including:
agribusiness
environmental law
patent law
public policy and service
secondary school science teaching
technical sales and management
writing in science, business or law
The program may also serve as a preprofessional curriculum for students interested in dentistry, medicine and other health professions. This degree is not recommended for those who plan to pursue graduate studies in chemistry.

The BS program in chemistry is an American Chemical Society-certified degree program that prepares students for careers as professional chemists and serves as a foundation for careers in other fields, such as environmental science and medicine. The program provides a strong grounding in the traditional subdisciplines of chemistry (analytical, biochemistry, inorganic, organic and physical), as well as foundational training in physics and mathematics. Graduates are well prepared to succeed in graduate programs, in chemistry-related industries and professional schools.

With more than 30 award-winning faculty members, the School of Molecular Sciences has expertise in the full range of chemistry subdisciplines, with particular strengths in areas of critical importance to the state and the nation, including energy, medicine and sustainability.

Undergraduate students have many opportunities to conduct faculty-mentored research in areas such as: artificial photosynthesis, atmospheric and environmental chemistry, catalysis, drug discovery and design, energy conversion and storage, fundamental theory, materials chemistry, nanoscience, protein structure and function, solid-state chemistry.
Accreditation status: American Chemical Society

description:
The BA program in Chicana and Chicano studies offers an interdisciplinary curriculum that provides students with a broad understanding of the history, culture and contemporary social conditions of Chicanos and other Latinos in the U.S. and in a global context. The program also highlights the history, culture and contemporary social conditions of Indigenous peoples of the Americas.

Students learn to use a variety of theories and methods to analyze such phenomena as:

- community empowerment
- ethnic identity and relations
- family and gender roles
- folklore and popular culture
- language issues
- literature and arts
- political and socioeconomic status
- transnationalism

The Bachelor of Science in child development is a multidisciplinary program from the T. Denny Sanford School of Social and Family Dynamics. Students focus on children's development from conception through early adolescence.

The curriculum includes courses focused on developmental theory as well as practical, real-world application of material, so that students understand how to help children grow and learn to the best of their abilities.

Students gain insight into how children develop within the contexts of family, culture, school and neighborhood, and they are trained to improve the lives of children and families.

All students complete a senior year capstone internship. The capstone provides students with hands-on experience working with children and families in the community. Many students choose to participate in an optional study abroad experience.

The BA program in Chinese provides students with a command of the Chinese language and an understanding of the literature and culture of China. Coursework in the major is conducted in Mandarin Chinese and English.

The study of Chinese complements a number of other disciplines, such as art history, global studies, history, political science, religious studies and sustainability. Graduates find employment in business, government, law, the military, translation and other areas. Many graduates continue their education in graduate school, law school or other professional schools.

Students who successfully complete the requirements for the BA degree in Chinese are able to:
- communicate in spoken and written Chinese at a level of proficiency equivalent to the advanced-low level on the ACTFL scale
- understand, analyze and critique a variety of texts from different historical periods and cultural settings in China
- demonstrate an in-depth understanding of selected aspects of Chinese culture

Civil engineering is the professional engineering discipline that deals with the design, construction and maintenance of the physical and naturally built environment, including works such as bridges, roads, canals, dams and buildings. Civil engineering is the oldest engineering discipline after military engineering and it was defined to distinguish nonmilitary engineering from military engineering.

The bachelor's degree program in civil engineering offers a concentration in environmental engineering that prepares students for careers in the environmental engineering field. Students learn to apply the principles of engineering, soil science, biology and chemistry to develop solutions to environmental problems.

Students in the civil engineering BSE program may select the 4+1 program and obtain both a BSE and a master's degree in civil, environmental and sustainable engineering in five years.

This program is a good choice for students interested in making an impact on the quality of life in a society and who want to be involved in public works and infrastructure that are all around us. The program provides an excellent background for those wishing to pursue careers in consulting engineering, construction and public works as well as for those interested in advanced studies, including those seeking to pursue other professional degrees, including law, medicine and business administration.

This program provides a broad-based background in all areas of civil engineering with an emphasis in environmental engineering and prepares graduates for entry into the civil engineering profession. Graduates are prepared to take the Fundamentals of Engineering examination, the first step to becoming a registered professional engineer. In their final year of study, students have the opportunity to participate in a capstone project that provides a culminating major design experience and provides the foundation for professional engineering licensure.
Accreditation status: The BSE program in civil engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

description:
The Bachelor of Science in Engineering program in civil engineering gives students a broad-based background and the professional skills they need for a career in areas such as:

structural engineering
sustainable engineering
transportation engineering
The civil engineering curriculum includes required coursework in mathematics, chemistry, physics and engineering sciences. The courses in civil engineering build upon this foundation and develop the student's understanding of engineering principles. Students learn to apply these principles to the design of civil engineering systems through a series of design courses, which culminate in a capstone design experience. This major includes a concentration in sustainable engineering.

The BSE program in civil engineering has a common freshman year with other BSE programs in the School of Sustainable Engineering and the Built Environment. Students in these programs may change their major to any of the other BSE programs in the school at any time during the first year. The sophomore year has a common engineering core with a course sequence in civil engineering topics.

Students who choose the sustainable engineering concentration take courses focused on the principles of sustainability and the application of those principles in engineering design. Students in this concentration learn about environmental regulations and law, green building design, and life cycle assessment in the context of civil engineering.
Accreditation status: The civil engineering, BSE program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

Concentration name: Construction Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Geotechnical Engineering, Structural Engineering, Sustainability, Transportation Engineering, Water Resources
description:
Civil engineering is the design, construction and maintenance of public works, such as roads, bridges, water and energy systems, ports and airports, as well as the infrastructure for a cleaner environment.

Civil engineers work in the public and private sectors in a variety of roles, including design, research and development, construction, and education.

Students in the BSE program in civil engineering gain a strong foundation in science and mathematics and learn the fundamentals of engineering design and management. They have the opportunity to focus on a specialized area of civil engineering in the senior year.
Accreditation status: The civil engineering, BSE program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

description:
The Bachelor of Science in civic and economic thought and leadership is a distinctive liberal arts program that provides students with an integrated and interdisciplinary understanding of the intellectual foundations of free societies and self-government. Students explore these questions by reading and discussing the great works of political, economic, ethical and philosophical thought.

The curriculum includes two semesters of study abroad or a semester in Washington, D.C., with a substantive internship.

The program combines liberal arts education with skills and experience for a broad range of careers, including in the fields of business, law, public service, nonprofit and education.
Program name: Civic and Economic Thought and Leadership, BS

description:
The Bachelor of Arts in classical studies is an interdisciplinary program designed for students who want a broad background in the cultures of ancient Greece and Rome and the influence of classical antiquity on later societies.

In this program, students study the contributions of the classical world to Western civilization through coursework in history, literature, philosophy, and religious studies.

The flexible curriculum allows students to design a course of study that aligns with their intellectual interests and professional goals, such as K-12 teaching, law school and graduate studies.

Students explore a number of different topics through their coursework, including:

ancient Greek and Roman literature
classical mythology
the history of women in antiquity
ancient medicine
the religions of ancient Greece and Rome
Roman law
Students interested in concentrating on a specific area of classical studies, such as history or philosophy, may count up to nine credit hours of coursework in other disciplines toward their major requirements. Those who want to study the ancient languages may count up to 14 credit hours of coursework in ancient Greek or Latin toward their major requirements.

Graduates are prepared for a variety of careers in business, education, government and law, and they are also well-prepared for graduate studies in a variety of fields, such as ancient history, archaeology, art history, classical studies, history, law, museum studies, philosophy and religious studies.

The Bachelor of Arts program in communication helps students understand the vital role of human communication. The program focuses on communication processes in a variety of contexts, from face-to-face to computer-mediated, from intrapersonal and interpersonal to group and organizational, and from intercultural to political and other societal-level contexts.

Students develop a broad-based understanding of the discipline and learn about the scholarly origins of the field through a diverse set of course offerings. They explore how communication creates, maintains and transforms identity, relationships, workplaces and communities.

Students develop critical thinking and analytical skills to address real-world problems. The program emphasizes the development of theory-based and research-informed communication skills and practices for professional and civic life.

The BS program in communication provides students with an understanding of the central role of communication in human lives. Students learn communication theories, research methods and practical skills that prepare them for a variety of careers and for graduate school.

The program emphasizes a social science approach to communication, focusing on theory and research.

Students may concentrate their studies in one of several areas: communication in relationships, group and organizational communication, health communication, intercultural communication, performance studies, persuasion and social influence, and political communication.

The BA program in community advocacy and social policy prepares students to address issues such as poverty, affordable housing, food security and health care access by working directly with communities to advance social, economic and environmental justice. Students in this interdisciplinary program gain the knowledge and skills necessary to bring about social change through community organizing and action.

The curriculum emphasizes an understanding of how public policies are made and implemented and of how to advocate for policies that lead to greater social justice. Students develop skills in leadership, communication, community organizing, advocacy and policy analysis through courses, internships and research. These skills prepare students to work with public officials, nonprofit organizations and community members to improve the social and economic well-being of local communities. Students learn to create positive social change through collective action.
Program name: Community Advocacy and Social Policy, BA

description:
The BS program in community development is a transdisciplinary program that provides students with the knowledge, skills and values to affect positive social change in diverse communities through public service in government and nonprofit organizations. The curriculum prepares students with the theoretical and practical knowledge needed to become professional community leaders, administrators and managers. The degree also prepares students for graduate studies in a variety of fields, including public administration, public policy, nonprofit studies and community development.

The coursework covers a wide range of topics, including social entrepreneurship, community organizing, nonprofit management, public policy, grant writing and fundraising, and program evaluation. All students complete a culminating experience that allows them to apply their knowledge in a real-world setting, solving public problems for public good.

The BS program in community health prepares students for a variety of career paths in public health and health care. Community health professionals improve the health and well-being of whole communities through education, promotion of healthy lifestyles and development of health programs and policies.

Students learn how to assess health needs and plan, implement and evaluate health programs for diverse populations across the lifespan. They also gain skills in communication, advocacy, leadership and critical thinking, all essential skills for a public health professional.

The community health program teaches students how to address all aspects of community health, from education to policy. Coursework focuses on the core functions of public health, including:
biostatistics
environmental health
epidemiology
health services administration
social and behavioral health

This program provides students with practical, real-world experiences through internships with community partners. Students also have the opportunity to participate in service-learning projects in partnership with local organizations and global health programs around the world. Graduates are qualified to take the exam to become a Certified Health Education Specialist.

The BS program in community sports management is a comprehensive degree program that prepares students for positions in managing and leading community sports programs offered by public, private and nonprofit organizations.

Students learn how to develop, lead, manage and evaluate community-based sports programs. The curriculum focuses on management and leadership theory and practice, the role sport plays in community and economic development, the importance of sports in promoting health and well-being, and strategies for using sport to promote social change. Students gain real-world experience through a senior-year internship.

Students must complete all program requirements, which include a minimum of 120 credit hours.

The comparative literature Bachelor of Arts program in the School of International Letters and Cultures provides students with the critical skills to analyze literature and culture from an international and interdisciplinary perspective. The comparative literature major offers a flexible curriculum allowing students to concentrate their coursework in a specific area of study that best aligns with their academic interests and career goals. Students choose their primary and secondary areas of emphasis from more than 10 areas of study, including literature from Africa, Asia, Europe and the Americas, as well as classical literature, Jewish studies, Latinx studies, film studies and translation. In addition to a global approach to the study of literature and culture, students benefit from a close-knit intellectual community of dedicated faculty and students. The comparative literature major develops students' foreign language expertise, cross-cultural understanding and research skills. A capstone course in the final semester allows students to conduct in-depth research on a topic of their choice and produce a final research project under the supervision of a faculty member.

The BSE program in computer engineering with a concentration in cybersecurity provides students with in-depth knowledge and skills in cybersecurity to build a secure and resilient cyberspace. The cybersecurity concentration addresses the design and analysis of secure systems. Students learn to identify and mitigate security vulnerabilities in computer systems and networks. They are taught how to design, develop and deploy secure software and hardware systems as well as how to apply cybersecurity principles and techniques to protect computer systems and networks from cyber threats. The program also provides hands-on experience in cybersecurity through lab-based courses and projects.

This program has the following main objectives:

graduates have a mastery of the fundamental knowledge for the practice of or for advanced study in computer engineering, including its scientific and engineering principles and the analytical and experimental skills to apply this knowledge;
graduates are prepared for a professional career in computer engineering, and they will be able to apply their knowledge and skills to solve real-world problems and to design and develop new products and systems; and
graduates are prepared for personal and professional growth through a commitment to lifelong learning, and they have the communication and teamwork skills to work effectively with others from a wide range of backgrounds.
Accreditation status: The computer engineering, BSE program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

description:
The computer engineering program is a broad-based engineering discipline that deals with the design and development of computer systems. The field has two major areas: computer hardware and computer software.

The study of computer hardware focuses on the design of digital systems and their component parts. The study of computer software engineering involves the specification, design, development and verification of software systems.

The curriculum is composed of courses in engineering, mathematics and the basic sciences (physics and chemistry). The engineering courses include a strong core of electrical and computer engineering classes and provide a well-rounded design experience. The courses cover the major areas of the discipline: computer architecture, computer networks, computer system design, digital logic design, embedded systems, programming and software engineering.

Graduates of this program are qualified for employment in the computer, defense, electronics, manufacturing and telecommunications industries and in government. They often work as embedded system designers, application developers and computer system designers.
Accreditation status: The computer engineering, BSE program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

Concentration name: Business Data Analytics, Cybersecurity, Enterprise Systems, Food Industry Management, Global Logistics Management, Human Resource Management, Sales and Marketing Essentials, Sports Business, Supply Chain Management
description:
The BS program in computer information systems is an innovative program that prepares students for careers in the rapidly expanding information technology field. The curriculum focuses on business concepts and information technology and the development and management of quality business computer information systems.

Students develop a strong foundation in application programming for business systems. This foundation is enhanced through upper-division coursework in areas such as systems analysis, database management, data communications and project management. Students learn to use state-of-the-art tools and techniques to develop creative solutions for business problems.

The W. P. Carey School of Business has an international reputation for its outstanding faculty and its research and is ranked in the top 30 nationally for its undergraduate business programs by U.S. News & World Report. Students have access to a rich learning environment and a nationally recognized faculty.

The program is offered at the Polytechnic and West campuses. The program at the West campus emphasizes the management of information systems. The program at the Polytechnic campus emphasizes enterprise computing and problem-solving through application development.
Accreditation status: The BS in computer information systems is accredited by the Computing Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org. The W. P. Carey School of Business is accredited by AACSB International, the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.

description: The Bachelor of Science in computer science with a concentration in cybersecurity provides students with an in-depth understanding of the essentials of computer science, including algorithms, data structures and computer architecture, as well as the theoretical foundations of computing. In addition, students gain a strong foundation in cybersecurity that will allow them to identify and mitigate security threats. The program emphasizes a hands-on approach to problem-solving with a focus on building systems and writing programs. Students complete courses in specialized topics such as information assurance, software security and network security. Graduates of this program are well prepared for careers in a range of industries, including health care, finance, and technology, as well as for further graduate studies in computer science and related fields.
Accreditation status: The BS program in computer science is accredited by the Computing Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

description:
The Bachelor of Science in computer science is a comprehensive program that prepares students for a variety of careers in computing. Students in the program develop a strong foundation in computer science and are introduced to topics such as:
- algorithms
- data structures
- logic
- programming languages
- software engineering

Students receive a broad education in the fundamentals of computer science, including its theoretical and mathematical foundations. Core coursework includes object-oriented programming, data structures and algorithms, and principles of programming languages. Students can specialize in an area of their interest through a variety of technical electives in areas such as artificial intelligence, computer graphics and software engineering.

The program's educational objectives are to produce graduates who:
- are successful in their professional careers.
- contribute to their profession and to society.
- are successful in post-baccalaureate studies, if they choose to pursue them.

Students learn to adapt to a changing technological world and can enter professions that are yet to be imagined.
Accreditation status: Computing Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org

description:
The Bachelor of Science in Engineering program in computer systems engineering is focused on the analysis, design, testing, integration and evaluation of hardware and software for digital computer systems, including embedded systems and general-purpose computer systems.

Students learn the fundamentals of computer systems from a bottom-up perspective, beginning with the basic building blocks of modern computer systems. They develop expertise in hardware design and computer architecture and in the operating systems and systems software that control and connect them. The program curriculum culminates in a year-long capstone design experience in which students work in multidisciplinary teams to solve a real-world problem and apply the knowledge gained throughout the program.

The curriculum gives students breadth across all the core engagement areas of computer systems engineering: computer systems design and analysis, hardware systems, software systems and applications. Students can also choose a concentration in cybersecurity. All students gain real-world experience through the two-semester capstone course, and they are prepared for the design and development of innovative computer systems to solve challenging real-world problems.
Accreditation status: The computer systems engineering (BSE) program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org/. Student outcomes and enrollment data are available at https://engineering.asu.edu/accreditation/.

description:
The BSE program in construction engineering provides students with a strong foundation in engineering fundamentals, construction management and engineering design. The curriculum prepares students to enter the modern construction industry with its ever-increasing challenges to build in a more efficient, safe and sustainable manner. Graduates are well-prepared for professional registration and leadership positions in the construction industry.

This program has a strong industry connection and hands-on curriculum. Students have many opportunities for internships and co-ops with some of the best construction companies in the nation. It also offers unique, hands-on learning experiences and opportunities to work with faculty on research. Students have access to a large network of successful alumni for career mentoring and professional guidance.

The construction engineering curriculum has three focus areas:

    building construction: design and management of building systems, which include electrical, heating and air conditioning, and plumbing systems
    heavy construction: infrastructure design, equipment and methods, and project management topics
    specialty construction: topics such as trenchless construction, demolition, and concrete materials and methods
Accreditation status: Accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org

description:
The BS program in construction management and technology prepares students with the knowledge and skills necessary for professional careers in the construction industry. The program emphasizes construction principles and management practices, offering students a broad range of career choices in the rapidly growing construction industry.

The curriculum includes three main areas: management, construction science and engineering. Students learn about construction materials, methods, cost estimating, scheduling and project control, and they develop business and management skills.

Through a comprehensive and integrated curriculum, the construction management and technology program develops professional builders and managers who can successfully carry out the construction process for complex building and civil projects. Students are able to focus their technical studies in one of three areas: commercial, heavy or specialty construction.

This program is offered by the School of Sustainable Engineering and the Built Environment, one of the seven Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering.
Accreditation status: The construction management program is accredited by the American Council for Construction Education.

description:
The BS program in counseling and applied psychological science provides students with a strong foundation in counseling and psychology theories and applications in a culturally diverse world.

The counseling and applied psychological science curriculum focuses on foundational knowledge in psychology and counseling, including multicultural counseling, theories, assessment, case management and research methods.

Students gain the research skills and the professional and ethical values needed to work with individuals, families and groups in a variety of mental health and human services settings.

Graduates are well-prepared for entry-level positions in those fields as well as for graduate study in counseling, social work and related areas.
Program name: Counseling and Applied Psychological Science, BS

description:
The Bachelor of Arts in English with a concentration in creative writing gives students the opportunity to work with nationally recognized faculty in a vibrant literary community. The curriculum allows students to explore multiple creative writing genres. The program emphasizes the study of literature as a foundation for the practice of creative writing.

The creative writing program provides a rich and diverse literary experience, a rigorous and inspiring classroom environment and a wealth of internship and publishing opportunities. Students gain experience in writing workshops and literature classes that provide the necessary skills for a variety of professions.

The Bachelor of Science in criminology and criminal justice is a nationally recognized program that provides a comprehensive understanding of the nature and causes of crime, criminal behavior, and the criminal justice system.

Students learn about the complexities of crime and justice in today's society. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in criminological theory, research methods, and the criminal justice system, which is crucial for careers in law enforcement, corrections, court administration, and various social service agencies. Students also gain valuable skills in critical thinking, data analysis, and effective communication, preparing them for a variety of professions in which a keen understanding of human behavior and social systems is required.

Graduates are well prepared for law school and for graduate studies in criminology and criminal justice or related fields.

The cross-sector leadership bachelor's degree program prepares students to become future leaders who are able to work with diverse stakeholders across the nonprofit, for-profit and public sectors to address and solve complex social challenges.

The program offers a core foundation in the values, knowledge and skills needed for leading across sectors, with the opportunity to customize the course work to focus on a particular leadership interest area (e.g., sustainability, social entrepreneurship, health care, etc.) through both required electives and a required minor.

Students pursuing this degree will examine the differences between the sectors, learn the historical context of each sector, understand how to work with a range of key stakeholders (e.g., boards of directors, staff, volunteers, etc.) and analyze the various governance and leadership structures within each sector.

Students also will develop skills in financial management, fundraising, marketing and evaluation as they apply to a range of organizations.

The BA program in cultural studies is an interdisciplinary program that focuses on the study of culture as a crucial domain for understanding social life, politics and power. In this program, students develop an understanding of what constitutes culture; how culture is produced, circulated and consumed; and how culture is connected with social, political and economic forces on local and global scales.

The program highlights the relationship between culture and power and explores how cultural forms and practices can both reproduce and contest social inequalities related to race, ethnicity, gender, class and nation. The curriculum provides students with the critical and methodological tools to analyze a wide range of cultural phenomena, including popular music, film, television, digital media, art, literature, fashion and subcultures.

Students gain transdisciplinary perspectives by taking courses taught by faculty in the humanities and social sciences from a variety of fields, including:

American studies
communication
history
literary studies
performance studies
political science
sociology
women and gender studies
The program's flexible curriculum also allows students to complement their coursework in cultural studies with a wide range of electives from across the university and encourages them to gain professional experience through internships.

Graduates are prepared for a variety of professions in which a critical and broad understanding of culture is vital, including careers in education, journalism, law, marketing, public service and the nonprofit sector. Graduates are also well-prepared for graduate study in cultural studies, the humanities and the social sciences.

The BA program in culture, technology and environment provides students with a broad set of tools for understanding and addressing the complex interrelationships of technology and environment through society and culture. The program also trains students to communicate effectively about science, technology and environment in a variety of contexts and through diverse media.

The curriculum trains students in social and historical approaches to examining and communicating about science, technology and environment. Students learn to analyze and frame humanistic and social science issues, such as environmental justice, and they gain experience with diverse media through which they are communicated. They become familiar with the social, political and cultural dimensions of major areas of scientific and technological change, such as information technology, biotechnology, energy, nanotechnology and sustainability. The program emphasizes problem-based and experience-based learning in which students develop intellectual, professional and practical skills.

The BS program in data science provides a strong foundation in computer science, mathematics and statistics and enables students to develop interdisciplinary data science knowledge through a wide variety of application domains. Students can gain experience with data acquisition, data modeling and data analysis, with a particular focus on the computational tools to accomplish these at scale. The curriculum culminates with a senior-year capstone experience in which students work in teams on a data science project, often with an external industry or government partner. This hands-on experience provides students with the critical skills and knowledge they need to be successful in the data science workforce or to continue their education in graduate school.

The bachelor's degree program in graphic design provides students with a broad-based, hands-on and diverse learning experience that prepares them to participate in a variety of creative professional fields. Students learn about design history and theory and put their knowledge into practice with a wide range of required studio courses that explore typography, branding, print, web design, experience design and more. The curriculum also allows for flexibility in students' final year of the program to allow them to pursue their individual interests. Students benefit from the program's strong connections to the local and national design community. The program's design studios, lecture halls, labs and galleries are located at the heart of the ASU Tempe campus in the College of Design North and South buildings and the Art Building.

The industrial design program at The Design School is widely acclaimed and NASAD-accredited. It is a comprehensive, transdisciplinary and professional course of study, where students are prepared to design a future that is socially, culturally, economically and environmentally sustainable.

Graduates of the industrial design program are prepared to enter a wide variety of careers where they can apply their creative, collaborative and problem-solving skills to help businesses and organizations to develop services, products and systems that improve everyday life. The curriculum of the industrial design program fosters a user-centered design approach, which provides students with a qualitative understanding of people and a rigorous framework for developing more meaningful designs. Students learn to translate their empathetic understandings of people's wants and needs into compelling products, services and systems that improve the human experience.

The industrial design curriculum prepares students to thrive in a global marketplace by providing them with the professional knowledge and technical skills they need to transform their ideas into reality. Students learn how to communicate and collaborate within transdisciplinary teams and to work with a diverse set of partners, including small businesses, multinational corporations, governmental agencies and not-for-profit organizations. Through these partnerships, students in the industrial design program are provided with numerous hands-on, project-based learning opportunities and are connected to an accomplished community of professional practitioners who help to inform, guide and mentor them during their education and after they graduate.
Accreditation status: NASAD-accredited

description:
The BSD program in interior design at The Design School provides students a formal education that cultivates the knowledge and skills necessary to design functional, safe, efficient and beautiful interior environments for a wide range of human activities and purposes, ranging in scale from the domestic to the corporate and from the retail to the institutional.

Students learn to critically assess user and client needs and to creatively and systematically apply the design process to solve complex problems and create innovative, life-enhancing interior designs. Graduates of this program are prepared to enter professional practice to pursue careers in a variety of design firms or in related fields.
Accreditation status: The interior design program is accredited by the Council for Interior Design Accreditation, https://www.accredit-id.org/, 206 Grandville Avenue, Suite 350, Grand Rapids, MI, 49503.

description:
The BA program in design studies is an interdisciplinary, research-focused degree that provides students with a broad understanding of design thinking and practice.

This human-centered program is ideal for students who are interested in design but seek a liberal arts-based degree. Students develop a transdisciplinary and holistic understanding of design as a social, cultural, historical, economic and political force in society. They learn through making, researching and writing about design in its various forms. Coursework allows students to examine design through a range of lenses, including: design history, theory and criticism, social innovation, sustainability, materials and technology, business and entrepreneurship.

Students are not required to take studio classes; however, with special permission, they may incorporate a selection of design studio courses into their program. Students have access to state-of-the-art facilities, including fabrication labs and photography and printmaking studios.

Students gain essential skills in research, problem-solving, creative and critical thinking, communication, leadership and collaboration. Graduates are prepared for a variety of careers in both the public and private sectors, including positions in education, curation, design research, and strategy and management, and for advanced study in fields such as business, law, design criticism, and design history and theory.

The BS program in digital audiences provides students with a foundational understanding of how to engage and grow audiences across digital platforms. Students learn to use data and analytics to understand digital audience behavior and develop content strategies that build and engage audiences through social media, search engine optimization and other digital channels.

Coursework emphasizes practical applications, critical thinking, problem-solving, and the ethical issues related to digital audiences and platforms.

Students learn to develop strategies and tactics to build and grow digital audiences across various digital platforms and channels. They also learn how to create and distribute compelling content to digital audiences and measure and report on the effectiveness of those strategies.

Graduates are prepared for careers that involve creating and managing content for online audiences, managing social media and online communities, creating content marketing, and analyzing audience data.

The digital culture BA program with a concentration in art is part of the School of Arts, Media and Engineering, a collaboration between the Herberger Institute for Design and the Arts and the Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering.

The program gives students a solid foundation in the concepts, methods and technologies of digital media creation in an arts context, including 2-D and 3-D imaging, sound, video, interactivity, web design, and programming for media arts.

Students develop creative and critical thinking skills through an interdisciplinary curriculum combining arts, design and engineering coursework, research and hands-on projects. In the program's project-based learning environment, students gain valuable teamwork and leadership experience, working with other students and with faculty in arts and engineering to build new systems for creative expression.

Students in the digital culture program use the resources of both the Herberger Institute for Design and the Arts and the Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering and work with faculty members from both. The program is one of the only of its kind in the nation to offer a curriculum with courses from both an arts and an engineering college.

The Bachelor of Arts in digital culture with a concentration in arts and design studies provides students with a project-based curriculum where they gain an understanding of digital systems, and they learn to develop computational media and integrate new technologies with creative practice and expression. The digital culture BA program provides an opportunity for students to choose from a highly interdisciplinary set of courses focused on a common theme or area of practice. Students choose from a rich set of concentration areas to create their own course of study, or they can design their own focus in consultation with a faculty advisor.

This program is available for students as a standard four-year bachelor's degree program or for students who have completed an Associate of Arts in digital arts from an Arizona community college. Students transferring with an Associate of Arts in digital arts may be able to complete their degree in two years.
Program name: Digital Culture (Arts and Design Studies), BA

description:
The Bachelor of Arts in digital culture with a concentration in English is a transdisciplinary degree that connects the humanities and the arts with science and technology. Students in this program focus on the study of language and writing within the digital realm.

The curriculum prepares students with a strong foundation in the history and contemporary practice of digital media, as well as opportunities for hands-on, collaborative and project-based learning. In addition to a variety of digital culture course options, students also take a series of courses from the Department of English in The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences.

The digital culture BA program with a concentration in film enables students to learn film and media production in the context of a 21st-century digital-media environment.

Students in the film concentration learn by making. They are introduced to the full pipeline of film and media production, from ideation and screenwriting to production (cinematography, directing, sound) to post-production (editing, sound and visual effects).

The concentration provides a strong basis for further study in film theory and history by embedding production courses within a larger media-studies context.

Students can choose to further specialize in areas like directing, screenwriting, producing, cinematography, editing and visual effects. The curriculum focuses on narrative and documentary filmmaking in single-camera and multicamera studio production modes.

Through their study, students gain a solid foundation for careers in the film industry.

The digital culture BA program with a concentration in graphic information technology is an interdisciplinary program that allows students to focus on how new media is transforming the creation, visualization and consumption of graphics, particularly in cross-media publishing environments, such as print, web and mobile devices. Students learn how media is produced, used and evaluated in a variety of contexts, including fine arts, humanities, social sciences, and science and technology.

The program of study is composed of a broad range of courses from a number of different disciplines and encourages students to experiment and combine different media in new and innovative ways. Students will develop their creativity and critical thinking skills as they learn how to produce, analyze, and manage media for a variety of audiences.

Core coursework provides a solid foundation in the techniques and practices of digital media, and in the critical and theoretical analysis of media and information. The curriculum is project-based, and students are encouraged to be independent learners and to participate in a variety of learning communities, including student organizations, clubs, research groups and labs.

Students in the graphic information technology concentration learn to apply principles of graphic design in web design and publishing, multimedia design and commercial photography and video. The program prepares students for a range of career opportunities involving visual design and technology and provides a strong foundation for a variety of graduate programs.

The Bachelor of Arts in digital culture with a concentration in media processing provides students with a foundation in the computing principles and creative practices of digital media. Students gain an understanding of the cultural and social implications of new forms of media creation and expression, and they develop practical skills in media art production. The program offers transdisciplinary coursework in digital media, programming, arts and design, and students use the concepts they learn in class to create their own original artworks and build a portfolio of diverse projects. This program's focus on media processing helps students develop a mastery of audio and visual media computation. The program faculty are leaders in their respective fields, and they bring their expertise and passion to the classroom.

The Bachelor of Arts program in digital culture with a concentration in music focuses on creating new musical works and tools. Students combine their musical training and creativity with new digital technologies in order to explore and create in areas such as:
algorithmic composition
interactive performance
music and multimedia
new interfaces for musical expression
sound art
sound design
This is a concentration in the Digital Culture, BA program.
In their coursework, students work in a research-based, transdisciplinary and collaborative environment that provides the technical, theoretical and historical foundations for them to create their own digital media work. The core curriculum is a project-based learning environment. Students learn by making.
Additionally, students take courses in a related area and complete their studies with a final portfolio project.
Graduates are prepared for careers in the creative industries and for graduate study.

The Bachelor of Arts in digital culture with a concentration in theatre is an interdisciplinary program that prepares students for careers in the performing arts as well as in areas that use performance-based approaches and methods, such as film, media performance, motion capture, gaming, performance capture and virtual performance.

The curriculum provides a foundation of courses in theatre history, dramatic literature, acting and directing, performance and design and technology. Students select a series of courses that align with their interests, in consultation with a faculty mentor.

The program culminates in a senior project that involves the creation and production of a live performance or media project. Students are prepared to enter graduate programs in film, performance studies and theatre and to work in professional theatre companies and in the entertainment industry.

Concentration name: Art, Design, English, Film, Interdisciplinary Arts and Performance, Media Arts, Music, Theatre
description:
The Bachelor of Arts in digital culture prepares students to be creative thinkers, collaborative leaders and innovative designers of new media.

Students pursuing the digital culture BA degree select one of the following concentrations: art, design, English, film, interdisciplinary arts and performance, media arts, music, theatre.

The concentration allows for in-depth study in a specific arts and design discipline as it is impacted by digital technology and culture. Digital culture faculty are leading experts and researchers in their fields, from responsive environments and experience design to virtual reality and games.

The program is part of the School of Arts, Media and Engineering, a transdisciplinary school where artists and scientists collaborate. Students learn in an environment that values curiosity, creativity, collaboration and discovery, and they graduate prepared for a wide array of careers in the culture and creative industries.

The digital culture program provides a project-based and transdisciplinary curriculum in which students learn by doing. Foundational coursework in computer science, art, design and music provides students with the creative and technical skills to succeed in their future coursework and careers. Students then build upon these skills in advanced coursework and applied projects focused on topics ranging from wearable technology and interactive installations to game design and virtual reality. Throughout the program, students collaborate with peers from a variety of disciplines and with faculty who are leaders in their fields.

The BS program in digital marketing provides students with the critical knowledge of marketing in the digital environment. The curriculum offers a solid grounding in business and marketing and a specialization in digital marketing techniques and practices.

The focus is on search engine optimization, social media and mobile marketing, content marketing, web analytics, and marketing automation. Students are trained to use state-of-the-art tools for web and social media analytics and learn how to help businesses create and manage their digital marketing strategies.

Students gain valuable experience through project-based learning. In their final year, they develop a portfolio by developing a social media campaign for a real client as well as a search engine optimization project.

Graduates of this program may become social media marketing managers, marketing analytics specialists or search engine optimization specialists, or they can pursue a variety of other careers in marketing.
Accreditation status: All W. P. Carey School of Business degrees are accredited by AACSB International.

description:
The BS program in disability studies provides students with a complex understanding of disability as a social, cultural and political phenomenon. This interdisciplinary degree program draws upon faculty and courses from a wide range of academic disciplines, including history, literature, philosophy, applied behavior analysis, and speech and hearing science, among others.

Students examine the ways in which social values, cultural representations and institutional practices have shaped the experiences of people with disabilities throughout history, as well as the ways in which people with disabilities have shaped their own lives. Students gain a deeper knowledge of the history of disability, disability culture and the disability rights movement. They also gain a deeper understanding of key disability legislation, including the Americans with Disabilities Act, and they learn to think critically about how disability is represented in the media and popular culture.

Graduates are prepared for careers in fields such as disability advocacy, policy, education, health care, social work, rehabilitation, counseling and human services.

The BAE in early childhood and early childhood special education offers an innovative, inclusive and interdisciplinary approach to early childhood education for children from birth to age 8. The program emphasizes the development of the whole child as well as learning experiences that are relationship-based, culturally responsive, play-based, and family centered. This program is offered with teacher certification. Students in the teacher certification track benefit from a yearlong residency and a professional learning network as part of their program. Students can select to add an English as a second language endorsement for no additional credit hours, helping them become more culturally responsive educators prepared to teach in diverse classrooms. Graduates are eligible to receive an institutional recommendation from ASU for teacher certification in early childhood education (birth to age 8 or grade 3) and early childhood special education (birth to age 8 or grade 3) in the state of Arizona and most other states.
Accreditation status: Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College is accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation.
Program name: Early Childhood and Early Childhood Special Education, BAE

description:
The Bachelor of Applied Science in early childhood studies provides a pathway for students who have earned an associate degree in early childhood education to complete a bachelor's degree. Students acquire advanced knowledge of the early childhood field with a focus on leadership, advocacy, and working with diverse children and families.

Graduates are prepared for a variety of careers in early childhood education, including teaching in Head Start or child care programs, providing early intervention services, and serving in an administrative capacity in early childhood programs.

This degree does not lead to teacher certification.

The Bachelor of Arts in earth and environmental studies prepares students for careers in which they assess, understand and manage the natural world and our relationship to it. Students learn the fundamental concepts of earth system science and systems thinking; gain proficiency in geospatial and field techniques for observing the environment; and master qualitative and quantitative approaches for analyzing and interpreting environmental data.

The interdisciplinary curriculum addresses the structure and function of Earth's natural systems, including the solid earth, hydrosphere, atmosphere and biosphere, as well as the complex ways that human societies interact with these systems. Students can focus on topics that include earth system science, geological sciences, environmental science, sustainability, water resources, natural resource management and environmental policy. The program is flexible and allows students to choose courses that suit their individual interests and career plans.

A senior-year capstone experience gives students the opportunity to conduct independent research, engage in an internship or study abroad.

The Bachelor of Science degree program in earth and space exploration with a concentration in astrobiology and biogeosciences is an an interdisciplinary program designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the natural sciences and engineering with a focus on understanding the past, present and future of life in the universe. Astrobiology and biogeosciences are fields that bring together geology, biology, chemistry, astronomy and physics to address questions about the origin of life and its evolution on Earth and to search for life elsewhere in the universe.

The program prepares students for graduate studies and a wide variety of careers in the space industry, environmental consulting, medical science, laboratory research, science education and public outreach.

The curriculum includes a core set of courses in geology, biology and chemistry and advanced coursework focused on topics such as the evolution of life, the search for life in the solar system, and the interactions between life and the environment. Students are required to conduct research with a faculty mentor, which provides them with hands-on experience in the field and the laboratory.

Students should be sure to work with an academic advisor in the School of Earth and Space Exploration to select courses that are right for their career goals.
Program name: Earth and Space Exploration (Astrobiology and Biogeosciences), BS

description:
The Bachelor of Science degree program in earth and space exploration with a concentration in astrophysics is an appropriate choice for students interested in careers in astronomy, planetary science and space exploration.

Students in this degree program are required to participate in an introductory seminar in their first year of study as well as a senior-level capstone research or design experience.

This program has an optional component of paid, degree-related employment available through its partnership with the ASU Co-op program. An internship may count toward career-focused required or elective credit in the student's degree program. Students are responsible for securing their own internship or co-op opportunities. Career and Professional Development Services is a resource for students. Students should speak with their academic advisor for more information.

Students in this program are well-prepared to pursue careers in a range of science, technology and engineering fields as well as attend graduate school.

The Bachelor of Science in Earth and Space Exploration with a concentration in Earth sciences provides students with a fundamental background in Earth sciences and prepares them for graduate school or a career in the many quantitative subdisciplines of Earth and environmental sciences. These include environmental consulting, resource exploration, economic geology and geochemistry and geophysics.

The curriculum is designed to have the necessary rigor in mathematics, physics and chemistry to enable students to tackle the real-world Earth and space problems of today and the future. Students engage in authentic, research-oriented activities both inside and outside the classroom. They have the opportunity to participate in field trips and can learn to operate a variety of analytical instruments in their courses and through independent study projects supervised by faculty members.
The degree program offers students exceptional opportunities to participate in research with faculty in the School of Earth and Space Exploration who are internationally recognized in their fields. This program produces highly competitive graduates who go on to careers in research and industry.
Program name: Earth and Space Exploration (Earth Sciences), BS

description:
The Bachelor of Science in Earth and Space Exploration with a concentration in exploration systems design is a transdisciplinary degree that provides a deep understanding of space mission engineering and scientific fundamentals. This degree is well suited to students who wish to pursue a career as a systems engineer in the space and defense industries.

Students in this concentration take a series of systems engineering courses offered through the School of Earth and Space Exploration that prepare them to develop and operate complex systems, including space flight hardware, ground-based scientific instrumentation, and scientific data processing systems. These courses use a hands-on, project-based approach, and students spend most of their time working on a team to build and test space flight hardware or to design space missions. Many systems engineering courses are taken with graduate students who bring valuable experience to the student teams. The courses culminate in a senior capstone project course in which the students design, build, test, fly and operate a payload on a high-altitude balloon, sounding rocket or orbital CubeSat spacecraft.
Program name: Earth and Space Exploration (Exploration Systems Design), BS

description:
The geological sciences concentration in the BS program in earth and space exploration focuses on understanding the past, present and future of the Earth and other rocky planets. Students learn to apply the principles of chemistry, physics and mathematics, in combination with modern geological concepts, to understand the solid Earth and to explore its resources. The program's challenging coursework and ample research opportunities prepare students for graduate studies and a wide variety of careers in the energy and mining industries, environmental consulting, government, and K-12 and postsecondary education.

Students in the geological sciences concentration are trained to understand Earth systems and their resources. The curriculum gives students a robust foundation in the physical sciences and a broad background in all core areas of geology. Students can work with faculty on research ranging from the study of active volcanoes and their hazards to the analysis of the geology and composition of other planets. School of Earth and Space Exploration faculty are internationally recognized in their fields, and the school has state-of-the-art analytical, experimental and computational facilities.
Program name: Earth and Space Exploration (Geological Sciences), BS

description:
The BA program in East Asian studies offers students a broad interdisciplinary perspective on China, Japan and Korea. The program brings together faculty and courses from a wide range of academic disciplines, including anthropology, art history, business, geography, history, languages and literatures, political science and religious studies.

The curriculum allows students to pursue an area of particular interest while also providing a solid foundation of knowledge about the broader East Asian region.

Students are encouraged to develop a high level of language proficiency and to participate in a study abroad program in order to enrich their understanding of the cultures, societies and contemporary affairs of East Asia.

Concentration name: Politics and the Economy, Public Policy
description:
The BS program in economics provides students with a deeper and more quantitative understanding of economics than is available through the BA program. It prepares students for a wider range of careers in business and government and is especially appropriate for students who wish to pursue a doctorate in economics or an advanced degree in a quantitative business field, such as finance.

A distinguishing feature of the program is its emphasis on the development of quantitative and analytical skills.

The Department of Economics in the W. P. Carey School of Business has an international reputation for its research productivity, with a faculty that produces cutting-edge research in a wide variety of areas, including:

- econometrics
- macroeconomics
- international economics
- industrial organization
- labor economics
- experimental economics
- environmental economics
- health economics
- public economics
- law and economics
- development economics

Many of the faculty have been elected as fellows of the Econometric Society, a distinction of high honor in the economics profession.

The BS in economics is a STEM-designated degree program.
Accreditation status: The W. P. Carey School of Business is accredited by AACSB International.

description:
The BAE in educational studies with a concentration in early childhood studies offers a pathway for students interested in a variety of careers working with young children from birth to age 8. The program focuses on child development, learning theory and family and community relationships.

Graduates are well-prepared for entry-level positions in a variety of roles within the early childhood field, such as in Head Start and Early Head Start, child care centers, private preschool programs and other organizations that serve young children and their families.

This program does not lead to teacher certification.

The BAE in educational studies is a non-licensure bachelor's degree program that provides a broad foundation of knowledge in education theory and practice. The curriculum focuses on how people learn and how to best facilitate that learning, giving students the skills and knowledge to engage in meaningful work in education-related fields without obtaining a teaching credential.

Students in this program are prepared for a variety of careers in educational settings outside of the traditional K-12 public school classroom, such as in community education, nonprofit organizations and private tutoring companies. This major is also ideal for those interested in education policy and advocacy, and for students who are passionate about learning but who do not intend to become classroom teachers.

Students can customize their degree program by selecting electives to align with their specific interests and career goals. An array of relevant minors and certificates are also available.

The BSE program in electrical engineering with a concentration in electric power and energy systems is focused on the area of electrical engineering concerned with the generation, transmission, distribution and utilization of electric power and the electrical apparatus connected to such systems. This program provides students a rigorous curriculum in electrical engineering combined with focused coursework in electric power and energy systems.

Electrical engineering is a driving force of modern technology. Graduates with a BSE in electrical engineering with a concentration in electric power and energy systems learn how to develop new products or systems that use electricity or electromagnetism and become specialists in generating, transmitting, distributing and utilizing electric power.

The curriculum provides a strong foundation in circuits, electromagnetics, solid-state devices and computers that allow graduates to pursue careers in a wide range of industries.
Accreditation status: The electrical engineering, BSE program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Program Criteria for Electrical, Computer, Communications, Telecommunication(s) and Similarly Named Engineering Programs.
Program name: Electrical Engineering (Electric Power and Energy Systems), BSE

description:
The BSE program in electrical engineering is a broad-based, flexible program that provides students with a strong foundation in the fundamentals of electrical engineering.

The curriculum provides a thorough grounding in the basics of electrical engineering, including circuits, electronics, electromagnetics, and digital systems. Students learn about the design and analysis of electrical and electronic systems, as well as the application of electrical engineering principles to a wide range of problems.

The program also includes a strong emphasis on laboratory work and design projects, which provide students with hands-on experience in the field.

Graduates of the program are well-prepared for careers in a variety of industries, including electronics, telecommunications, power systems and aerospace. They are also well-prepared for graduate study in electrical engineering and related fields.
Accreditation status: The electrical engineering, BSE program at the Tempe campus is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

Concentration name: Bilingual Education and English as a Second Language
description:
The BAE program in elementary education with a concentration in bilingual education and English as a second language prepares students to work with children in K-8 general education classrooms and to work specifically with children who are English language learners. The program provides teacher candidates with a strong foundation in the professional knowledge and skills necessary to become a successful classroom teacher in a variety of school settings.

The program is specifically designed to prepare teacher candidates for the multicultural and multilingual classrooms of today's schools and fulfills all requirements for the Arizona Elementary Teacher Certificate for grades K-8 as well as the Bilingual and English as a Second Language endorsements.

The professional education component of this degree features a series of courses focusing on child development, teaching methods, English language acquisition, Spanish language and Latino culture, and the needs of exceptional children. Students participate in a number of school-based experiences throughout the program that provide opportunities to apply what they are learning in their university courses to the real world of the classroom. These experiences are structured so that students begin by observing and assisting in a classroom and gradually assume more responsibility for instructing and managing the classroom. The program culminates in a full-time student teaching experience.

For information about the professional education sequence, including the specific courses that students take and the school-based experiences in which they participate, students should visit the Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College website at http://education.asu.edu/.
Program name: Elementary Education (Bilingual Education and English as a Second Language), BAE

description:
The BAE program in elementary education prepares students to teach kindergarten through eighth grade. The program leads to teacher certification in elementary education, grades K-8, in Arizona.

Students also have the opportunity to add an endorsement or an additional certificate to their degree. Coursework in education theory and methods is combined with multiple field experiences in K-8 classrooms throughout the program. Students gain extensive experience working with children in a variety of school settings. Students' professional growth is supported through personalized academic and career advising as well as by expert faculty and accomplished mentor teachers.

The program is offered at four ASU campuses and at sites across Arizona through ASU Local, providing options for students seeking a range of university experiences and learning environments.
Accreditation status: Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College is accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation.

Concentration name: Bilingual Education and English as a Second Language, Educating Multilingual Learners
description:
The BAE in elementary education prepares students to teach first grade through eighth grade. The program combines rigorous, research-based coursework with extensive classroom-based field experiences. These experiences are structured to produce highly qualified, confident and effective elementary school teachers.

Students select from a variety of school settings in which to complete their field experiences, including public, charter, private, urban, suburban and rural schools. These classroom-based experiences are guided by their assigned mentor teacher and a university supervisor. In their final semester, students complete a full-time, student-teaching residency.

Graduates earn an institutional recommendation from ASU to the Arizona Department of Education for teacher certification in elementary education for grades one through eight. This program is available to students at the ASU Downtown Phoenix, Polytechnic, Tempe and West campuses, as well as at several off-campus locations in eastern and central Arizona.
Accreditation status: Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College is accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation.

Concentration name: Biosecurity and Threat Management, Community Resilience, Cybersecurity Policy and Management, Emergency Management, Homeland Security, Hazard Mitigation and Resilient Communities
description:
The BS program in emergency management and homeland security focuses on the management of all hazards and threats that pose a significant risk to people, communities, infrastructure and the nation. These challenges include manmade, natural and technological disasters, as well as terrorist threats. The program's goal is to minimize the impact of these events on individuals, communities and the nation.

The curriculum prepares students for future leadership positions in public, nonprofit and private organizations. The program's core courses provide a strong theoretical foundation in the comprehensive, all-hazards approach to the emergency management and homeland security fields.

Students are provided with a robust practical dimension through which they learn to apply their classroom knowledge to real-world problems. They also are equipped with the analytical and critical thinking skills needed to effectively respond to and manage complex critical incidents.

The program's faculty have extensive professional experience in all levels of government, the private sector and nonprofit organizations. They also are nationally and internationally recognized for their research and expertise in these fields.
Program name: Emergency Management and Homeland Security, BS

description:
The automotive systems concentration in the engineering BSE program focuses on the design and manufacturing of automobiles and on the integration of automotive components into a final product that is efficient, safe and cost-effective. The program places emphasis on hands-on experiences and solving real-world problems in student team environments, including many opportunities for students to participate in national competitions.

The curriculum in the automotive systems concentration covers topics in automotive structures, vehicle dynamics and controls, hybrid vehicle powertrains, advanced manufacturing and alternative fuels. Upon graduation, graduates will have the knowledge and skills necessary to make an immediate impact in the automotive industry.
Accreditation status: The engineering, BSE program with a concentration in automotive systems is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

description:
The BSE program in engineering with a concentration in electrical systems focuses on the theme of power and energy systems. Electrical systems are responsible for the generation, transmission and distribution of electric power as well as the design and manufacturing of a large variety of electrical devices and systems, from small-scale integrated circuits to large-scale power generators.

Students learn how to design and build electrical devices and systems, such as:

biomedical devices
communication systems
electric motors and drives
electronic circuits
power generation and distribution systems
remote sensors

The curriculum is hands-on and project-based. Students build on a foundation of mathematics and science to develop analytical skills and learn to design and build real-world systems in a collaborative, team-based environment. This program is offered by the School of Electrical, Computer and Energy Engineering, part of the Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering.
Accreditation status: The bachelor's degree program in engineering (electrical systems) is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

description:
The BSE program in engineering with a concentration in mechanical engineering systems is focused on the design of mechanical systems. Graduates of this program will be equipped with a fundamental knowledge of mechanics, thermal sciences and design process to create innovative products and services. Coursework covers the following areas: statics, dynamics, solid mechanics, materials, thermodynamics, heat transfer, fluid mechanics, design, manufacturing processes and systems analysis. The program is specifically designed to provide students with hands-on labs and state-of-the-art facilities that include advanced equipment, such as wind tunnels, material testing machines, manufacturing systems and 3D printing, enabling them to gain practical skills and experience to meet the needs of the industry.

This program is offered at the Polytechnic campus and offers a practice-based curriculum with a focus on project-based learning. In their final year of study, students are required to complete a senior capstone design project that involves them working with a team to solve a real-world problem for an external stakeholder. The program's proximity to industry in the East Valley of Phoenix provides opportunities for student internships, research and projects.

This program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.
Accreditation status: This program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

description: The BSE program in engineering with a concentration in robotics focuses on the design and development of robots and robotics systems. This interdisciplinary curriculum provides a broad foundation in the science and mathematics of engineering along with hands-on experience in the design and prototyping of modern engineering systems.
