The courses in the curriculum focus on mechanical design, manufacturing, electronics, control systems and computer science to develop a strong foundation in robotics. The program provides the knowledge and skills necessary to design, develop and implement robotic systems to meet the needs of modern society. Graduates of the BSE in engineering with a concentration in robotics are well-prepared for a variety of job opportunities in the high-demand areas of robotics, automation and manufacturing. Industries served by robotics engineers include aerospace, automotive, national defense, medical devices, agriculture, entertainment, manufacturing and the emerging area of personal robotics.
Accreditation status: This program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Program Criteria for an engineering program of a level and scope commensurate with the title of the program.

description:
The Bachelor of Science in Engineering program in engineering management provides a foundation of engineering, math, science, business and management, upon which is built the technical skills and business acumen needed to excel in management and leadership roles.

The curriculum is a blend of traditional industrial engineering courses and courses in business and management, covering topics such as supply chain management, project management, quality control, production planning, computer applications and operations research. The program has two focus areas: industrial engineering and software engineering.

Graduates are able to design, implement and manage complex management systems that involve people, materials, information, equipment and energy. They have an in-depth understanding of technology, innovation, and the challenges of a globally competitive market, as well as the ability to improve the quality of goods and services while reducing costs.

The program's educational objective is to produce graduates who are technically competent and business-aware and who are prepared to succeed in a globally competitive marketplace.
Accreditation status: The engineering management, BSE program at the Polytechnic campus is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

description:
The Bachelor of Arts in English with a concentration in creative writing gives students the opportunity to work with and be mentored by distinguished faculty with national and international reputations.

Students in this program study the art and craft of creative writing in a variety of genres, including:

Creative nonfiction
Fiction
Poetry
Screenwriting
Spoken word and performance poetry
Students read and analyze a wide variety of texts to identify and learn narrative and aesthetic strategies. They apply what they learn as they write and revise their own work. In small workshop classes, students share and critique each other's work and gain experience in craft analysis, collaborative discussion and revision strategies. In addition to gaining a solid foundation in the study of literature, students may also take courses in linguistics, film and media studies or creative writing.

Graduates of this program have all the skills of an English major, including skills in critical reading, analysis and writing, with the added benefit of experience in writing creatively, giving and receiving feedback, and revising their own work for an audience.

This program is also available as an online program.

The Bachelor of Arts program in English with a concentration in linguistics focuses on the formal study of language in its humanistic and scientific dimensions, including the nature of subconscious linguistic knowledge, the ways in which languages are acquired, the ways in which languages change and vary, and the roles language plays in society and literature.

The concentration includes courses covering the core areas of linguistics (phonetics, phonology, syntax and semantics) as well as courses in a variety of other topics, including:

    historical linguistics
    language acquisition
    language variation and change
    morphology
    pragmatics
    sociolinguistics

Students in the linguistics concentration acquire skills in data analysis, argumentation and cross-cultural understanding. These skills can lead to careers in business, computer science, government, law and teaching, including teaching English to speakers of other languages.

The Bachelor of Arts in English with a concentration in literature immerses students in the study of literature and culture. Literature is a living art form with a rich history of traditions from around the globe. Those who study literature at ASU explore the ways it reflects, shapes and critiques cultures. Students learn to read with greater insight, to write with greater clarity and grace, and to think with greater critical acumen.

The literature program offers a wide range of courses in English, American and world literatures, from introductory surveys to specialized seminars, including courses on:

classical and medieval literature
digital humanities
ethnic American literature
film studies
global and postcolonial literature
literary history
literary theory
popular literature
Renaissance literature
rhetoric and composition
women's literature

Students can count courses from other departments --- classics, history, philosophy, religious studies, and women and gender studies --- toward the major. The flexibility of the curriculum encourages students to combine a passion for literary study with a wide range of other interests.

The Bachelor of Arts in English with a concentration in secondary education prepares students for careers as English language arts teachers in middle schools, junior high schools and high schools. In this program, students develop a broad and deep understanding of literature, rhetoric and composition, linguistics, and adolescent literacy that translates directly into effective and inspiring teaching of the English language arts. Coursework is aligned with the standards of the National Council of Teachers of English and the Arizona Department of Education.

The program is offered by the Department of English in The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences in collaboration with Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College.

Professional experiences are an integral part of this program. Students complete a variety of field experiences in which they observe, tutor and teach in middle school and high school classrooms. During the final two semesters, students are engaged full-time in student teaching with an experienced and qualified mentor teacher. The MLFTC Office of Professional Experiences assists in coordinating all placements.

This program prepares students to meet the requirements for institutional recommendation for teacher certification in the state of Arizona.
Accreditation status: The Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College is accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation.

description:
The Bachelor of Arts in English with a concentration in writing, rhetorics and literacies provides a comprehensive education in writing and rhetoric useful for a variety of professions in which written, visual and digital communication are central.

This English program emphasizes the study of writing in a variety of contexts to prepare students for careers in which strong writing, research and analytical skills are essential.

Students in this program explore the history, theory and practice of writing. They develop skills in argument and persuasion, discourse analysis, digital literacies, research methods and the study of writing in a range of public and professional contexts.

Students analyze how texts (written, visual, digital) are produced, how they circulate and how they are received by different audiences in a variety of contexts. They learn to be more effective writers and communicators, preparing them for jobs in industry, government and education as well as graduate study.

The bachelor's degree program in English provides a comprehensive and dynamic curriculum in which students explore the power of language and literature to shape the world.

The program features small classes, award-winning faculty and a great deal of flexibility so that students can focus their studies on what most interests them.

The curriculum also fosters transferable skills that are highly valued by employers in every profession: sophisticated reading and writing skills, critical and creative thinking, strong research abilities and a nuanced understanding of diverse cultures.

The Department of English also offers students the opportunity to earn a bachelor's degree and a master's degree in a shorter amount of time through the 4+1 accelerated degree program. After completing the undergraduate requirements, students in this accelerated program can share up to 12 credit hours between the BA and the MA, thus decreasing the time it takes to earn both degrees.

The BA program in enterprise leadership is for students who want to develop essential leadership skills necessary for navigating and succeeding in a variety of complex organizational settings, from small businesses to large corporations and from nonprofits to government entities. This innovative program focuses on real-world challenges and problem-solving, equipping students with the tools to inspire, motivate and guide teams toward common goals. Students gain a deep understanding of organizational dynamics, strategic thinking and ethical decision-making, preparing them for impactful careers across various sectors. The curriculum combines theoretical knowledge with practical application, ensuring graduates are well-prepared to lead with integrity and vision in a rapidly changing global landscape. This program is ideal for aspiring leaders who are passionate about making a difference and driving positive change within their organizations and communities.

Concentration name: ['Conservation Biology and Ecology', 'International Development and Sustainability', 'Sustainable and Renewable Resources']
description:
The BS program in environmental and resource management provides students with a science-based curriculum focused on the management of natural resources, including water, land, plants and wildlife. Students learn principles of ecosystem resilience, and they learn how to apply those principles to the management of natural resources in a changing world.

The curriculum is interdisciplinary in nature. Students take courses in chemistry, biology, physics and math as a foundation for a core of classes in environmental and resource management that prepares them for careers in which they are tasked with finding solutions to complex environmental challenges. Students also have considerable flexibility in selecting their upper-division science electives, which allows them to design a more specialized curriculum based on their interests and career goals.

Graduates with a BS in environmental and resource management are well-prepared for a variety of careers in the environmental consulting industry as well as with local, state and federal government agencies responsible for the stewardship of natural resources. They are also well-prepared for graduate studies in a variety of related fields, including ecology, conservation biology, hydrology, resource management and environmental science.

The BS program in environmental chemistry provides students a strong background in chemistry that is tailored to understanding and solving environmental problems at the molecular level. Graduates are prepared for careers in a wide range of fields, including:

environmental consulting
environmental law
environmental regulations and compliance
hazardous waste management
industrial hygiene
pollution control and remediation
public health
water purification

The bachelor's degree program in environmental design and construction provides the skills and knowledge needed to pursue a variety of careers related to building and landscape construction, materials, methods and management, as well as those careers in the area of historic preservation. Students graduate from the program with a Bachelor of Science degree. The environmental design and construction program is composed of two concentrations: construction management and historic preservation.

The BSE program in environmental engineering focuses on the scientific and engineering principles needed to protect and clean the environment. Students learn to apply their knowledge of the natural sciences (chemistry, biology, physics) and mathematics to design and operate pollution control and resource recovery systems. The coursework provides a strong foundation in the concepts of fluid mechanics, and water and wastewater treatment, as well as air pollution control, solid and hazardous waste management, and environmental systems modeling. The program provides the technical competence and professional skills to prepare students for a career in environmental engineering. Graduates are prepared for professional practice or for advanced studies. Environmental engineers are involved in a variety of activities that can directly impact public health and the environment. Opportunities for environmental engineers include working in industry, for consulting firms, or in government agencies. The undergraduate program in environmental engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.
Accreditation status: The undergraduate program in environmental engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

Concentration name: ['Conservation Biology and Ecology', 'Environmental Chemistry', 'Environmental Engineering', 'Environmental Policy and Management', 'Geological Sciences', 'Sustainable Food Systems', 'Sustainable Horticulture', 'Water, Climate and Energy']
description:
The environmental science BS program provides students with a strong foundation in the sciences to understand environmental problems and the skills to generate solutions. It is designed to develop a generation of leaders to address critical challenges in the environment, including climate change, biodiversity loss and ecosystem degradation, and pollution. The curriculum combines a foundation in natural and social sciences with extensive hands-on experience in the field and laboratory and with data analysis to provide students the skills and knowledge needed for a successful career in the environmental sector.

Students in the program also develop strong written and oral communication skills, as well as problem-solving and critical thinking skills.

Graduates are prepared for a variety of careers in consulting, governmental agencies and nongovernmental organizations. The degree program also prepares students for graduate studies in environmental science or a related discipline.

The BS program in family and human development explores the dynamic and complex nature of human development across the life span within the context of families, communities and society. This program gives students the tools to improve the lives of children, youth and adults with an interdisciplinary approach that combines coursework in psychology, sociology, physiology and education. Through a variety of class formats and out-of-the-classroom learning experiences, students apply what they have learned to hands-on settings in the community. Students learn how to create and implement evidence-based programs in human services agencies and educational settings.

The BA program in fashion is a transdisciplinary program that provides a foundation for students to work in many roles in the global fashion industry, from design and merchandising to marketing and management. The program is housed in the Herberger Institute for Design and the Arts, with strong connections to the W. P. Carey School of Business and the Walter Cronkite School of Journalism and Mass Communication.

This forward-thinking, industry-facing degree program focuses on creative exploration and professional practice, emphasizing the development of an entrepreneurial mindset. Students learn the fundamentals of design thinking, fashion history, materials and technology, and business principles.

Within this flexible curriculum, students pursue a concentration in either fashion design or fashion merchandising.

The concentration in fashion design prepares students for positions in the areas of creative and technical design within the fashion industry.

The concentration in fashion merchandising prepares students for positions within the areas of fashion marketing, journalism, public relations, event management and merchandising.

The curriculum is enhanced by a required internship, study abroad opportunities and student-run ventures, including a student fashion blog, a retail venture and an annual fashion show. The program is committed to developing well-rounded, creative professionals who can adapt to the rapidly evolving global fashion industry.

The BA program in film with a concentration in film and media production offers students a broad, liberal arts-based course of study in the cinematic arts. Students are provided the opportunity to study film from a variety of perspectives, including theory, history and practice. The curriculum develops students' creative and critical skills, allowing them to pursue careers as independent filmmakers, work in a variety of roles on film and media productions, or find film-related jobs in areas such as cinematic arts management, film programming, and film and media archiving and preservation.

Students in this program are not required to complete a second language.

Students pursuing this degree will be enrolled in the film and media production concentration, which is housed at the Tempe campus and provides students with a solid foundation of production courses along with the flexibility to pursue an internship, minor or second major of their choice.

The BA program in film with a concentration in filmmaking practices is an interdisciplinary degree that gives students a broad understanding of the art, craft and business of filmmaking. The curriculum helps students develop the critical and creative skills to produce compelling media content for a range of platforms and venues.

In this program, students are immersed in a hands-on production environment from their first year. They gain proficiency in all aspects of filmmaking, from preproduction to post-production, including:

- directing
- producing
- screenwriting
- cinematography
- editing
- sound
- production design
- visual effects

Students have the opportunity to make a variety of media projects, including narrative and documentary shorts, commercials, and web series. The school has a state-of-the-art production facility, with editing suites, sound mixing rooms, and a sound stage. Students also have access to a wide range of professional equipment, including industry-standard cameras, lighting and sound gear.

The program is part of the Sidney Poitier New American Film School, which is dedicated to training the next generation of diverse film artists and industry leaders. The school is committed to creating a more inclusive and equitable film industry, and its curriculum reflects this commitment. Students learn about the history and theory of film, with a focus on underrepresented voices and perspectives.

Students have opportunities to network with industry professionals through guest lectures, workshops and internships.

The film and media studies program offers a Bachelor of Arts degree that focuses on the history, theory and criticism of film, television and new media. It is an academic, not a production, program.

Students are encouraged to develop a critical understanding of film and media from various historical, cultural and theoretical perspectives. They work with a faculty of national and international standing, and they have opportunities for internships in the film industry and various other media-related institutions.

The curriculum offers a liberal arts education that prepares graduates for a wide range of career opportunities. Graduates are well prepared for careers in film and media criticism, the film industry, arts administration and education as well as for graduate study in film and media.

The BS program in finance provides students with the knowledge and skills necessary to work in a variety of finance-related fields.

The curriculum is designed to familiarize students with the institutions, theory and practice of finance. The program provides an understanding of how financial markets and institutions work, how to value and use a variety of financial instruments, and how to assess and manage risk in a variety of settings. Students learn how to analyze financial information and make sound financial decisions that create value.

Students may also complete a certificate in financial planning.

The Department of Finance has strong ties to the local and national business community. Finance faculty members are nationally and internationally recognized for their research. The department provides students with many opportunities to interact with finance professionals. Many student organizations, including the Financial Management Association and the Student Investment Management Fund, bring prominent professionals to campus to speak with students.
Accreditation status: The W. P. Carey School of Business is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB International).

description:
The Bachelor of Science in financial planning provides students with the necessary knowledge and skills to assist individuals and families with a variety of financial needs, including investment selection, retirement and estate planning, and risk management.

Graduates of the financial planning program find career opportunities in the fast-growing industry of personal financial services. The BS program in financial planning is a CFP Board-registered program. Graduates are eligible to sit for the national Certified Financial Planner™ certification examination. The program combines rigorous financial planning coursework with an applied learning component. Students gain hands-on experience by volunteering in the community to deliver financial literacy workshops and by working in paid and unpaid internships with financial services firms. In addition, students have opportunities to participate in professional development activities, to meet industry professionals and to network.
Accreditation status: The BS program in financial planning is a CFP Board-registered program.

description:
The BS program in food and nutrition entrepreneurship is a unique business-focused nutrition program designed to prepare students for careers that create innovative, evidence-based solutions for health.

Students learn about food, nutrition, business, communication and leadership. They gain essential knowledge and skills that will enable them to contribute to new and existing businesses in the rapidly growing health and wellness industry. In addition to a comprehensive science-based nutrition curriculum, students develop business acumen by learning about finance, marketing, management and entrepreneurship.

The curriculum prepares students for employment in a variety of settings, such as food industry, health care, health and wellness companies, government agencies, entrepreneurial enterprises and nonprofit organizations.

The BS program in food and nutritional sciences is for students who wish to apply basic food and nutritional sciences to careers in the food industry or in community or public health nutrition.

The food science curriculum provides a strong foundation in food chemistry, food microbiology, food engineering and food processing. Students gain a deeper understanding of current food processing techniques, food safety and quality control.

The nutrition curriculum provides a strong foundation in human nutrition. Students learn about the physiological needs for nutrients throughout the life span and how to plan diets and community programs to meet these needs.

The program can prepare students for a variety of professional schools, including:

dental school
medical school
nursing school
optometry school
pharmacy school
physical therapy school
physician assistant programs

This program does not include all courses required for dietetics registration.

The BS program in forensic science provides a strong foundation in the sciences with extensive laboratory experience. This degree program meets the educational requirements for the FBI's specialized scientific positions.

The curriculum is based on the recommendations of the Technical Working Group for Education and Training in Forensic Science and is designed around a strong science core (chemistry, biology, physics and mathematics) to provide students with a solid foundation in the sciences along with specialized forensic science coursework in the junior and senior years.

Students have opportunities to participate in hands-on learning through laboratory-based courses and internships in working forensic science laboratories. An internship provides a culminating experience in which a student is placed in a crime laboratory or other forensic science setting to gain valuable, real-world experience.

The School of Mathematical and Natural Sciences has strong relationships with local, state and federal crime laboratories, including the Phoenix Police Department Crime Laboratory, the Arizona Department of Public Safety Crime Laboratory system, the Maricopa County Medical Examiner's Office and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives.

The forensic science curriculum includes a diverse range of topics, including crime scene investigation, forensic chemistry, forensic biology (DNA), physical evidence (firearms, prints), quality assurance and the law.

Forensic science graduates find employment in a variety of settings, including federal, state and local crime laboratories; law enforcement agencies; and medical examiner offices. Some graduates go on to medical or law school.

The BA program in French provides students with a high level of proficiency in the French language and a strong knowledge of the literatures and cultures of France and the French-speaking world.

The program offers a solid foundation for students planning to pursue careers in a variety of fields, including education, translation, interpretation, business, tourism, diplomacy, international development, national security, foreign service and social work, as well as for those wishing to enter graduate programs in French or related fields.

The curriculum offers a variety of courses in French language, literature, culture and linguistics. Through these courses, students acquire and develop sophisticated abilities in oral and written expression, including critical thinking, textual analysis and research skills.

The Bachelor of Arts in general studies is a degree completion program for students with at least 60 semester hours of transferable college credit or an associate degree from a regionally accredited institution. It is recommended that transfer students have an ASU GPA of 2.00 or higher and a transfer GPA of 2.50 or higher.

The general studies program provides students with the opportunity to design a program of study that meets their unique educational and career goals. Students choose three of 11 available subject area concentrations to create a customized program of study in consultation with an academic advisor.

Students interested in the general studies program should meet with a College of Integrative Sciences and Arts academic advisor to create a plan of study.

The general studies program is designed for students who have a variety of interests and who seek a broad, interdisciplinary education. The program is flexible and allows students to explore different fields of study while developing critical thinking, communication and problem-solving skills. Upon graduation, students are well-prepared for a variety of careers in fields such as business, education, government and nonprofit organizations.

Students must complete all ASU general studies requirements, including the first-year composition requirement.

The subject areas from which a student may select are:
communication
history
leadership
personal health
political science
psychology
social justice
social welfare
sociology
U.S. and global diversity
U.S. history

The Bachelor of Science degree program in geography with a concentration in meteorology-climatology is for students interested in a wide range of atmospheric science careers, including weather forecasting and broadcast meteorology.

The School of Geographical Sciences and Urban Planning is home to the most advanced meteorology-climatology program in the Arizona-New Mexico-West Texas region and offers unique learning opportunities for students.

The meteorology-climatology concentration curriculum meets all the American Meteorological Society and National Weather Service recommendations for an undergraduate degree in atmospheric science. Many graduates are employed by the National Weather Service, the U.S. military or private forecasting companies, while others go on to top graduate programs around the country.

The program has three main areas of focus:

Climatology: Students study topics including the physical causes of climate, how climate varies over space and time, and the role of climate in human affairs. A variety of research tools are used in this field, from satellite data to state-of-the-art climate models. Students explore issues such as global warming, urban climate, drought and climate change.

Meteorology: Students delve into atmospheric dynamics and thermodynamics with the goal of understanding and forecasting weather. Coursework gives them direct experience with satellite and radar data, weather maps and numerical weather prediction models. Many students pursue broadcast meteorology, gaining experience through an internship program with a local Phoenix television station.

Extreme weather: Students examine events such as thunderstorms, tornadoes, hurricanes and floods to better understand their physical causes and their effects on humans. In addition to coursework, students can get involved in research through the school's Severe Weather Research Group.

Geographers study the Earth's landscapes, peoples, places and environments. It is, quite simply, about the world in which we live. Geographers are keenly aware of the space around us and how it is organized and changed over time. They bring a unique spatial perspective to social, environmental and physical sciences, offering a holistic view of the world.

Students in the geography BA program are able to focus their studies in areas of their interest. Some examples of these areas include:

urban studies
population geography
cultural geography
political geography
globalization
economic geography

The curriculum's flexibility allows students to also pursue a minor or a second major.

Because geographers must have a broad understanding of the world, they take courses in a variety of related fields. This major has a strong interdisciplinary focus that prepares students for careers in both the public and private sectors, including in urban planning, real estate, community development, tourism and marketing.

The degree is excellent preparation for continued graduate studies in geography as well as in other fields, such as urban planning and law.

This program allows students to develop an understanding of major concepts, theoretical perspectives and historical trends in human and physical geography.

The Bachelor of Science in geography is an interdisciplinary social science degree that allows students to focus on areas of human and environmental geography.

Geographers seek to understand complex social and environmental issues from a spatial perspective. They analyze the arrangement of people and their activities on Earth's surface and their relationships, their use of and impact upon the human and physical environment, and their patterns of movement.

Students in this program will be equipped with the necessary knowledge and skills to describe, analyze and explain the arrangement of the Earth's physical and human features and the processes and interrelationships that create them. The program is flexible to allow students to specialize on a particular theme or region.

The German bachelor's degree program helps students build a strong foundation of skills in the German language, with an emphasis on practical application, whether for use in business, government, research or other professions.

Students achieve proficiency in the German language and develop a sophisticated knowledge of German culture through coursework that promotes intellectual growth and the development of analytical and critical thinking skills. The core curriculum focuses on language, literature, culture, linguistics and phonetics. Students practice and develop their language skills through compositions, oral presentations, conversation and class discussions in German.

The curriculum gives students the ability to customize their degree program by choosing from an expansive list of electives related to German literature, film and cultural history. All students complete a senior capstone project in their final semester that incorporates the knowledge and skills they have cultivated as German majors.

The BS program in global agribusiness prepares students for management and leadership positions in the food and agriculture industries, which encompass a wide array of enterprises, from production agriculture to food manufacturing, distribution and retailing. Students develop strong analytical and business skills and learn how to apply them in a socially responsible way on a global scale. The program draws on faculty expertise in agribusiness and is enhanced by the resources of the W. P. Carey School of Business and other ASU academic units. Core areas of study include: agricultural marketing, finance, management, food systems, economics, international development, policy and business analytics. The program trains students in business and economic analysis, providing a strong foundation for understanding and managing complex challenges faced in a globalized food system.
Accreditation status: Business (BUS) accredited by AACSB International.

description:
The Bachelor of Arts in global health is a holistic, transdisciplinary program that provides a unique opportunity for undergraduate students to learn about the complexities of global health problems and to build the skills necessary to address these challenges.

The program combines a natural sciences-based curriculum in human health and disease with social science coursework that explores the cultural, economic, historical and political factors that shape health patterns and policies around the globe.

The global health major has a strong emphasis on research and prepares students to become future leaders in a variety of global health-related careers, including global public health, medicine and other health professions, international development and resource management.

The BS program in global logistics management provides students with a high-quality education in the areas of logistics, supply chain management, and operations management. The program is designed to provide students with a solid foundation and understanding of the role of logistics in the global economy.

Students in global logistics management develop the skills necessary to manage and move goods and services within a business and between businesses anywhere in the world. The curriculum provides a broad understanding of the business environment as well as an in-depth understanding of the critical importance of globally integrated supply chain management.
Accreditation status: The W. P. Carey School of Business is accredited by AACSB International, the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business. AACSB accreditation is the oldest and most recognized in the world, and it is the benchmark of quality for business education.

description:
The Bachelor of Global Management program from the Thunderbird School of Global Management at ASU prepares students with the essential hard and soft skills they need to lead and succeed in the Fourth Industrial Revolution. The innovative BGM curriculum combines cross-cultural studies, regional expertise, and a liberal arts core with a cutting-edge education in global business, technology and management. Students learn from world-class faculty members with extensive experience in international business and leadership. The program teaches in-demand skills such as adaptability, critical thinking, cross-cultural communication, data analytics, global citizenship, global mindset and problem-solving.

This program is available for first-time, first-year students.

Students learn to navigate the complexities of global business in a curriculum that includes courses from across the university as well as specialized Thunderbird courses on topics like communicating in global teams, global accounting, global leadership, and states and governance in a globalized world.

There is no foreign language proficiency requirement for admission; however, all students are required to achieve intermediate-level proficiency in a second language to graduate. Thunderbird offers professional language instruction in a variety of languages.

Through a required global experience, such as a semester-long study abroad program or an international internship, students can apply their knowledge in a real-world setting, further developing their cross-cultural communication and leadership skills.

With more than 45,000 graduates in more than 140 nations, Thunderbird's alumni network is a powerful resource for graduates throughout their careers. Graduates are prepared for leadership roles in a variety of sectors, including business, government, and nonprofits, and are equipped to make a positive impact on the world by creating sustainable prosperity worldwide.
Accreditation status: The Bachelor of Global Management program is accredited by the Higher Learning Commission.

Concentration name: Economic Development, Global Business, Global Health, Global Management, Governance and Conflict, Human Rights, International Relations, Migration, Refugees and Displaced Persons, Sustainable Development
description: The Bachelor of Arts in global studies is an interdisciplinary program that prepares students for the challenges of living and working in a globalized world. Students learn to analyze complex global issues from a variety of perspectives, drawing upon the methods and theories of the social sciences and humanities. The program is flexible, allowing students to combine the study of global studies with another major or to select from one of nine concentrations. Students who pursue the concentration are required to have an international experience. Global studies graduates are prepared for employment as global professionals in a variety of fields.

The bachelor's degree program in graphic design provides a foundation in visual communication principles, theory and history in order to prepare students for a changing industry. Students work in a professional, collaborative and interdisciplinary design environment.

The curriculum is focused on a rigorous design process that culminates in developing a comprehensive portfolio. Students are prepared to enter a rapidly changing field, work in a variety of settings and collaborate on teams with other design professionals.

The program values design thinking, craft, technology, community engagement and collaboration. Students will:
- explore typography, visual communication, image making and publication design
- develop user interface and user experience design
- investigate branding and information design
- create a final portfolio and capstone project
Accreditation status: The graphic design program is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Art and Design.

Concentration name: ['Animation', 'Commercial Photography and Video', 'Full-Stack Web Development', 'Internet and Web Development', 'Printing and Publishing', 'User Experience']
description:
The Bachelor of Science in graphic information technology program provides students with a creative, technological and managerial understanding of the graphic information industry.
The GIT program at ASU is a comprehensive, contemporary, hands-on and project-based learning program that focuses on creating visual content for multi-channel distribution, including print, web, photo, video and animation.
Students are encouraged to develop their own unique interests within the broader field of graphic information technology by concentrating in one of the specialty areas below. They become highly sought after for their specific skill sets as well as their general knowledge and versatility in the field.
Graduates of the GIT program are not only skilled designers and technologists but they also possess strong skills in project management, teamwork and communication and a comprehensive understanding of business operations. They are true leaders and innovators in the field of visual design and technology.

The health care administration and policy major prepares students to manage the business and policy side of health care, including hospitals, health insurance companies, pharmaceutical companies, government agencies and public health organizations.

The program curriculum is composed of courses from across ASU, including those offered by the College of Health Solutions; the W. P. Carey School of Business; the School of Public Affairs; the Hugh Downs School of Human Communication; and The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences.

Students in the program have opportunities to pursue an accelerated degree program, research and honors theses, and internships.

The health care administration and policy degree program provides the foundational knowledge needed to pursue graduate and professional school opportunities in health care administration and health care policy or to enter directly into the workforce upon graduation.
Program name: Health Care Administration and Policy, BS

description:
The health care compliance and regulations bachelor's degree program prepares students to work as compliance specialists in various health care settings, including hospitals, clinics, long-term care facilities, insurance companies, and government agencies.

Students learn how to interpret and apply complex federal and state laws and regulations in real-world situations, investigate potential violations, and develop and implement compliance plans.

The coursework for the health care compliance and regulations degree is developed and delivered by expert faculty and covers the fundamental areas of compliance, such as privacy and security, billing and coding, and quality of care. Students learn the tools and techniques needed to audit and monitor compliance programs and how to respond to government investigations.

Graduates of this program may go on to careers as compliance analysts, managers, officers or specialists, or in roles related to health care privacy and security, medical coding and billing, or revenue integrity. The skills learned in this program may also provide a foundation for those interested in pursuing a law degree or other graduate-level studies.
Program name: Health Care Compliance and Regulations, BS

description: The health care coordination bachelor's degree program prepares students to work as part of an interprofessional health care team. The curriculum is focused on health care coordination within a population health framework. Students gain foundational knowledge in social determinants of health and the role of value-based care in achieving the Quadruple Aim. They will learn strategies to help patients navigate the complex health care system, access community resources and improve health outcomes. Graduates are equipped with the foundational knowledge and functional skills to be effective health care coordinators and patient navigators in primary care, hospital and community health settings. Coursework covers topics in interprofessional collaboration, leadership, patient-centered communication, health information technology and health care financing.

The BS program in health education and health promotion prepares students for careers as health education specialists in a wide variety of settings, including governmental public health agencies, nonprofit community health organizations, hospitals and medical care organizations, and corporate wellness programs.

The curriculum is aligned with the areas of responsibility for health education specialists as identified by the National Commission for Health Education Credentialing. The program emphasizes an ecological approach to health, focusing on the social and environmental determinants of health and health behavior. Students acquire the knowledge and skills necessary to assess health education needs; plan, implement and evaluate health education programs; and advocate for health-enhancing policies and environments. The program also provides excellent preparation for graduate studies in public health and other health professions.

Graduates are eligible to sit for the national certified health education specialist exam. Upon passing the exam, graduates receive the CHES credential.

Upon graduation, students are prepared to work in a variety of health settings.
Program name: Health Education and Health Promotion, BS

description:
The BS program in health entrepreneurship and innovation is designed to prepare students to be leaders and innovators in a rapidly changing health care landscape. This transdisciplinary program focuses on entrepreneurship and innovation within the health sector, not as a business program but as a way of thinking and problem-solving to create value.

Students learn how to identify opportunities in health care to create valuable solutions for individuals and populations. The curriculum helps students think critically and creatively to solve complex problems and identify solutions for real-world health and health care challenges. They learn how to use an entrepreneurial mindset and systems-level thinking to become a change agent in health care.

The BS program in health sciences with a concentration in healthy lifestyles and fitness science provides a strong foundation in evidence-based principles of lifetime wellness, physical activity and fitness. The degree program emphasizes the knowledge and skills necessary for those interested in healthy lifestyles and fitness careers, including those that lead to national certifications by organizations such as the National Academy of Sports Medicine and the National Strength and Conditioning Association. The curriculum provides a strong foundation for students who want to continue their studies in graduate and professional programs.

The concentration in healthy lifestyles and fitness science prepares students for a variety of careers in fitness, wellness, health education and promotion and other health-related fields.

The program is offered by the College of Health Solutions. Students can complete this degree program at ASU's Downtown Phoenix campus or through ASU Online.
Program name: Health Sciences (Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science), BS

description:
The BS program in health sciences provides students with a strong foundation in health-related coursework to prepare them for a variety of roles in health care and for entry into graduate-level clinical programs.

Students in the BS program in health sciences focus on health-related topics, including:

anatomy and physiology
biology
chemistry
medical terminology
nutrition
pharmacology
physics
psychology

This major is also available in a concentration in healthy lifestyles and fitness science.

Through this comprehensive curriculum, students develop the skills and knowledge needed to excel in their chosen health care field.

The BS program in healthy lifestyles and fitness science prepares students to be leaders and innovators in the burgeoning fields of corporate wellness, public health, health coaching, personal training, and strength and conditioning. The program's core coursework provides a strong science foundation with an emphasis on evidence-based principles. This prepares students for careers in the health and fitness industry, helps them prepare to apply for graduate programs in health and for nationally recognized certifications.

The rigorous science-based curriculum for the healthy lifestyles and fitness science program is founded on the exercise science and health-related content areas of anatomy, biomechanics, exercise physiology, health promotion, lifestyle behavior change, nutrition, and research and statistics.

Students have opportunities for hands-on, experiential learning in the core classes, in a broad selection of elective courses and through a required internship. This combination of required coursework, electives and internship experiences offers students the opportunity to learn, practice and demonstrate competencies and professional skills in all areas of healthy lifestyles and fitness science.
Program name: Healthy Lifestyles and Fitness Science, BS

Concentration name: Global History, History of the Americas, Public History, U.S. History
description:
The Bachelor of Arts in history is one of the most versatile degrees a student can earn, with a curriculum that provides a broad, comprehensive knowledge of the past and a method for organizing and interpreting human experience. In courses, students are exposed to the historical experiences of people from many different cultures in different time periods.

Students learn how to:
- evaluate evidence
- interpret and weigh sources of information
- organize information in a coherent way
- think critically
- write clearly

The curriculum is designed to help students think historically and gain a better understanding of the global community in which they live. The research, analytical and writing skills that are part of a history major's training provide excellent preparation for a wide variety of careers in business, public service, education and law, and can help students more fully engage in their communities and understand the challenges and opportunities of the 21st century.

The BA program in the history of science, ideas and innovation is for students who are fascinated by science, technology and medicine and want to study them from a humanistic perspective. This major is perfect for students who love both the sciences and the humanities and are seeking a course of study that integrates the two.

This history of science degree program combines rigorous training in historical methods with a deep dive into the history of science, technology and medicine and their interactions with culture, politics and the arts. Students learn how to analyze primary historical sources, evaluate arguments in historical scholarship, and craft their own evidence-based arguments about the past. They also learn how to communicate effectively about science, technology and medicine with diverse audiences.

This degree program prepares students for a wide range of careers, from law, medicine, public policy and science journalism to business, education and archival or museum work. Students learn how to ask complex questions about the world and how to find answers by drawing on a diverse range of evidence. Graduates are nimble thinkers, excellent communicators and creative problem-solvers, all qualities in high demand in the contemporary job market.
Program name: History of Science, Ideas and Innovation, BA

description:
The BA program in hospitality provides students with knowledge, skills and abilities in the business of hospitality. Students learn how to manage the various aspects of businesses in the hospitality industry, such as lodging, restaurants, tourism, meetings and events.

Students are prepared to manage the business side of hospitality, with coursework that includes financial management, human resource management and strategic management in addition to core hospitality operations courses.

Students complete an internship near the end of their program, which provides them with paid, real-world experience. Many students find full-time jobs at the successful conclusion of their internship.

The hospitality BA program is offered by the School of Community Resources and Development.

The BS program in housing and community development provides students with a broad and inclusive understanding of the political, economic and social issues associated with community and economic development. The curriculum familiarizes students with the literature, theory, law, policy and practice of community development. Students learn a wide range of analytical skills in order to identify and effectively address the opportunities and challenges present in rural, urban and suburban communities.

The curriculum is designed to teach students how to:

analyze data for evidence-based decision-making
collect data using a variety of methodological approaches
conduct community assessments
design programs
identify stakeholders
manage nonprofit organizations
write grants and conduct fundraising

Students also have the opportunity to take advanced coursework in an area of concentration such as community health, economic development or housing.

The Bachelor of Arts in human resources and employment law provides students with a strong foundation in human resources, employment law, policy, leadership and management. Students study business concepts, leadership, the legal system and the policies that shape today's work environment. The program equips students with marketable skills in communication, management, analysis and problem-solving, along with a deep understanding of human resources and its complex legal framework.

The human resources field is a key component of every organization, business and corporation, and knowledge of human resources and employment law provides a distinct career advantage. This interdisciplinary program prepares students to meet the needs of today's changing work environment as they pursue graduate school and careers in human resources and employment law.
Program name: Human Resources and Employment Law, BA

description:
The BS program in human systems engineering focuses on the analysis, design, and evaluation of systems in which humans and technology interact. Students learn to apply the theories of human performance and the principles of psychology, along with the methodologies of engineering, systems analysis and design, in order to create safe, effective and satisfying human-centered systems and technologies.

The field applies to a wide range of industries, including aviation, aerospace, health care, product design, information technology, transportation and defense.
Accreditation status: The BS program in human systems engineering is accredited by the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society.

description:
The bachelor's degree program in industrial design at ASU provides students with a solid foundation in the fundamental principles and skills of design, with a strong emphasis on hands-on making, creative problem-solving and an understanding of human needs.

The industrial design program focuses on the design of manufactured objects, and students gain a comprehensive understanding of the entire design process, from ideation and concept development to prototyping and production. Through a series of studio-based courses, they learn a wide range of design techniques, including sketching, 3D modeling and digital fabrication. They also develop an understanding of materials, manufacturing processes and user-centered design principles.

In addition to studio courses, students take a variety of lecture and seminar courses that provide a broad understanding of the historical, cultural and theoretical contexts of design. They also have the opportunity to participate in a variety of extracurricular activities, such as design competitions, workshops and study abroad programs.

The industrial design program prepares students for a variety of careers in the design industry, including product design, furniture design, toy design, and exhibition design. Graduates have gone on to work for some of the world's leading design firms and companies.

The BSE program in industrial engineering is focused on the design, improvement and installation of integrated systems of people, materials, information, equipment and energy. The curriculum is based on specialized knowledge and skills in the mathematical, physical and social sciences together with the principles and methods of engineering analysis and design to specify, predict and evaluate the results to be obtained from such systems.

Coursework emphasizes the application of engineering methods to the analysis and design of service systems, but the principles are also applicable to production and manufacturing environments. Students learn how to analyze and design systems that provide services to people, such as health care, transportation, banking and government. They develop an understanding of operations research, human factors and ergonomics, production and service logistics, quality engineering, and integrated information systems.

This BSE program is a participating program in the Western Undergraduate Exchange (WUE) program. The WUE program is not available to online students.
Accreditation status: The industrial engineering BSE program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

description:
The BS program in informatics uniquely combines information technology with social and behavioral sciences. Students learn to harness information technology for human benefit while studying the social context in which it operates.

The curriculum is composed of a solid technical foundation, including programming, databases, networking and web design, along with a firm understanding of the social sciences. The program emphasizes user-centered design and a deep understanding of the way people use and interact with information systems.

The software development concentration focuses on the design, development and evolution of complex software systems. Students learn the basic principles of object-oriented design and development and gain experience with a wide range of state-of-the-art tools and technologies, including Java, C++, Python, MySQL, JavaScript, HTML, CSS and various mobile application development platforms.

The BS program in information technology prepares students for a variety of careers in information technology. The curriculum is focused on a breadth of knowledge in the information technology field and includes a general education component along with an information technology core. The information technology core provides students with a solid foundation in programming, networking, databases, web technologies, computer hardware, operating systems and cybersecurity.

The program prepares students for positions such as: application developer, computer and information security professional, computer network architect, computer support specialist, computer systems analyst, database administrator, IT consultant, network and computer systems administrator, software developer, web administrator, web developer. Graduates possess a strong background in problem-solving in the information technology profession and are well prepared to advance their knowledge through lifelong learning.
Accreditation status: The information technology, BS program at the Polytechnic campus is accredited by the Computing Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

description:
The BA program in innovation in society explores innovation and its social contexts and impacts from a variety of perspectives. Students learn to analyze social, ethical and policy issues surrounding emerging technologies and other innovations; lead in creating more just, sustainable futures; and engage with diverse communities to solve complex problems and create public value. Graduates are prepared for a variety of careers in the private, public and nonprofit sectors.

The curriculum is transdisciplinary, drawing on insights from the social sciences, humanities, engineering and the natural sciences. Students gain knowledge in areas such as science and technology policy, public engagement, ethics, leadership, and communication and social change. They develop skills in analysis, creativity and communication, and they apply their knowledge and skills in real-world contexts through hands-on, team-based projects in the classroom and the community.

The core courses provide an introduction to innovation and society, a set of analytic tools and theories for understanding innovation in its social context, and a project-based capstone experience. All students complete an internship, which allows them to explore professional pathways while making a tangible impact in the community. Students work closely with faculty mentors to design an individualized course of study that aligns with their personal and professional interests.

The Bachelor of Science in innovation in society prepares students to be leaders who can help shape the future for the betterment of humanity. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in interdisciplinary social sciences and real-world engagement to empower students to develop innovative solutions for the complex challenges of our time.

Students learn a variety of problem-solving skills, including foresight and anticipatory governance, responsible innovation and public engagement. This transdisciplinary degree allows students to complement their core innovation in society courses with a variety of electives from across the university, allowing them to tailor the program to their individual interests and career goals.

The curriculum culminates in a capstone experience through which students apply what they've learned to a real-world project. Students who complete this degree are well prepared for careers in a wide range of fields, including sustainability, policy analysis, education and social entrepreneurship.

The integrative health Bachelor of Science program provides students with the educational foundation needed to flourish in a variety of health care settings or to pursue graduate studies. The program is specifically designed to provide students with a holistic view of health and wellness that blends conventional medicine with evidence-based complementary approaches.

The curriculum for the integrative health degree explores the art and science of health and healing for the whole person --- mind, body and spirit. Students learn a wide range of therapies that work in conjunction with conventional Western medicine.

The program helps students develop the critical thinking skills needed to assess the credibility of evidence for or against the use of various therapies. Students also gain a better understanding of the cultural context of health and healing and of the legal and ethical issues related to the use of complementary health care.

The integrative social science bachelor's degree program is a unique interdisciplinary studies program that offers the tools to understand and analyze human behavior and social structures through a variety of lenses. Students explore issues such as social and economic inequality, crime, globalization, race and ethnicity, and family dynamics, learning to apply a range of theoretical and methodological approaches to their inquiry.
The degree program combines a strong core in research methods with the flexibility of interdisciplinary coursework, which prepares students for graduate school and for careers in fields that demand critical and analytical skills, such as policy analysis, human resources, law and public service. The coursework is designed to help students sharpen their critical thinking and writing skills while they broaden their understanding of society and social issues.
The faculty includes nationally and internationally recognized scholars in a wide range of social sciences. These faculty members bring their expertise and insights into the classroom, offering students a vibrant and challenging intellectual environment in which to explore the complexities of the social world.

The Bachelor of Arts in interdisciplinary arts and performance is a practice-based, transdisciplinary degree that provides students with opportunities to engage in a wide variety of collaborative, creative, experimental and socially engaged practices.

Students in this innovative program learn to integrate a spectrum of artistic disciplines, including:

art
dance
music
sound
theatre and performance

Students also develop an understanding of arts and design in a variety of social contexts and communities and are provided with the critical and creative skills to develop their unique interests and artistic voices. The program emphasizes collaboration, process and emergence, and students work closely with faculty to design and create original works, performances and projects that extend beyond the classroom into the surrounding community.

The degree program prepares students for a variety of futures as artists, designers and creative professionals. Students may also pair this degree with other disciplines in order to develop unique skill sets and approaches for future careers.

This interdisciplinary arts and sciences bachelor's degree program from the College of Integrative Sciences and Arts at ASU's Polytechnic campus allows students to design a plan of study based on their personal interests and career goals. Students choose two subject areas to concentrate on from a broad range of options available on the Polytechnic campus and through ASU Online. The options are grouped into seven clusters: art and design, communication and media, cultural studies, exploratory, social sciences, sustainability, and technological innovation.

The core courses in the major are taught using an integrative approach, focusing on theories and methods from the humanities, social sciences and natural sciences. The courses build skills employers seek in areas such as evidence-based inquiry and analysis, critical thinking, creative thinking, problem-solving, teamwork and collaboration, and written and oral communication.

The curriculum culminates in an applied project or internship and portfolio in which students are able to articulate their personal and professional growth and showcase the skills learned in the major. The major also is available through ASU Online.

The Bachelor of Arts in interdisciplinary studies with a concentration in organizational studies is a degree program for students who want to build on a chosen subject area with an interdisciplinary course of study focused on how organizations function.

The organizational studies concentration provides a theoretical framework for understanding organizations and the contexts in which they operate. The curriculum prepares students for a range of leadership and administrative positions in business, government and nonprofit organizations. Coursework combines perspectives from social sciences, humanities, and applied and professional fields to prepare students for the challenges of a rapidly changing, increasingly global work environment.

Students select two subject areas from an approved list of more than 150 subjects. They combine 18 credit hours of upper-division coursework in each area with 9 credit hours of core courses to complete the 45 credit hour major.

The BA program in interdisciplinary studies helps students create an individualized, academically sound program of study to meet their specific educational and career goals. Students in the program take the lead in designing their own cross-disciplinary course of study. They choose two concentration areas from the more than 350 undergraduate majors, minors and certificate programs offered at ASU. Interdisciplinary studies students are intellectual trailblazers who combine their passions and interests to forge a new path of learning. They see connections others don't, and they are not afraid to learn in different ways. With the help of an academic advisor, students in this program select courses that are most relevant to their goals, and they learn to articulate the value of their unique academic background to others, including future employers and graduate schools. Students should contact the College of Integrative Sciences and Arts at the Downtown Phoenix, Polytechnic, Tempe or West campus for further information about the BIS program.

The BSD program in interior design at The Design School is highly ranked in the U.S. and focuses on design excellence, innovation and interdisciplinary collaboration. Interior design is a multifaceted profession in which creative and technical solutions are applied within a structure to achieve a built interior environment.

The curriculum emphasizes research and analysis to enhance the function and quality of interior spaces for residential and commercial design, including corporate, health care, hospitality and retail design. These solutions are functional, enhance the quality of life and culture of the occupants, and are aesthetically attractive.

Designs are created in response to and coordinated with the building shell and acknowledge the physical location and social context of the project. Designs must adhere to code and regulatory requirements and encourage the principles of environmental sustainability.

The interior design process follows a systematic and coordinated methodology, including research, analysis and integration of knowledge into the creative process, whereby the needs and resources of the client are satisfied to produce an interior space that fulfills the project goals. Interior design includes a scope of services performed by a professional design practitioner, qualified by means of education, experience and examination, to protect and enhance the health, life safety and welfare of the public.

Interior design students gain a broad foundation in design history, theory and technical skills. They also have the opportunity to participate in domestic and international travel programs, interdisciplinary research and design projects, faculty-led student organizations and community service.
Accreditation status: The interior design program is accredited by the Council for Interior Design Accreditation, https://www.accredit-id.org/, 206 Grandville Avenue, Suite 350, Grand Rapids, MI 49503.

description: The BA program in international letters and cultures with a concentration in Arabic studies offers comprehensive language training and a solid background in the culture and civilization of the Arabic-speaking world. The program aims to create global citizens who are knowledgeable about the Arab world and its significant cultural, intellectual and political contributions to the world. The curriculum allows students to explore the diverse and rich cultural heritage of the Arab world, from classical to modern times, through the study of literature, culture, and intellectual and political history. The school works to make the ASU Tempe campus a hub of intellectual and cultural activities related to the study of the Arab world, the Middle East and the larger Muslim world. The school's faculty members in Arabic are all native or near-native speakers with doctoral degrees from leading universities in North America and years of experience teaching Arabic as a foreign language. The Arabic program in the School of International Letters and Cultures is a vibrant and fast-growing academic unit that promotes a humanistic approach to the study of language and culture. Students can participate in study abroad programs in various countries in the Middle East as a way of enhancing their linguistic proficiency and deepening their cultural understanding of the Arab world.
Program name: International Letters and Cultures (Arabic Studies), BA

description:
The Bachelor of Arts program in international letters and cultures with a concentration in Asian studies offers an integrated course of study in the languages and cultures of Asia, with an emphasis on China or Japan. Students gain a foundation in an Asian language and its cultural and literary traditions. Coursework includes both broad surveys and specialized topics in English as well as advanced training in the selected language.

The program includes three areas of focus:
- Chinese language and culture
- Japanese language and culture
- a general Asian studies track that allows for the study of multiple areas

Through a diverse range of courses, students explore the rich traditions of Asia while developing their proficiency in an Asian language. The flexible curriculum is designed to help students reach their specific academic and career goals. Students benefit from the expertise of the faculty in the School of International Letters and Cultures who are committed to providing a comprehensive education in the languages and cultures of this large and diverse continent.
Program name: International Letters and Cultures (Asian Studies), BA

description: The Bachelor of Arts in international letters and cultures with a concentration in classical studies offers students the opportunity to learn about the ancient Greek and Roman worlds. In this program, students study the languages, literature and cultures of ancient Greece and Rome and their impact on later cultures and on the development of Western civilization. Students also have the opportunity to study the material culture of the ancient world through classics courses in art history and archaeology. The classical studies concentration is inherently interdisciplinary and provides an excellent foundation for a variety of careers by helping students develop valuable skills in critical thinking and analysis as well as in oral and written expression. This program is available as an accelerated degree program.
Program name: International Letters and Cultures (Classical Studies), BA

description:
The Bachelor of Arts in international letters and cultures with a concentration in classics provides students with a broad and deep understanding of the language, literature and culture of the classical world (ancient Greece and Rome), helping them gain a better understanding of the global community of the 21st century. The study of classics can reveal much about our own world and the assumptions and values of our own culture through comparison with another.

Students in the classics concentration must choose between one of two tracks: classical languages or classical studies. The classical languages track is for those who wish to focus their studies on the languages of Greek and Latin. The classical studies track does not require students to study Greek or Latin, but offers a wider range of courses in classical civilization, literature and culture.

All students can explore subjects ranging from classical literature and mythology to philosophy, art, archaeology, history, and social and religious life. Students can also participate in study abroad programs that visit and explore important sites from the classical world, programs that enrich their understanding and appreciation of other cultures and the global context.

Beyond the classroom, students can participate in campus organizations such as the classics club, Eta Sigma Phi (the classics honor society), and the Central Arizona Society of the Archaeological Institute of America.

A BA in international letters and cultures with a concentration in classics prepares students to become global citizens who are able to think critically, communicate clearly and understand other cultures. These skills are valuable to a wide variety of employers.

The Bachelor of Arts in international letters and cultures with a concentration in French offers a comprehensive and in-depth study of the French language and the cultures of France and the Francophone world. Students study French language at all levels, from beginning to advanced, and can begin their language study at the level appropriate to their previous experience.

The program provides a solid foundation in French and Francophone literatures, cultures and linguistics.

The program offers many opportunities for students to study abroad and encourages them to participate in faculty-led summer programs in France, Quebec and other Francophone regions and in semester or yearlong exchange programs at universities in France and elsewhere in the French-speaking world.

A French major provides a gateway to a variety of careers in business, education, government, the hospitality industry, international relations, nonprofit organizations, publishing and technology, and the concentration prepares students for graduate studies in French and a variety of other fields.

The Bachelor of Arts in international letters and cultures with a concentration in German provides a deep understanding of German language, literature, culture and film, preparing students for an ever more connected and multilingual world. The program is specifically designed to educate global citizens who are prepared for the challenges of a new century and who have an understanding of other cultures. Students also study the complex relationship of the United States to other countries and cultures.
Students in this program can study, intern and research abroad in Germany, Austria and Switzerland. Students also may opt for a dual-major path and obtain a degree in German and another discipline, such as business or biology, to enhance their career opportunities. An accelerated master's degree is also an option for qualified students.
In addition to the B.A., the school offers an undergraduate certificate in German.
The school's study abroad programs are among the best in the nation, providing students with the opportunity to develop a deeper understanding of language and culture. Students can participate in faculty-directed summer programs or, for a more immersive experience, semester or yearlong programs.
The School of International Letters and Cultures is a place for leaders, for risk-takers and for those who are passionate about the future of the planet and its people. This is where language study and cultural awareness enable the tangible, positive changes that the world needs.

The bachelor's degree program in international letters and cultures with a concentration in Italian provides students with an in-depth knowledge of Italian language, literature and culture, while at the same time giving them the tools to analyze and discuss them in a critical fashion.

The major offers a wide spectrum of courses that go well beyond the typical modern language curriculum. Students can take a variety of courses in English that span from the Middle Ages to the 21st century and cover topics as diverse as Dante, cinema, food culture, Italian American studies and fashion. Advanced students can also take a range of classes taught in Italian, from language to literature and culture.

All students are encouraged to participate in one of the many study abroad opportunities offered by the program and the university.
