A major in Italian develops the necessary skills for a variety of careers in fields such as business, communication, education, government, law, media, public service and technology. It also provides the foundation necessary for those students who plan to continue their studies in graduate school.

The Bachelor of Arts in international letters and cultures with a concentration in Japanese offers comprehensive training in Japanese language and culture, allowing students to develop advanced linguistic proficiency while gaining in-depth knowledge of Japanese literature, culture, history and society.

The program provides the cultural and linguistic expertise necessary for students to excel in various careers, including international business, translation and interpreting, tourism, journalism, government, foreign service, and teaching English in Japan.

The Bachelor of Arts in international letters and cultures with a concentration in Romanian provides a comprehensive education in Romanian culture as a whole, focusing on its connections to European, Balkan and global cultures.

Students learn about the geography, literature, culture and art of Romania in a curriculum emphasizing critical thinking as well as linguistic and cultural proficiency. They gain the background necessary for pursuing careers in a wide range of fields, including education, tourism, international business and government service.

The international letters and cultures bachelor's degree program with a concentration in Russian offers students comprehensive training in the Russian language, as well as in-depth knowledge of the culture, literature, history, politics and intellectual traditions of Russia and the Russophone world.

Russian is an official language of the United Nations and one of the most widely spoken languages in the world. The language is an important medium for global communications in the fields of science, technology and world affairs.

The program offers a sequence of courses at all levels, from beginning to advanced Russian. Through a variety of required courses and electives, students gain a strong command of the language, develop sophisticated analytical and critical skills, and build a solid foundation in Russian studies.

In addition to in-depth studies in culture and literature, students also may choose to complement their major with courses from other fields and disciplines, such as:

business
communication
global health
global studies
history
Jewish studies
justice studies
political science
religious studies
sustainability

Students are strongly encouraged to complement their studies with an internship or a study abroad experience in a Russian-speaking country.

The bachelor's degree program in international letters and cultures with a concentration in Spanish provides students with a solid foundation for understanding the Spanish language and Hispanic cultures, as well as a broad humanistic perspective.

The program is oriented toward the development of advanced language proficiency and an understanding of the diverse social and cultural contexts in which the Spanish language is spoken. Students engage with a wide range of fields, including:

cultural studies
film studies
history
languages for the professions
linguistics
literature

The curriculum gives students the ability to communicate in Spanish orally and in writing with a high level of proficiency and to understand and analyze a wide variety of texts from Spain and Latin America. In this environment, students develop skills in cross-cultural understanding and communication.

Students in this program may not minoring in Spanish.

The curriculum is designed for students who have an interest in foreign language, literature and culture and a desire to better understand the Hispanic world.

The BS program in international public health is designed to meet the increasing demand for culturally competent public health professionals who can effectively address global health challenges. This program provides students with a solid foundation in the principles of public health, epidemiology, biostatistics and health promotion, while also incorporating a unique emphasis on international health issues, cross-cultural communication and global health policy. Students in this program develop the knowledge and skills necessary to design, implement and evaluate public health interventions in diverse international settings. They explore topics such as infectious diseases, maternal and child health, nutrition, environmental health and health disparities from a global perspective. Graduates of the program are well-prepared for careers in international health organizations, nongovernmental organizations, government agencies and the private sector, where they can make a meaningful impact on the health and well-being of populations around the world.
Accreditation status: The BS program in public health is accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health.

description:
The BS program in international trade provides a strong foundation in international business and economics, along with advanced coursework in international trade relations, international finance, regional economic issues and the cultural aspects of international business.

Students in the BS program in international trade select an emphasis in one of four languages: Chinese, German, Japanese or Spanish. Students must complete a series of advanced courses in their chosen language. An international experience is also required.

Through a combination of business, economics, foreign language and area studies coursework, graduates are prepared for a variety of international careers. Graduates possess both the qualitative and quantitative skills necessary to compete for jobs with multinational corporations, international banks, government agencies and a wide variety of other organizations involved in international trade and finance.

This program offers a strong liberal arts education combined with professional training in economics and international business. This well-rounded background provides an excellent foundation for professional careers in the global economy and for graduate study in fields such as business, law, economics and international affairs.
Accreditation status: All W. P. Carey School of Business programs are accredited by AACSB International.

description: The BA program in Italian provides students with a solid foundation in the Italian language and an in-depth knowledge of Italian literature and culture, from the Middle Ages to the present day. Students achieve an advanced level of linguistic competency through a range of language and culture courses and refine their critical understanding of Italy's cultural and literary history by working closely with a variety of primary texts and cultural artifacts. Graduates are prepared to use their language skills and cultural knowledge in a range of professions, including education, international relations and business, as well as for admission to graduate programs in Italian studies and related fields.

The BA program in Japanese provides students with a solid foundation in Japanese language, literature and culture. It emphasizes proficiency in the Japanese language and a broad understanding of Japanese culture in both its traditional and contemporary forms.

Courses cover Japanese language, literature, culture, linguistics and film. Students study the four essential skills of language learning (speaking, listening, reading and writing) in modern Japanese at all levels of instruction.

The program in Japanese provides excellent preparation for a variety of careers in business, education and government.

The Bachelor of Arts in Jewish studies is an interdisciplinary degree program for students interested in studying the long and diverse history, religion, literature, languages and culture of the Jewish people.

In addition to a core curriculum covering a broad range of subjects, students have the opportunity to focus on areas of Jewish studies that they find especially compelling.

Students have the opportunity to hone their skills as readers, writers and thinkers. The program helps them acquire a sophisticated global perspective and the knowledge and skills necessary to serve as educated citizens and to go on to an advanced degree program or a career in the private or public sector.

In addition to courses on Jewish history, religion and culture, students take two years of Hebrew language, as part of the degree's core requirements. They also have the option to take more advanced modern or biblical Hebrew, or introductory Yiddish or another language of the Jewish diaspora, to fulfill their foreign language requirement.

Courses in Jewish studies are taught by faculty specialists from a wide variety of academic disciplines, including history, religious studies, English, German and Jewish studies. Faculty members have strong ties with other programs, centers and schools at ASU, such as the Center for the Study of Religion and Conflict, the Melikian Center for Russian, Eurasian and East European Studies, and the School of Historical, Philosophical and Religious Studies.

The BA program in journalism and mass communication provides students with the broad-based liberal arts education and professional skills necessary to succeed in today's media professions. The program is committed to the values of accuracy, fairness and diversity.

Students learn how to report and write for print, broadcast and online media. They learn how to produce news and information on multiple platforms, from mobile to social to broadcast to web. They learn the professional and ethical principles of journalism, the role of journalism in a democracy, and the importance of a free press.

Students may specialize in print journalism, broadcast journalism or public relations. They also may choose to explore other areas of interest, such as sports journalism, business journalism or digital media.
Accreditation status: The journalism and mass communication program is accredited by the Accrediting Council on Education in Journalism and Mass Communications, one of 113 such programs in the United States and the only one in Arizona.

description:
The Bachelor of Science degree in justice studies examines the meanings of justice and injustice in political, economic, social and cultural contexts. The BS degree emphasizes skills that are increasingly in demand in a variety of public and private justice-related professions. These skills include ethical reasoning, quantitative and qualitative data analysis, and oral and written communication skills.

Students learn a social science approach to the study of justice and take courses that emphasize research and analytical skills and that have policy relevance. They also develop the skills for a critical understanding of how justice is denied or realized. This course of study is particularly valuable for students interested in law school, graduate school or research positions in justice fields.

Justice studies graduates have an understanding of the challenges and opportunities for achieving justice and an ability to critically assess complex problems and communicate potential solutions.

The BS program in kinesiology prepares students for a variety of careers in health- and fitness-related fields as well as for entry into graduate programs in kinesiology and professional programs such as physical therapy, occupational therapy, physician assistant, medicine and chiropractic. Kinesiology is the study of human movement and students in the program learn about anatomy, physiology, biomechanics, exercise physiology and motor control as they relate to human health and performance. Kinesiology majors enjoy a rigorous curriculum that provides an outstanding foundation of knowledge and skills.

Students can work directly with faculty in a variety of research opportunities ranging from clinical populations to elite athletes. Students learn in state-of-the-art research and teaching laboratories, including those focused on biomechanics, motor control and learning, exercise physiology and body composition.

In the final semester, students can choose to participate in an internship with one of our numerous affiliated companies and organizations in the Valley, state and nation. These experiences often lead directly to offers of employment after graduation.

Students who earn a degree in kinesiology are well prepared to pursue any of a number of graduate degrees, including athletic training, clinical exercise physiology, exercise and wellness, physical education, physical therapy and strength and conditioning. In addition, many of our graduates successfully go on to medical school and physician assistant programs.

The BSLA in landscape architecture is a professional degree program that focuses on public life and the art and science of designing the built environment. Landscape architecture encompasses the analysis, planning, design, management and stewardship of the natural and built environments. The program emphasizes urban landscape design through the study of social, cultural and environmental issues in the arid Southwest.

The curriculum is centered on a sequence of design studios that increase in complexity, from garden design to urban design. Students also learn hand and digital drawing, landscape history and theory, plant materials and ecology, and construction technologies. The Phoenix metropolitan area serves as an urban laboratory for the program, and students have opportunities to collaborate with students and faculty in architecture, industrial design, interior design and visual communication design as well as with students in other ASU programs, including sustainability, urban planning and construction management.

This program is accredited by the Landscape Architectural Accreditation Board.
Accreditation status: This program is accredited by the Landscape Architectural Accreditation Board.

description:
The BA program in languages and cultures with a concentration in classics offers students the opportunity to learn about the history, literature and cultures of ancient Greece and Rome. Students develop proficiency in ancient Greek or Latin (or both) and gain in-depth knowledge of the classical world and the rich traditions of classical thought and expression.

In studying classics, students acquire important intellectual skills --- critical thinking and reading, sound argumentation, and clear and persuasive writing --- that provide an excellent basis for a variety of careers.

The School of International Letters and Cultures is a place for leaders, and students can take advantage of a variety of award-winning study abroad programs and research opportunities that allow them to explore and find their place in the world.

Recent graduates of this program have pursued careers as educators, editors and museum curators or have continued their education with graduate studies in a variety of fields, such as archaeology, art history and law.

The Bachelor of Arts in Latin American studies is a multidisciplinary program in which students are provided the opportunity to study a broad range of subjects related to Latin America and develop an in-depth, interdisciplinary understanding of the region.

The curriculum is designed for students who desire to learn about the society, history, languages and culture of this region and for those who wish to pursue a career involving the Latin American region. Students also have an opportunity for advanced language training in Spanish or Portuguese, and they are encouraged to study abroad in Latin America.

The program offers an honors track with a thesis option for students interested in developing the research, writing and analytical skills needed for graduate school. The program's internship program provides students hands-on professional experiences in fields like social justice, immigration advocacy, international business, health care, community development and sustainability.

The BA program in leadership and management prepares students for careers in leadership and management in the public, private and nonprofit sectors. The core of this innovative degree program consists of five thematic areas:

communication
finance
leadership and management
research and methods
sector and community

The core curriculum provides students with a breadth of knowledge and skills necessary for effective leadership in the 21st century. Through the choice of electives and concentration courses, students develop deeper knowledge and skills in an area related to their specific career interests.

Students learn the necessary skills for a successful career in a variety of public, private and nonprofit settings through hands-on practice, including service-learning and internships and a senior capstone project in which they work in a professional setting and present a portfolio of their learning to the community.

What can I do with a degree in leadership and management?

Graduates of this program may find positions that require skills in a variety of areas, such as leadership, program management, community development and financial management. Graduates may be prepared for careers such as:

community outreach specialist
corporate trainer
human resources specialist
management consultant
operations manager
program coordinator
public administrator

The Bachelor of Science in leadership in military and aerospace is an applied degree program in which students receive credit for formal military and aerospace training and experience and apply it toward a bachelor's degree. Students also study the fundamentals of leadership and choose from a variety of interdisciplinary options related to their specific academic and professional goals.

This applied science degree is best suited for students who already possess a significant number of credits from military and aerospace training programs that have been evaluated for college credit by the American Council on Education.

Students select an area of interdisciplinary study related to their unique interests and career aspirations. Available study areas include business, communication, engineering management, project management and public policy, among many others.

The degree is ideal for students with an interest in leadership roles in the civilian and military sectors.
Program name: Leadership in Military and Aerospace, BS

description:
The BA program in liberal studies is an interdisciplinary program designed for students who have a wide range of interests and who are seeking a broad liberal arts education. It provides students with a general education in the arts, humanities, natural sciences and social sciences.

The liberal studies major is a flexible degree program for students who have a variety of interests and who want to become well-rounded, interdisciplinary thinkers. The degree program offers a broad-based education in the humanities, social sciences, and natural sciences with the opportunity for students to tailor coursework to meet their individual interests and goals.

Students learn how to think critically and analytically, communicate effectively, develop intellectual curiosity and creativity, appreciate diversity, and understand the historical context of contemporary life. Students apply their interdisciplinary knowledge to social issues through engagement with the community.

Linguistics is the scientific study of human language. Linguistics majors explore the formal properties of language (sound systems, words, sentences, meaning), how children and adults learn language, and how language is used in society, including its relationship to culture, politics, and identity.

The curriculum gives students a solid foundation in the core areas of linguistics and the flexibility to pursue their own interests by choosing from a variety of electives offered within the Department of English and related fields such as anthropology, communication, computer science, philosophy and psychology.

In this program, students develop sought-after skills in communication, analysis and problem-solving.

A BA in linguistics opens doors to employment in business, government, technology and education, and it provides excellent preparation for graduate studies in linguistics and related fields.

The BS program in management provides students with a broad and comprehensive background of cutting-edge management knowledge and skills. Students gain a solid understanding of the key functions of management and the essential role that managers play in all types of organizations. The curriculum addresses the skills and knowledge needed to successfully manage organizations in a changing, global and diverse environment. Specific topics include leadership, human resource management, team management, organizational strategy, behavior and change, international management, business ethics, and entrepreneurship. Students also gain experience in applying their knowledge to solve real-world problems and develop practical managerial skills through various applied learning projects and activities.
Accreditation status: The W. P. Carey School of Business is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB International).

description:
The marketing program with a concentration in digital and integrated marketing communications helps students build skills to effectively reach consumers in the global marketplace. The concentration prepares students to work for organizations that need to adapt to an increasingly complex and dynamic environment. The curriculum is designed to educate students on the latest digital marketing trends, strategies and tactics being used by today's leading brands. The curriculum has a data-driven focus with in-depth training on the latest platforms, marketing technology and analytical techniques being used to drive business results. The integrated marketing communications perspective ensures students learn how to strategically integrate various communication tactics and channels to effectively reach target audiences.

Students gain specialized expertise in digital and integrated marketing communications and a broad foundation in general business, along with flexibility in their senior year to choose electives in an area of interest. Topics of study include:

advertising management
analytics
content marketing
digital marketing
marketing communications
public relations
search engine optimization
social media
In addition to classes, students are able to participate in professional development and leadership opportunities through student organizations such as the American Marketing Association, the professional business fraternity Alpha Kappa Psi, and DECA, a collegiate organization preparing emerging leaders and entrepreneurs.

The W. P. Carey School of Business has a dedicated undergraduate career center to assist students with their internship and career search. Graduates are prepared for a variety of marketing positions across industries, including:

advertising agencies
brand management
digital marketing
health care
marketing analytics
marketing research
professional sales
public relations
retail management
sports marketing
technology
This program is available for students in the W. P. Carey School of Business. Students should refer to the W. P. Carey School of Business website for admission standards for this program.

To learn more about the school, students should visit the W. P. Carey School of Business website.

This program provides a strong academic foundation in business and a focused expertise in digital and integrated marketing communications and the general marketing core.
Accreditation status: The W. P. Carey School of Business is accredited by AACSB International, the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.
Program name: Marketing (Digital and Integrated Marketing Communications), BS

description: The BS program in marketing with a concentration in professional sales provides a premier curriculum and platform to prepare students for a successful career in sales. Students develop strong foundations in sales and marketing principles and gain critical insights into the best practices to build and maintain strong customer relationships. They learn the process of creating, communicating and delivering offerings that have value for customers, clients, partners and society at large. Coursework from top-ranked faculty in the Department of Marketing, along with hands-on, real-world experience via internships and other opportunities, gives students the skills and confidence to create, communicate and deliver value to customers in any business setting.
Accreditation status: The W. P. Carey School of Business is accredited by AACSB International, the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.

description:
The BS program in marketing provides students with a broad foundation of marketing knowledge that prepares them for success in the dynamic, competitive and global world of business.

The marketing curriculum emphasizes practical, real-world business applications that develop the essential knowledge and skills needed for a variety of marketing positions. The coursework helps students develop specific career-related skills and abilities, particularly in advertising and promotion, data analytics, global marketing, professional selling and retailing.

Through the study of consumer behavior, marketing research and marketing strategy, students learn how to create, communicate and deliver value to customers in a variety of settings. Students apply what they learn through case analysis, problem-solving, real-world business projects and simulations. This approach enables them to transition seamlessly from the university to a variety of exciting and rewarding marketing careers.
Accreditation status: The W. P. Carey School of Business is accredited by AACSB International, the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.

description:
The BSE program in materials science and engineering is focused on the relationships between material structure and properties for all classes of materials, including biomaterials, electronic materials, metals, polymers and ceramics.

Students learn how to select and create materials for a variety of applications and to predict the performance and failure of engineering materials. The program emphasizes hands-on laboratory experience using modern materials processing and characterization equipment in courses and undergraduate research. Small class sizes in upper-division courses create a personalized learning experience and an excellent atmosphere for student-faculty interaction.

Students may also be interested in the accelerated 4+1 bachelor's and master's degree program that allows them to obtain both a bachelor's degree and a master's degree in as few as five years.
Accreditation status: The materials science and engineering, BSE program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

description:
The BS degree program in mathematics with a concentration in actuarial science is for students interested in the profession of actuary. An actuary is a business professional who uses mathematical and statistical methods to manage financial risk. Actuaries have been consistently rated as holding one of the best jobs in the United States.

The actuarial profession is a challenging and rewarding career, and the actuarial science program at ASU is designed to prepare students for the first several professional examinations that must be passed in order to become an actuary.

The Society of Actuaries has approved the curriculum for this ASU program to meet the Validation by Educational Experience requirements for economics, corporate finance and applied statistical methods. Students can earn VEE credit from the SOA by achieving a grade of B- or better in approved ASU courses.

In addition to the strong mathematical and statistical background required by the profession, students receive a solid foundation in business by taking several courses in accounting, economics and finance. Students gain hands-on experience by completing a required internship or research experience.
Accreditation status: The undergraduate and graduate programs in the School of Mathematical and Statistical Sciences are not accredited.

description:
The BA program in mathematics with a concentration in mathematics education is for students who are interested in becoming mathematics teachers in a middle school or high school. The program, offered by The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences, provides a strong background in mathematics and in the art and science of teaching. Through coursework in the School of Mathematical and Statistical Sciences and in Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College, students build a deep understanding of the mathematics they will teach. Through focused coursework and structured, extended experiences in middle school and high school classrooms, students build the specialized knowledge, skills and dispositions necessary for teaching mathematics effectively to diverse learners.

Students who complete this degree are recommended for certification by the Arizona Department of Education to teach mathematics in middle school and high school (grades 6-12). To be recommended for certification, students are required to pass the appropriate secondary subject knowledge and professional knowledge exams of the Arizona Educator Proficiency Assessments.

The BS program in mathematics with a concentration in secondary education, offered by the School of Mathematical and Statistical Sciences, is an interdisciplinary program with the Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College. It is designed for students who want to combine a love of mathematics with the desire to teach and share that love with others.

Students gain a deep understanding of mathematics and of the connections between the different branches of mathematics. This includes geometry, algebra, trigonometry, calculus, and statistics, as described in the high school curriculum standards of the National Council of Teachers of Mathematics and the Arizona Department of Education. The degree program includes all the coursework needed to recommend a student for certification to teach mathematics in grades 6-12 in Arizona.

The program meets the requirements of the National Council of Teachers of Mathematics for the preparation of secondary mathematics teachers.
Accreditation status: The Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College is accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation.

description:
The BS program in mathematics with a concentration in statistics provides a solid foundation in statistics in addition to a general background in mathematics. The curriculum includes a yearlong sequence in mathematical statistics, a course in regression analysis and a course in the design of experiments. These core courses provide students with the necessary background for a professional career in statistics or for graduate study in the field.

Students learn to:
- apply critical thinking skills to analyze and solve problems using statistical methods.
- conduct and analyze case studies.
- make and evaluate statistical arguments.
- use statistical software.

The Bachelor of Arts in mathematics is for students who want to combine a strong background in mathematics with a second area of concentration. Students pursuing the BA degree in mathematics often use this degree to prepare for a career in a mathematics-related field.

A student with a strong mathematics background and a concentration in a second area such as statistics, business, economics or computer science has an advantage in today's technologically oriented job market. For instance, students interested in careers in actuarial science usually major in actuarial science, but a major in mathematics can also be a good path to that career, particularly if the second area of concentration is in finance or economics.

Students who want to become teachers of mathematics in grades 7-12 usually complete the BS degree program in mathematics with a concentration in secondary education.

The Bachelor of Science in mathematics provides a strong foundation in the traditional areas of mathematics as well as an introduction to new and emerging fields.

The core of the BS program gives students a solid background in calculus, linear algebra and differential equations. This is complemented by upper-division courses in analysis, algebra and applied mathematics, allowing students a great deal of choice in planning a program that is best suited for their interests and career goals.

Students who complete the program are well prepared for careers that require strong analytical and problem-solving skills, and for graduate school in mathematics, statistics and other related fields.

Mechanical engineering is a broad discipline that applies the principles of engineering, physics and materials science for the design, analysis, manufacturing and maintenance of mechanical systems. Mechanical engineers possess a high degree of skill in mathematics and the physical sciences, with an emphasis on forces, motion and energy.

The mechanical engineering program provides a broad foundation of knowledge in the thermal and fluid sciences, solid mechanics, manufacturing and system dynamics and control, as well as opportunities for more specialized education in a variety of areas.

The computational mechanics concentration is designed for students with a strong aptitude for mathematics and an interest in using the power of modern computers to analyze and design complex mechanical systems. Computational mechanics blends traditional mechanical engineering with computer science and applied mathematics. Career opportunities are plentiful in areas such as aerospace, automotive, electronics and heavy equipment design and manufacturing.

Graduates of the mechanical engineering program are prepared for a variety of careers in industry, government and academia.
Accreditation status: The mechanical engineering (computational mechanics), BSE program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org. Student enrollment and graduation data are available at engineering.asu.edu/enrollment.

description:
The Bachelor of Science in Engineering program in mechanical engineering with a concentration in energy and environment provides a solid foundation in mechanical engineering principles, with special emphasis placed on energy systems and the environment.

Students in the energy and environment concentration develop the expertise needed to design and develop new technologies for energy generation and transfer and for environmental protection.

Examples of study areas include:

- Alternative energy technologies, including fuel cells and solar energy
- Energy efficiency and conservation
- Energy generation and conversion systems
- Environmental protection and remediation technologies, including pollution control systems for power plants and vehicles
- Fossil fuels
- Green building design
- Heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) systems
- Renewable energy
- Sustainable energy and environmental system design

The program includes instruction in basic sciences and a strong curriculum in engineering academics and design. Coursework in the major includes topics in thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, heat transfer, solid mechanics and machine design.

In the senior year, students have the option to pursue an accelerated 4+1 program, which allows them to earn a BSE and a master's degree in five years.
Accreditation status: The BSE program in mechanical engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org. Student enrollment and graduation data are available at engineering.asu.edu/enrollment.

Concentration name: Computational Mechanics, Energy and Environment, Robotics
description:
Mechanical engineering is one of the broadest engineering disciplines, providing a wide range of career choices. Mechanical engineers have a hand in designing and manufacturing everything from a new generation of vehicles to the latest medical devices. Through their skills and knowledge, they create and develop new products and technologies that improve health, the environment and the quality of people's lives.

The mechanical engineering program is designed to provide students with a broad education emphasizing the fundamentals of mechanical engineering. It also provides an excellent background for a wide variety of careers in industry, government and academia. Students learn to apply the principles of motion, energy and force to design, develop and manufacture devices and systems for the benefit of humankind. They learn about dynamics, engineering materials, fluid mechanics, heat transfer, machine design, solid mechanics and thermodynamics. In addition to gaining an understanding of these engineering fundamentals, students also benefit from the hands-on experience they gain through laboratory and design courses.

The undergraduate program is offered on campus and online. The undergraduate curriculum provides a strong foundation for professional practice or for graduate study in mechanical and aerospace engineering or a related field, such as biomedical or environmental engineering. The curriculum provides a strong background in science and mathematics, along with general education coursework.
Accreditation status: The mechanical engineering BSE program at the Tempe campus is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org. Student enrollment and graduation data are available at https://engineering.asu.edu/enrollment.

description:
The BS program in media arts and sciences is an interdisciplinary program that gives students the tools to create, design and develop new media experiences. Students learn in a project-based environment that combines art, design, computer science and engineering through the School of Arts, Media and Engineering, a collaboration between the Herberger Institute for Design and the Arts and the Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering.

The program is at the forefront of the information revolution, which has changed the way people communicate, get information, and learn. Students learn how to integrate physical computing, creative coding, and emerging technologies into experiential systems, learning systems, and computational media systems.

The program's hands-on, project-based learning model and interdisciplinary courses prepare students for many emerging careers involving coding, design and systems thinking. The program also prepares them for careers in established fields, such as web design and development, visual effects, game design and development, and creating interactive and educational media experiences for a variety of users.

Medical laboratory scientists are health care professionals who use their expertise to perform complex laboratory tests on patient samples. They use sophisticated biomedical instruments, technologies and methods to analyze blood, body fluids and tissues to provide critical information for the detection, diagnosis and treatment of disease.

The medical laboratory science program offers a professional curriculum in an accelerated format to provide a comprehensive education in the major disciplines of medical laboratory science. Students gain the necessary competencies to perform and interpret laboratory tests, to explain the clinical significance of laboratory test results, to manage laboratory operations and to maintain quality control.

Students complete three years of pre-professional coursework and then apply to the professional program for the final year. The professional program starts each May and consists of three semesters of professional coursework and clinical rotations at an affiliated clinical laboratory.

Upon completion of the program, students are eligible to take a national certification exam. Graduates find employment in a variety of settings, including hospital and reference laboratories, research and pharmaceutical laboratories, fertility clinics, and public health laboratories.
Accreditation status: The Medical Laboratory Science, BS program is accredited by the National Accrediting Agency for Clinical Laboratory Sciences.

description:
The Bachelor of Science in medical studies prepares students for careers in the health care field. Students build a strong foundation in medical sciences and develop an understanding of the social and behavioral aspects of health and health care.

The flexible curriculum provides students with a strong pre-health core and the ability to choose from a wide variety of medical- and health-related electives and other courses, allowing them to tailor the degree to their own career aspirations.

It is an excellent choice for students interested in pursuing graduate or professional health programs including medicine, dentistry, optometry, pharmacy, physical therapy and physician assistant studies.

Students in the medical studies program can benefit from the College of Health Solutions' extensive network of clinical partners, which provides opportunities to gain real-world experience.

Students may be eligible for an accelerated 4+1 program in which they can earn a BS in medical studies and an MS in the science of health care delivery in just five years.

The Bachelor of Science in microbiology program provides students with a strong foundation in the microbial sciences and prepares them for a wide range of careers in science and health. The curriculum is comprehensive and modern, including courses in general microbiology, immunology, microbial genetics, microbial physiology, virology, pathogenic bacteriology, microbial ecology and microbial diversity. The program has a strong laboratory emphasis, providing students with the skills required to be successful in the workforce. Students in this major can choose the medical microbiology concentration. The program provides excellent preparation for graduate study in microbiology and related fields as well as for admission to professional schools in medicine, dentistry, optometry, pharmacy and other health-related professions.

The Bachelor of Science in military studies provides students with a multidisciplinary educational experience to develop a well-rounded understanding of the roles of militaries and armed conflict in society and international affairs. Students gain skills in interdisciplinary research and analysis to support career fields in the armed forces, national security, homeland security, veteran services and the defense industry.

The curriculum provides a unique balance of coursework on leadership, strategy and tactics and history, along with technology, intelligence, cybersecurity and international security. Students gain a historical foundation and practical insights to enhance their understanding of the relationship between militaries, governments and societies. They also have an opportunity for advanced analysis of military operations in a complex global environment.

The military studies program is designed for students seeking to pursue a military commission upon graduation, but it is open to all students, including military veterans and family members. It may also appeal to students who are looking for careers in national security and the defense industry. The program provides the necessary flexibility to incorporate Air Force, Army and Navy ROTC course requirements within the major.

The Bachelor of Science in molecular biosciences and biotechnology is a unique, interdisciplinary program offered by the School of Molecular Sciences and The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences. The program focuses on the science and technology of the new revolution in molecular life sciences. Modern biosciences is a quantitative science grounded in chemistry, physics and mathematics, and it is revolutionizing the detection, treatment and prevention of disease. The degree program prepares students for careers in the growing and dynamic fields of biotechnology, medicine and other health professions.

The curriculum blends a strong scientific foundation in the molecular sciences (chemistry, biology, physics) with course work on the application of this knowledge. Hands-on experience is an essential part of the curriculum, with laboratory courses starting in the first year and culminating in a required research experience. A distinctive aspect of the program is the opportunity for students to join one of the many research groups that make ASU a national leader in life science research. Areas of research include mechanisms of disease, drug discovery, diagnostics and biomarkers, bioenergy, biomaterials, protein structure and function, and evolution. In their final two years, students have the opportunity to focus on either medicine or biotechnology through a flexible set of upper-division electives.

Students who are considering this degree program are encouraged to pursue four years of high school mathematics and a year each of biology, chemistry and physics.

The BA program in music with a concentration in music and movement is designed to train student musicians with an emphasis on embodied music making and somatic education. The program explores a range of movement practices and develops proficiency in movement skills. This concentration prepares students for a variety of careers including as private studio teachers and arts organization staff, as well as for further training in fields such as dance, physical therapy, yoga and other somatic practices.
The music and movement curriculum includes:
a core of music courses, such as theory, aural perception and music history
group and private instruction in the student's primary performance medium
instruction in movement and somatic practices
The Herberger Institute for Design and the Arts at Arizona State University is home to the ASU School of Music, Dance and Theatre, which has a long history of excellence and is a stimulating center of creativity and discovery. The school offers students a wide variety of experiences and hands-on learning opportunities with a diverse roster of faculty who are nationally and internationally recognized in their fields. Students interact with professionals in the Phoenix metropolitan area and across the world through a rich schedule of residencies, workshops and master classes.
Accreditation status: The music programs are accredited by the National Association of Schools of Music.

description:
The popular music program in the ASU School of Music, Dance and Theatre is a unique and innovative program for students who want to study the art of popular music and its place in today's culture.

The curriculum is designed to create an environment where students can realize their full potential and be equipped to enter a wide variety of music professions. Students learn to sing and play in a wide variety of popular music styles, to create original music, and to use the tools of music technology and music business and entrepreneurship to forge a unique pathway to a successful career in music.

The popular music program is led by an outstanding faculty of experienced and dedicated teachers who are also active and accomplished performers, songwriters, producers and engineers. Students are accepted into the program through a competitive audition process.
Accreditation status: The School of Music, Dance and Theatre is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music.

Concentration name: Choral Music Education, Instrumental Music Education, General Music Education
description:
The Bachelor of Music in music learning and teaching prepares students for careers as music educators in K-12 schools and for advanced study. The curriculum leads to Arizona teacher certification.

This program offers three concentrations: choral, instrumental and general music education. Students learn to effectively teach music to children and adolescents in a variety of contexts, including school-based programs, private studios and community music schools. Students learn from faculty members who are nationally and internationally recognized in their fields. Students hone their musicianship and teaching skills in a community of learners who are passionate about the potential of music to transform lives.

The School of Music, Dance and Theatre provides a stimulating artistic and academic environment with an impressive calendar of concerts, recitals, productions, master classes and guest artist presentations.

Students in the music learning and teaching program are eligible to enroll in a special 4+1 program in which they can earn a BM in music learning and teaching and an MM in music learning and teaching in five years. The program's combination of an undergraduate degree and a master's degree enables students to gain a competitive edge in the job market and to command a higher starting salary.
Accreditation status: The School of Music, Dance and Theatre is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Music; the National Association of Schools of Dance; and the National Association of Schools of Theatre. The dance program is also an accredited institutional member of the American Dance Therapy Association.

description: The BA program in music in the Herberger Institute for Design and the Arts at Arizona State University provides a broad foundation in music combined with a liberal arts curriculum. The program has a focus on music studies and scholarship, such as music history, ethnomusicology, music theory and music analysis. The program also provides a music core of ensemble participation, keyboard skills and private lessons. Students can select from a wide range of academic electives both within music and across the university to complement the required curriculum. The BA program in music is well-suited to the student who wishes to combine a major in music with a major or minor in another field of study. It is an excellent choice for a student who does not wish to pursue a performance-based program of study and who has music and academic interests in addition to music scholarship. Many students who complete the BA program in music pursue advanced studies in music history, ethnomusicology, music theory, music librarianship or music industry, and others pursue professional degrees such as law and medicine.
Accreditation status: The School of Music, Dance and Theatre is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music.

Concentration name: Composition, Jazz Performance, Music Learning and Teaching, Performance, Theory
description:
The Bachelor of Music in music is a professional degree designed to prepare students for careers in performance or composition and theory.

This degree program offers a rich and intensive educational experience that encourages a high level of professional and musical accomplishment. Students receive an education with an excellent foundation in music theory and music history.

The school promotes collaborative relationships among disciplines, and students in this program have the opportunity to participate in more than 400 concerts and recitals each academic year.
Accreditation status: The music programs are accredited by the National Association of Schools of Music.

description:
The bachelor's degree program in musical theatre provides students with conservatory-style training in acting, voice and dance in the context of a liberal arts education at a major research university. Students graduate with a Bachelor of Music in musical theatre.

The program is specifically designed to prepare students for a professional career in musical theatre as a performer on the stage and in film and television.

Students receive one-on-one voice instruction in both classical and contemporary musical theatre techniques (including belt, pop and rock styles) as well as group instruction in vocal styles, acting and dance (jazz, tap and ballet).

Students have many opportunities to perform in a variety of styles, in main stage productions and in student-led workshop productions, cabarets, revues, new work readings and senior capstone projects.

The capstone experience for musical theatre students takes place in the final semester and culminates in an industry showcase in New York City and Los Angeles. Students are mentored for careers as professional performers in musical theatre, stage, concert, theatre and film, or a combination of these areas.
Accreditation status: The School of Music, Dance and Theatre is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music.

Concentration name: Memory, Learning and Cognitive Neuroscience, Neurobiology, Pre-professional
description:
Neuroscience is the study of the nervous system, from the level of single molecules up to the intricacies of human behavior and cognition. It represents a vast, interdisciplinary field that draws from biology, chemistry, computer science, engineering, mathematics, medicine, philosophy, physics and psychology. The Bachelor of Science degree program in neuroscience provides a strong foundation for a variety of careers, including academic research, education, medicine and health care, biotechnology, pharmacology, science writing and law.

This program focuses on understanding the functions of the brain and nervous system in both health and disease. Students learn about the nervous system from the perspective of molecular and cellular biology, physiology and systems, and behavior and cognition. This broad base of knowledge prepares students for advanced studies and a wide variety of careers. The curriculum provides a balance of foundational and advanced coursework, including a series of four neuroscience courses that form the core of the major. The first three courses introduce students to foundational concepts in molecular, cellular, systems and behavioral neuroscience, and the senior capstone course provides an in-depth exploration of a specific area of neuroscience. The program offers a diverse selection of advanced electives covering a range of topics including neuroanatomy, neuroendocrinology, neuropharmacology, sensory physiology, and the biology of learning and memory.

To provide students with hands-on experience in neuroscience, the program requires a laboratory or research component. Students have the opportunity to take advanced laboratory courses or conduct independent research alongside world-class faculty. The honors thesis program offers motivated students the opportunity to work on an independent research project under the supervision of a faculty member.

The BS program in nonprofit leadership and management prepares students for professional careers in the nonprofit sector. The program provides a conceptual and practical background for working with and in diverse nonprofit organizations through a distinctive curriculum delivered by both world-class scholars and a diverse team of nationally and internationally recognized practitioners. Coursework focuses on key knowledge sectors of nonprofit management and leadership, including: community and social innovation, cross-sector collaboration, fundraising and development, human resources, leadership and ethics, marketing and social media, program evaluation and social entrepreneurship. Students apply this knowledge to the real world through capstone and internship experiences. The curriculum offers a unique learning experience through its engaged learning approach that emphasizes the practical application of theory to real-world problems facing nonprofit and philanthropic organizations. Students gain practical experience that allows them to learn important leadership skills in the classroom and in the field, working alongside nonprofit leaders and organizations in the community. Graduates of the program work in a wide variety of nonprofit organizations, including the arts, culture, community development, education, environment, health and human services, faith-based services, and sports.

The RN to BSN program in the Edson College of Nursing and Health Innovation at ASU is for registered nurses who have earned an associate degree or diploma in nursing and are looking for a top-quality, flexible and affordable online bachelor's degree program from a university with a national reputation for academic excellence. This program also serves as a strong foundation for nurses wishing to pursue graduate nursing education.

This fast-paced program has five-week courses that build on students' prior nursing knowledge and offer opportunities for professional growth. Students advance their skills in evidence-based practice, critical thinking and leadership. The program covers topics in professionalism, health promotion, patient safety, quality improvement, health information management, ethics, teamwork, collaboration and public health. Students in the program develop the knowledge and skills necessary for providing nursing care to an increasingly diverse population in a variety of health care settings.
Accreditation status: Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education

description:
The Bachelor of Science in nursing program at ASU's Edson College of Nursing and Health Innovation is a traditional, four-semester upper-division program that prepares students to function as generalists in acute care settings.

The curriculum follows a logical sequence, progressing from simple to complex concepts. Courses cover theory and concepts that are later applied in the clinical setting.

The clinical component, which enables students to develop the skills and competencies required of an entry-level professional nurse, consists of clinical and lab experiences in hospitals and community agencies throughout the metropolitan Phoenix area. An internship in the final semester offers students concentrated clinical experience.

Students completing the BSN program are eligible to apply to take the National Council Licensure Examination for Registered Nurses.
Accreditation status:
The Bachelor of Science in Nursing and Master of Science in Nursing programs at Arizona State University are accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (http://www.ccneaccreditation.org).

All ASU graduate and undergraduate academic programs are accredited by the Higher Learning Commission of the North Central Association of Colleges and Schools.

description:
The BS program in nutrition with a concentration in dietetics provides a curriculum based in the sciences to prepare students for a career as a registered dietitian nutritionist.

The program provides students with the academic foundation in nutrition science, food science, medical nutrition therapy, nutrition education and counseling, and community nutrition to provide services to individuals and groups.

Through coursework, lab and hands-on cooking and food preparation experiences, students learn how nutrition and food choices affect human health.

The curriculum provides a strong foundation in chemistry and the biological sciences to support students' understanding of nutrient metabolism and its application to human health and disease. Graduates of the program are well prepared for careers in a variety of settings such as health care organizations, community and public health agencies, corporate wellness programs, the food and nutrition industry, private practice, and research.

The concentration in dietetics is a Didactic Program in Dietetics that is accredited by the Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics.

Upon graduation, students are eligible to apply to an ACEND-accredited dietetic internship. Successful completion of the dietetic internship provides eligibility to take the Registration Examination for Dietitians. Passage of this exam grants the registered dietitian nutritionist credential.

Effective Jan. 1, 2024, the Commission on Dietetic Registration has changed the degree requirement for dietitian registration eligibility from a bachelor's degree to a graduate degree. In most states, graduates also must obtain licensure or certification to practice. For more information about the educational pathways to become a RDN, students should visit https://www.eatrightpro.org/acend/students-and-advancing-education/information-for-students.
Accreditation status: The concentration in dietetics is a Didactic Program in Dietetics that is accredited by the Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics.

description:
The BS program in nutrition with a concentration in food and nutrition management provides a strong foundation in nutrition science along with knowledge and skills in food and business management. It is designed for students interested in a career in areas such as:

community nutrition
foodservice systems management
nutrition management
public health

The curriculum is built upon a strong science foundation, including chemistry, biology, anatomy and physiology. The upper-division coursework includes advanced human nutrition, food science, quantity food production and management. The program is specifically designed to meet the academic requirements for students planning to become a registered dietitian nutritionist, the food and nutrition expert. A specific selection of courses provides students with the eligibility to apply to a dietetic internship, which is required prior to taking the national Registration Examination for Dietitians.

Graduates may also be interested in pursuing graduate study in a number of areas, including nutrition, food studies or public health.

This major is eligible for the Western Undergraduate Exchange (WUE) program. Students from Western states who choose this major and meet requirements may be eligible for a significant tuition reduction.
Accreditation status:
Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics
Status: Accreditation

Concentration name: ['Food and Nutrition Business', 'Human Nutrition', 'Nutritional Sciences', 'Public Health Nutrition']
description:
The Bachelor of Science in nutrition program at ASU provides a strong foundation in nutrition science, food and metabolism. The nutrition major is ideal for students interested in careers where they translate nutrition science to improve human health, including medicine and other health professions, nutrition research, community nutrition and the food industry.

Students are prepared to communicate nutrition information to diverse audiences, from individuals to communities to policy makers. With four distinct concentrations, students are able to tailor their education to match their career interests. Graduates can use the BS in nutrition as a standalone degree to enter the workforce or for entry into graduate or professional programs.

The BS program in nutritional science focuses on the physiological and biological aspects of foods and nutrients. This degree emphasizes the role of nutrition in health and disease and provides a strong foundation in the biological and chemical sciences.

Coursework in this program is science-intensive, with classes in biology, chemistry and biochemistry, organic chemistry, and physiology. Students learn to translate this information to meet the nutritional needs of individuals and populations.

The curriculum helps prepare students for further study in a graduate nutrition program or a professional health care program.

The Bachelor of Science in operations management and analysis program prepares students to use analytical and quantitative methods to solve operational problems. Operations management is a function of every business and organization and is focused on the design, management and improvement of the processes that create and deliver an organization's products and services.

Operations managers are problem-solvers who are interested in data and analysis and how to improve business processes.

Operations management and analysis graduates work in supply chain management, purchasing, logistics, consulting, quality management, project management and many other fields.
Accreditation status: All W. P. Carey School of Business degrees are accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.

description:
The Bachelor of Arts in organizational leadership with a concentration in project management offers an innovative, interdisciplinary curriculum with a focus on leadership theory, project management principles and techniques, and data-driven decision-making. Students benefit from an outcomes-based approach that includes a unique curriculum of eight-week courses that are fully online and taught by professional faculty from a variety of academic and professional backgrounds. Students are prepared to become versatile and resourceful project management professionals with the strong leadership and communication skills needed in today's global organizations, whether they are in the public, private or nonprofit sector.

The project management concentration focuses on providing students with the knowledge and skills needed for careers in the growing field of project management. The curriculum is aligned with the Project Management Body of Knowledge developed by the Project Management Institute and covers all the major areas of project management: scope, time, cost, risk, quality, communications, human resources, procurement and integration management.

In this program, students develop skills in project planning and scheduling, budgeting, resource allocation, risk management, and communication. Students learn how to effectively lead and motivate teams and manage project resources.

In the program's capstone course, students participate in a real-world project, which allows them to apply the knowledge and skills they have gained and to build their professional portfolio. This program prepares students for the Project Management Institute's Certified Associate in Project Management examination.

This program is offered by the College of Integrative Sciences and Arts.

The BA program in organizational leadership with a concentration in veterans, society and service focuses on developing the knowledge and skills for effective leadership in a variety of public, private and nonprofit settings, with a distinctive emphasis on understanding the veteran population. Students develop key communication, leadership and management skills for success in leading contemporary organizations. Students also gain a deeper and more thorough understanding of the unique strengths veterans bring to the workplace as well as the needs they and their families often have in health care, social services, and educational and career transitions from the military. The organizational leadership degree program is offered by the College of Integrative Sciences and Arts. The college's faculty is composed of nationally and internationally recognized scholars whose teaching and research focuses on the complex task of leading modern organizations in an increasingly diverse and globalized world. The program is ideal for veterans, active-duty military and military-family members as well as for those who aspire to work with and advocate for this growing and important segment of American society.
Program name: Organizational Leadership (Veterans, Society and Service), BA

description:
The BA program in organizational leadership provides an interdisciplinary education focused on theories and practices of leadership and leadership development. The program prepares students for leadership roles in a variety of public, private and nonprofit settings. The program also helps students who are already in leadership positions to be more effective.

Students in the organizational leadership major learn to:

apply leadership theories to real-world challenges
lead and manage organizational change
build teams and manage conflict
make ethical decisions
communicate effectively

The curriculum builds upon a liberal arts foundation and combines coursework from the social sciences and humanities. All students complete an internship or applied project, integrating classroom knowledge with practical experience.

The program's interdisciplinary focus cultivates intellectual flexibility and the critical thinking skills needed to analyze complex problems from multiple perspectives. The program's emphasis on ethics, communication and diversity prepares graduates who can help organizations thrive in an increasingly complex and diverse global marketplace.

The BS program in parks and recreation management prepares students for a variety of careers in the management of parks, recreation and tourism services and is designed for students interested in improving the quality of life within communities and for visitors. Parks and recreation management professionals work to provide and manage outdoor recreation experiences, sport and recreation programs in the community, and tourism and special event opportunities.

Students are prepared with a strong foundation of knowledge in management, marketing, leadership and programming. Throughout the curriculum, students gain career-relevant experience through hands-on learning in the classroom, in the community and in professional settings.

Graduates of the parks and recreation management program are well-prepared for entry-level professional positions and advancement to mid-management and upper-management positions within public, nonprofit and commercial organizations. Areas of emphasis in this major include park and recreation administration, sport management, tourism management and community recreation.
Accreditation status: The BS program in parks and recreation management with a concentration in therapeutic recreation is accredited by the Commission on Accreditation of Allied Health Education Programs upon the recommendation of the Committee on Accreditation of Recreational Therapy Education.

description: The BS program in pharmacology and toxicology provides a strong background in basic sciences, including chemistry and biology, as well as in-depth coursework and hands-on laboratory experience in pharmacology and toxicology. Students are introduced to the effects of chemicals on biological systems and learn about the discovery, development and regulation of drugs. They learn to identify and characterize the effects of drugs and other chemicals on the body, from the molecular and cellular levels to the organ systems and whole organism levels. They are exposed to a broad spectrum of topics including disease mechanisms and drug action, drug metabolism and disposition, mechanisms of chemical-induced toxicity, regulatory processes, and the application of modern research methods to solve pharmacological and toxicological problems. Through hands-on laboratory courses, students learn modern techniques used in the fields of pharmacology and toxicology. With a strong foundation in pharmacology and toxicology and basic sciences, graduates of this program are competitive for a wide range of graduate programs.

The Bachelor of Arts program in philosophy with a concentration in morality, politics and law provides a solid foundation for careers in law, public service, and public and private administration by focusing on the values and principles that underlie and justify political and legal institutions.

Students in this program benefit from close interaction with faculty who have international reputations for their scholarship. They develop their skills in reasoning, analysis and argumentation through challenging coursework, research opportunities and a variety of philosophy-related extracurricular activities.

Concentration name: Morality, Politics and Law, Science, Nature and Mind
description: The philosophy bachelor's degree program teaches students to think clearly and critically about the most important questions of human existence. In philosophy classes, students examine classic texts, analyze arguments and write their own reasoned arguments. These skills are valuable to a wide range of graduate studies and professional careers.

The BAE in physical education prepares students for careers as physical education teachers in K-12 schools.

The program emphasizes a holistic approach to physical education, focusing on developing physically literate individuals who have the knowledge, skills and confidence to enjoy a lifetime of healthful physical activity.

The program's curriculum is aligned with national and state standards for physical education and provides students with a strong foundation in the areas of motor development, exercise physiology, biomechanics, curriculum development and instructional strategies.

Students also gain extensive hands-on experience through a variety of field experiences in local schools, culminating in a full-time student teaching internship during their final semester.

Graduates are prepared to meet the requirements for teacher certification in Arizona and other states, and are equipped with the skills and knowledge to create and implement effective physical education programs that promote lifelong health and wellness for all students.
Accreditation status: The Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College is accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation.

description:
The BS program in physics with a concentration in astrophysics offers a strong foundation in classical and modern physics, and it provides specialized knowledge in astrophysics. This foundation prepares students for graduate study in astrophysics and related fields and for a wide range of careers in industry, data science, technology and education.

Specialized courses in astrophysics include theoretical astrophysics, observational astronomy and cosmology. The program focuses on active learning, with small classes and research opportunities, and provides exceptional career and academic mentoring by faculty members.

In addition to a rigorous and challenging curriculum, physics students often choose to enhance their education by getting involved in a wide variety of activities available at ASU, including the Society of Physics Students, research opportunities with faculty in the department, and science outreach programs.

The BS program in physics with a concentration in professional physics is designed for students with a keen interest in physics who plan to pursue graduate studies in the field or who plan to work as professional physicists in industry or government. Students gain a rigorous grounding in both classical and modern physics, learning to apply physical principles to the solution of problems. They learn to design and conduct experiments and to analyze and interpret the data collected. They also learn mathematical methods and the use of computers to solve physics problems. The concentration in professional physics is excellent preparation for graduate studies in physics, as the required coursework closely follows the guidelines of the American Institute of Physics. This includes advanced courses in electricity and magnetism, quantum mechanics and thermal physics, plus an advanced laboratory course. Graduates of this program may also elect to seek employment as physicists. They may find entry-level positions in industry or government in areas related to applied physics and engineering, such as aerospace, electronics, computation and energy.

The BA program in physics with a concentration in secondary education is a comprehensive program for students who wish to become high school physics teachers. The program provides a broad introduction to the fundamental principles of physics, with advanced coursework in mechanics, electricity and magnetism, and quantum physics. The program has been developed jointly by the Department of Physics and Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College. Graduates from this program receive an institutional recommendation from ASU to the Arizona Department of Education for certification as a secondary school teacher in physics. The program is part of a concerted effort by the physics department to respond to the urgent need for well-qualified high school teachers of physics and to the President's call for 100,000 new STEM teachers nationwide.
Accreditation status: Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College is accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation.

description:
The Bachelor of Arts in physics program provides a comprehensive survey of the main fields of physics in a flexible curriculum. It is intended for students who wish to pursue a career in a field where a strong background in physics is desirable or for students who wish to become certified as secondary school physics teachers.

The physics BA program gives students a solid foundation in physics while allowing them the flexibility to explore other academic areas. For example, students may wish to combine their studies in physics with preprofessional training in medicine, law or business; with a second major in philosophy, English or another liberal arts field; or with in-depth study in a technical area such as computer science, biology or engineering.

Students are not required to complete a senior-level capstone course; however, they may choose to complete an undergraduate research project or thesis as an elective.

For students who may be interested in a career in medicine, ASU offers a preprofessional health program. Pre-health professions advisors are available to help students prepare for medical school and other health professions.

Students who may be interested in a career in law can take advantage of the pre-law advising services at ASU. Students are encouraged to meet with a pre-law advisor early in their academic career and throughout their undergraduate experience.

Students who are interested in pursuing teacher certification should meet with their academic advisor to ensure that all requirements are met.

The Bachelor of Science in physics is designed to provide a broad and solid education in classical and modern physics with an emphasis on the theory and application of physics in the 21st century.
The program is suitable for those planning careers in research in physics or a related field (with a graduate degree); in secondary education; or in industry, including the aerospace, data science, defense, electronics, energy, medical, semiconductor and technology sectors.
In addition to the fundamental physics curriculum, students can participate in research projects in areas such as biophysics, cosmology, elementary particle physics, condensed matter and materials physics, nanoscience, and physics education. Many of these projects are in collaboration with faculty in other departments on campus and at other institutions and national laboratories. The Department of Physics offers research opportunities not only at the Tempe campus but at the Downtown Phoenix campus as well, through the Center for Biological Physics. Undergraduates will find access to state-of-the-art facilities for their research, such as the LeRoy Eyring Center for Solid State Science, the Center for Biological Physics and several facilities in the Biodesign Institute.

Political science is the study of governments, public policies and political processes, systems and political behavior. It is a social science dealing with the theory and practice of politics and the analysis of political systems and political behavior.

The BA program in political science provides students with a broad and systematic understanding of the political world and the skills to think critically, communicate effectively and conduct research. Students learn how to ask and answer important questions about politics, both domestic and international.
