They study how governments and political systems are structured and how they function, and they learn about the political ideas that have shaped the world.

Students may focus their studies on particular subfields, including:
- American politics
- comparative politics
- international relations
- political theory

In addition to a broad liberal arts background, this program provides students with the opportunity to develop skills in oral and written communication, as well as in critical and analytical thinking.

The Bachelor of Science in political science program provides students with the research tools to study social phenomena. This degree program prepares students to become leading researchers in a variety of social science fields.

The BS degree program in political science is recommended for students who want to develop more advanced quantitative analysis skills, especially those interested in continuing on to graduate school in political science, in data-driven careers in politics, government or the private sector, or in some law degrees where these skills are particularly helpful. The program prepares students to become leading researchers in various fields, with high-level skills in social science statistics, mathematics and research design.

The School of Politics and Global Studies is a dynamic and engaged community of scholars who are nationally and internationally recognized in their fields. Students learn from and work with faculty members who are leading experts on topics such as:

campaigns and elections
conflict and human rights
international relations
Latino politics
law and society
political theory
women and politics

As an integral part of the school, the BS program in political science prepares students with the tools they need to be socially aware, critically thinking and engaged citizens.

The BS program in population health provides students with the foundational skills and knowledge needed to improve the health of populations and promote health equity for all. Students learn the foundational skills and knowledge needed to improve the health of populations and promote health equity for all. They also develop the skills needed for evidence-based practice and decision-making by completing coursework in areas such as epidemiology, biostatistics, health policy, program planning, global health, and social and behavioral health. This comprehensive curriculum offers students the opportunity to examine the complex factors that influence human health and disease and to explore methods for protecting and improving the health of entire populations. The program can provide the foundation for graduate studies in public health or for medical, dental or pharmacy school, and it can prepare students for a wide range of career opportunities in the health care industry. Students interested in applying for graduate school or professional programs such as medical, dental or pharmacy school are strongly encouraged to connect with their academic advisor to discuss the specific courses they should take.

The BS program in preveterinary medicine is a comprehensive, four-year undergraduate course of study that combines coursework required for admission to a college of veterinary medicine with in-depth study of animal structure and function. Students develop a strong background in biology and chemistry and advanced coursework in anatomy, physiology, nutrition, immunology and other animal-related subjects.

The curriculum is ideal preparation for students who want to become veterinarians but who also may decide to pursue graduate or professional school opportunities in other health-related areas or careers in the biotechnology or animal health industries. The degree program includes all of the required coursework for admission to most colleges of veterinary medicine.

Students who wish to pursue a career in veterinary medicine may do so with a variety of undergraduate degrees. Because admission to veterinary college is not guaranteed and is extremely competitive, students are advised to choose a degree program that offers a strong background in the sciences and offers a variety of career options.

This major is eligible for the Western Undergraduate Exchange program at a reduced tuition rate. The WUE tuition rate is available to students from Alaska, California, Colorado, Hawaii, Idaho, Montana, Nevada, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oregon, South Dakota, Utah, Washington, Wyoming, Guam, the Republic of the Marshall Islands, the Federated States of Micronesia and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands (CNMI).

This program is offered by the College of Integrative Sciences and Arts at the Polytechnic campus.

Concentration name: Air Transportation Management, Unmanned Aerial Systems
description:
The BS program in professional flight prepares students to become professional pilots. Graduates earn a commercial pilot certificate with multi-engine and instrument ratings.

The program focuses on developing the aeronautical knowledge, skills and flight proficiency needed for a career as a professional pilot. Students learn to fly in the most technologically advanced aircraft and simulators available. The program meets the requirements for a restricted airline transport pilot certificate. With a restricted ATP, a pilot needs only 1,000 flight hours to be eligible to fly for an airline, compared with 1,500 hours otherwise required. Additionally, a graduate of ASU's professional flight program earns the commercial pilot certificate in as few as 450 flight hours versus the standard 1,500 hours it could take from other flight schools.

Students have the opportunity to make valuable contacts with industry professionals. Upon completion of flight training, students can apply for certified flight instructor positions with ASU's flight provider, AeroGuard Flight Training Center.

Graduates are prepared for careers as professional pilots.
Accreditation status: This program is accredited by the Aviation Accreditation Board International.

description: The BS program in professional science with a concentration in applied physics provides a unique alternative to traditional degree programs in science. This innovative program combines a strong core in the major with professional skills in communication, computation and workplace practices. Students are trained in the fundamentals of physics and in how to apply their knowledge to technology-based careers. In addition to technical proficiency, students gain critical workplace skills such as project management, business fundamentals and leadership.

The Bachelor of Science degree program in professional science with a concentration in environmental technology and management is an innovative, interdisciplinary program that combines a science background with professional skills to prepare students for a variety of careers in the technology and management sectors of the environmental industry.

The program provides students with the critical skills and knowledge needed to address the complex environmental challenges facing society.

The curriculum combines courses in life and physical sciences, technology and engineering, management, and leadership. Students learn from faculty in the College of Integrative Sciences and Arts and Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering who are experts in their fields and have extensive experience in the environmental industry.

Students have opportunities to gain hands-on experience through internships and research projects with industry partners and government agencies.

Graduates are well prepared for careers in a variety of fields, including:
-environmental consulting
-environmental health and safety
-natural resource management
-sustainability

Graduates are prepared for career paths in industry and governmental agencies as well as for admission to professional science master's programs.
Program name: Professional Science (Environmental Technology and Management), BS

description:
The BS program in project management provides students with the knowledge and skills needed for careers managing projects in a variety of industries.

Students learn the entire project life cycle, from initiation and planning to execution, monitoring, controlling and closing. The curriculum covers a wide array of courses, including:
-agile project management
-change management
-cost and schedule control
-leadership
-procurement
-quality management
-risk management

The program provides a deep understanding of project management principles, tools and techniques. Students are prepared to plan, execute and oversee projects to successful completion, making them valuable assets to any organization.
Accreditation status: The Bachelor of Science in project management is accredited by the PMI Global Accreditation Center for Project Management Education Programs (GAC). The GAC is the world's leading specialized accrediting body for project management and related degree programs, attesting to the quality of the ASU degree program and its graduates.

description:
The Bachelor of Arts in psychology provides a strong foundation for a variety of careers and for the pursuit of graduate studies in psychology and other professional fields. The degree program emphasizes the development of critical and analytical thinking skills.

Students learn about the science of behavior and mental processes through active learning and mentored experiences in research labs and community settings. Many psychology majors also complete a second major, a minor or a certificate in other areas, such as family and human development, business, or justice studies, to expand their skills and career options.

ASU's Department of Psychology is an award-winning department that has been recognized by the American Psychological Association for its undergraduate program. The program provides the opportunity to explore many areas within psychology through a wide variety of research areas and courses such as:

Social Psychology
Clinical Psychology
Cognitive Psychology
Developmental Psychology
Behavioral Neuroscience
Abnormal Psychology
Memory and Forgetting
These courses represent the major areas of psychological science.

Students interested in pursuing a graduate degree in psychology or a related area are strongly encouraged to gain research experience by working in one of the psychology department's more than 30 research labs. The Department of Psychology's website has a search tool for finding research opportunities.

The Bachelor of Science in psychology program provides a strong foundation in the concepts and methods of the science of psychology.

Psychology is the scientific study of behavior and mental processes, from the level of the nerve cell to the level of the group. The BS program offers a more extensive background in the foundational areas of psychology and a more comprehensive quantitative and research methods sequence than does the Bachelor of Arts program. The degree is excellent preparation for graduate study in psychology as well as other professional fields, such as law and medicine.

Psychology majors gain experience in analyzing, interpreting and synthesizing information in a scientific manner. These are skills that are highly valued in many work environments.

The bachelor's degree in psychology is a popular undergraduate major. Many students choose to combine their study of psychology with another major or minor. Psychology graduates are employed in a wide variety of work settings. Many jobs require specific skills and knowledge in a specialized area, such as applied behavior analysis, and students should check with a departmental advisor for details on specific career-related course sequences.

The BS program in public administration is intended for students who are interested in a career in public service. The program prepares students with the knowledge and skills necessary for management and leadership positions in government and nonprofit organizations.
The curriculum requires courses in a number of public service-related areas, including:

leadership and management
public policy
public finance
urban studies

The curriculum prepares students to solve public problems and to pursue and advance in a public service career. Coursework focuses on the knowledge and skills that are most useful to public service professionals, and students learn to critically analyze and creatively respond to the challenges of governance. Students also develop an appreciation for the ethical dimensions of public service and the importance of professional integrity.
The program is offered by the School of Public Affairs, part of the Watts College of Public Service and Community Solutions.

The BS program in public health prepares students to promote and protect the health of individuals and communities.

Students learn how to analyze and understand the complex factors that influence the health and well-being of individuals, families, communities and populations and develop skills to promote health equity and prevent disease, injury and disability.

The curriculum provides a strong foundation in the five core disciplines of public health:
biostatistics
environmental health
epidemiology
health policy and management
social and behavioral sciences

Students take coursework on topics such as:
global health
health communication
health disparities
health education and promotion
program planning, implementation and evaluation
research methods

Throughout the program, students gain real-world experience through an internship, which provides a valuable opportunity to apply their knowledge and skills in a public health setting.

Upon graduation, students are well prepared for careers in a variety of public health fields, such as:
community health
environmental health
global health
health communication
health education and promotion

They are also well-prepared for graduate studies in public health and related fields, such as health care administration, medicine and public policy.

Graduates of this program may be eligible to sit for the national credentialing exam to become a Certified Health Education Specialist. The CHES exam is offered by the National Commission for Health Education Credentialing and is the only accredited credential in the health education and promotion profession.

The BS program in public policy teaches students the skills to understand, analyze and influence public policy at the local, state and national levels. Students learn to critically evaluate policy arguments, research and data; conduct policy analysis; and communicate effectively about policy issues orally and in writing. The curriculum integrates a strong foundation in public policy with analytical courses in economics and research methods as well as a policy concentration of the student's choice. Graduates are well-prepared for a variety of careers in which they can make a difference in their communities and in leadership positions in government, nonprofit organizations and the private sector.

The BA program in public relations and strategic communications provides a comprehensive understanding of how to be an effective communicator in a variety of business, media and nonprofit organizations. Students in this degree program learn how to communicate effectively with diverse audiences and to create and sustain the quality of relationships that an organization needs to succeed. The program also provides skills in managing internal and external communications programs using traditional and new media. Students learn how to respond to and manage crises and to become innovative problem-solvers. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in professional ethics, media law, theory and research. All students are required to complete a professional internship prior to graduation.
Program name: Public Relations and Strategic Communications, BA

description:
The BS program in public service and public policy with a concentration in emergency management and homeland security offers an innovative, interdisciplinary curriculum. It draws on the expertise of faculty in the School of Public Affairs and from a variety of other academic units across ASU.

The curriculum combines a foundation in public service and public policy with specialized courses in emergency management and homeland security and electives drawn from related disciplines. The program prepares students for leadership and management roles in public, private and nonprofit organizations through the study of topics that include:

all-hazards emergency management
comparative disaster management
critical infrastructure protection
cybersecurity policy and management
disaster planning and preparedness
disaster response and recovery
ethical issues for emergency managers
health and medical issues in emergency management
homeland security policy and administration
information technology in emergency management
introduction to public service and public policy
terrorism
The coursework prepares students for challenging leadership positions within the public safety disciplines of fire services, law enforcement, and emergency medical and health services. Students gain the critical-thinking skills and understanding necessary to excel as leaders who must address the challenges of disaster response and recovery.
Program name: Public Service and Public Policy (Emergency Management and Homeland Security), BS

description:
The BS program in public service and public policy prepares students for careers in the public sector, including in government and nonprofit organizations. Students gain insight into public policy and the issues public and nonprofit managers face, from human resources and budgeting to policy analysis and ethics. Students learn to develop and implement policy and deliver public services effectively and ethically in a diverse and dynamic society. Students acquire an understanding of the structure and function of the public sector, the skills required for success in public service and the values characteristic of public service.

Core coursework in public policy and management provides the foundation for students to develop specializations in areas of individual interest.

The BS program in public service and public policy also offers a concentration in emergency management and homeland security. The concentration prepares students with the knowledge and skills necessary for a career in emergency management and homeland security. Students develop competence in the management of all types of hazards and disasters through the study of planning, mitigation, response and recovery. A wide variety of elective courses in criminal justice, social work, public affairs, geography, communication, sustainability and other areas are available to support and enrich the curriculum.
Program name: Public Service and Public Policy, BS

description:
The Bachelor of Arts in business with a concentration in real estate provides an overview of the tools and concepts used for real estate decision-making.

The program is designed for students who want to develop a broad-based knowledge of business with a specific understanding of real estate markets, law, finance and appraisal. Students are prepared to become leaders who create value in the real-estate development, investment, and lending industries.
Accreditation status: The W. P. Carey School of Business is accredited by the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB International).

description:
The Bachelor of Science in recreation therapy program at ASU is designed to prepare competent, entry-level recreational therapists with the knowledge, skills and abilities necessary to become leaders in the field and successfully complete the national exam. The program curriculum is specifically aligned with the requirements of the National Council for Therapeutic Recreation Certification.

The recreational therapy profession seeks to improve the quality of life for individuals with disabilities, injuries or illnesses through active treatment. This is achieved using a systematic approach called the therapeutic recreation process, which includes assessment, planning, implementation, evaluation and documentation. Recreational therapists are active, creative and compassionate professionals who use recreation activities and other life experiences to help people make the most of their lives --- physically, mentally, emotionally and socially.

The program requires students to complete a supervised, professional internship in the final semester of the program. Faculty members assist students in obtaining an internship that fits their desired career path.
Accreditation status: The recreation therapy program is accredited by the Commission on Accreditation of Allied Health Education Programs upon the recommendation of the Committee on Accreditation of Recreational Therapy Education.

description:
The Bachelor of Arts in religious studies is the undergraduate degree program in the academic study of religion.

The curriculum focuses on the critical, analytical and cross-cultural study of religions. Students learn to see religions as complex and historically dynamic traditions, involving texts, rituals, social institutions, and material cultures, which have shaped, and in turn been shaped by, their historical and cultural contexts.

The curriculum covers the major world religions (Buddhism, Christianity, Hinduism, Islam and Judaism) and also newer, smaller-scale or little-known traditions as well as non-religious meaning systems.

In addition to a broad comparative overview of religious traditions, students also develop expertise in one tradition or a particular theme. Students learn diverse approaches to the study of religion, from fields such as:

anthropology
history
philosophy
sociology

They gain strong research and writing skills, and they learn to think critically about complex texts, practices and social formations. The degree offers a basic foundation in the study of religion that can lead to graduate study or to a wide variety of careers.

The Bachelor of Science in Engineering in robotics program is an interdisciplinary program that prepares students to meet the challenges of designing and developing the intelligent systems of today and the future. Students will develop foundational knowledge in computer science, data structures, mathematics and the physical sciences, with strong hands-on experience in the design, development, construction and application of robotic and autonomous systems, including control systems and machine learning.

Through an integrative, experience-based curriculum, students will gain experience in the end-to-end design of robotic systems, as well as an appreciation of the social and ethical aspects of these technologies. Students who complete the BSE in robotics will be prepared for work in the increasingly interdisciplinary field of robotics, where expertise in both hardware and software is critical. The curriculum provides breadth and depth across the core areas of robotics (sensing, reasoning and acting) while also enabling students to pursue specialized interests in a specific area.

This program is offered by the School of Computing and Augmented Intelligence.
Accreditation status: The robotics BSE program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

description:
The Bachelor of Arts program in Russian offers students a solid foundation in the Russian language, with a focus on all four language skills (speaking, listening, reading and writing), and combines it with the study of Russian literature, culture, history, politics and film.

In addition to the skills gained through the study of a foreign language, literature and culture, which are highly valued by employers, students develop the strong intercultural communication and critical thinking skills needed to thrive in an increasingly interconnected and diverse world. Graduates are prepared for careers in a wide range of fields, including education, government service, journalism, national security, nongovernmental and nonprofit organizations, and translation and interpretation.

The program offers a diverse selection of Russian language, literature and culture courses. All Russian majors are strongly encouraged to participate in one of the study abroad programs available in Russia and other Russian-speaking countries.

The BAE program in secondary education with a concentration in biological sciences prepares students to become middle school or high school science teachers. Students learn how to be effective teachers and how to develop and evaluate curriculum and instructional materials.

The program combines coursework in biology and other sciences with courses in the theory and practice of teaching. Teacher candidates learn how to plan lessons, manage a classroom and assess student learning. They are taught how to foster a learning environment in which all students, including those from diverse cultural and linguistic backgrounds, can succeed.

Extensive field experiences in a variety of school settings give students the opportunity to practice their teaching skills and connect what they are learning in their university classes with the realities of the classroom. The program culminates in a full-time clinical experience (student teaching).

Graduates are recommended for teacher certification in Arizona to teach biology in grades 6 through 12.
Accreditation status: This program, which is accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation, leads to teacher certification in the state of Arizona.

description:
The BAE program in secondary education with a concentration in chemistry prepares students to teach chemistry in grades seven through 12. The program is a collaboration between the Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College and The College of Liberal Arts and Sciences. Students complete subject matter coursework in the partner college and teacher preparation coursework in the Teachers College.

Graduates of this program earn an institutional recommendation from ASU to the Arizona Department of Education for teacher certification in the state of Arizona in chemistry, grades 7-12.

All students must meet the requirements for Arizona teacher certification. This includes extended field experiences (teacher residencies) in a variety of settings appropriate to the student's chosen content area and grade level. Students should see the academic advisor for information on completing requirements for teacher certification.

The BAE program in secondary education with a concentration in earth and space sciences prepares students to become middle school and high school earth and space sciences teachers.

Coursework in this Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College program emphasizes the content knowledge and pedagogical skills needed to be a highly qualified teacher, including research-based teaching strategies and methods. The coursework is integrated with extensive field experiences in partner districts, culminating in a full-time student teaching internship.

Upon completion of the program, students are prepared to teach a variety of earth and space sciences subjects, including:
- astronomy
- geology
- meteorology
- oceanography

Students who complete this program earn a bachelor's degree and an Arizona teaching certificate in secondary education, 6-12, and a structured English immersion endorsement, K-12. This program is also offered as a fast-track option for eligible students, allowing them to complete both their undergraduate and master's degrees in education in four and a half years.
Accreditation status: All educator preparation programs in the Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College are accredited by the Association for Advancing Quality in Educator Preparation. ASU is also accredited by the Higher Learning Commission.
Program name: Secondary Education (Earth and Space Sciences), BAE

description:
The BAE program in secondary education with a concentration in English prepares students to teach English in grades 6-12. The program emphasizes the knowledge, skills and dispositions needed to be an effective teacher of English in a multicultural society.

Coursework focuses on knowledge of the subject matter, the learner and learning, and curriculum, instruction and assessment. Students learn about the English language and how to analyze literature as well as how to teach reading and a wide range of types of writing.

This secondary education program includes professional experiences in a variety of school settings, including a full-time student teaching internship. The professional experiences, which are integrated with the coursework, provide students with a rich, hands-on experience of working with students from various cultural, linguistic and socioeconomic backgrounds.

All coursework is taken in a sequential manner.

Arizona teacher certification for grades 6-12 is awarded upon successful completion of the program. The Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College provides a teaching certification officer who is a liaison to the Arizona Department of Education and who is able to provide information on the certification process.
Accreditation status: The Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College is accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation.

description:
The BAE program in secondary education with a concentration in history prepares students to teach history in grades 6-12. Students learn to develop curriculum, instruction and assessment materials to meet the needs of all learners in history classrooms, including English language learners and students with disabilities.

Students in this program are not required to complete a minor.

In addition to the content knowledge courses in history, students take a range of professional teacher preparation courses grounded in research-based practices, and they spend significant time in partner-district schools working with mentor teachers and students. The program culminates in a full-time student teaching internship. Upon successful completion of all program requirements, graduates are recommended for teacher certification in Arizona.
Accreditation status: The Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College is accredited by the American Psychological Association and the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation.

description:
The BAE program in secondary education with a concentration in mathematics prepares students to teach mathematics to students in grades seven through 12.

The program offers students rich, discipline-based content knowledge and research-based pedagogical training in a clinically rich teacher preparation program. Graduates of the program are prepared to have a positive impact on student learning and to meet the unique needs of diverse student populations.

Students in this program benefit from the expertise of world-class faculty in Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College. This professional educator preparation program in the college is a model for 21st-century teacher education.

The program includes cutting-edge coursework, extensive clinical experiences and a student-centered environment that is supportive of diversity. Students' coursework is enriched by research and hands-on learning in a variety of school and community settings.

Graduates are recommended for teacher certification in Arizona.
Accreditation status: Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College is accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation.

description:
The Bachelor of Arts in Education in secondary education with a concentration in physics prepares students to teach physics in a secondary school setting (grades 6-12).

The program provides students with a broad and balanced curriculum of physics and pedagogy coursework. Students explore the principles of physics and how to translate those concepts into engaging and effective lesson plans.

Students also gain hands-on experience by completing a two-semester student teaching experience in a local school. The program is designed to meet the certification requirements of the Arizona Department of Education.
Accreditation status: The Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College is accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation.

description:
The BAE program in secondary education with a concentration in political science prepares students to teach political science in grades 7-12.

The program offers a solid foundation for teaching political science in secondary schools. It features a combination of academic work in a content area, professional education experiences and courses leading to institutional recommendation for teacher certification.

The secondary education program is an intensive, cohort-based program that requires students to apply for admission in their sophomore year. All students complete a common core of courses providing a strong foundation in secondary education theory and practice, and they are assigned to a full-year internship in the senior year. In addition, students work with an advisor from the Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College to ensure that all requirements for teacher certification are met.

The BA program in social and behavioral sciences provides students with an integrated learning experience that draws on the social sciences to explain the causes and consequences of human behavior. The program's interdisciplinary approach provides students with a holistic understanding of people and societies. Students take courses in a variety of fields, including communication, economics, history, political science, psychology and sociology, to analyze human behavior and its connection to the broader social world.

Students also have opportunities to work alongside faculty on research projects and to pursue their own research interests through the New College Undergraduate Inquiry and Research Experiences program. The college's faculty are nationally recognized scholars in their fields who are dedicated to excellence in both teaching and research.

In this program, students develop a core set of analytic and methodological skills and then choose a variety of social science electives based on their career goals. These courses prepare students for careers in diverse fields, such as business, counseling, law, public administration and social work.

Students pursuing an undergraduate certificate in social sciences research methods can learn social science research techniques and gain hands-on experience by collecting, analyzing, interpreting and presenting data.

The BA program in social and cultural analysis with a concentration in American studies is an interdisciplinary program focusing on the historical and contemporary formations of American culture. Students in American studies explore how race, class, gender, sexuality and place have shaped American society. Coursework in American studies challenges students to learn and use theories and methods from a wide range of academic fields, including:
cultural studies
history
literary studies
media studies
performance studies
sociology
Students have opportunities for independent research and for internships in museums and other cultural institutions in the Phoenix metropolitan area.
The degree can be used to prepare for a wide range of occupations, including:
cultural programming
education
journalism
law
library science
social justice and advocacy work
Program name: Social and Cultural Analysis (American Studies), BA

description:
The social and cultural analysis program provides students with a transdisciplinary and integrated understanding of culture, society and identity.

Students in the program analyze social and cultural phenomena through the lenses of history, theory, cultural production, power and positionality. They examine social constructs such as race, ethnicity, class, gender, sexuality and dis/ability, and they learn to communicate effectively about the critical issues of the day, including privilege, inequality and social justice. The curriculum challenges students to move beyond the classroom to engage in the broader community and practice the skills they learn through research and real-world application.

The social and cultural analysis major consists of a common core of courses that grounds students in the fundamental theories and practices in the study of social and cultural phenomena. The program also offers a number of concentrations in specific fields of study, which gives students the opportunity to choose the courses that most closely match their interests and career goals.

The ethnic studies concentration offers in-depth examination of the social construction of race and its impacts at personal, interpersonal, institutional, societal and global levels. Students analyze racial identity formation and the intersections of race with class, gender, sexuality, nationality, ability and other markers of difference. Students learn the histories and cultures of a wide array of racialized and Indigenous groups to prepare for living and working in a diverse society. Courses examine race and racism through multiple disciplinary lenses from the humanities and social sciences. Students are strongly encouraged to select elective courses from across the School of Social Transformation curriculum and from other disciplines across the university.

Students who major in social and cultural analysis are well prepared to work in a variety of settings where critical analysis, creative thinking, intercultural communication, and a strong sense of social responsibility and civic engagement are valued. The program is also excellent preparation for graduate study in a wide range of academic disciplines and professional fields. A bachelor's degree in social and cultural analysis with a concentration in ethnic studies provides a strong foundation for law school or graduate studies in fields such as the humanities, social sciences, cultural studies, communication and justice studies. This concentration is also valuable to careers requiring a strong liberal arts background with a focus on human diversity.
Program name: Social and Cultural Analysis (Ethnic Studies), BA

description:
The BA program in social and cultural analysis with a concentration in Latin American studies offers an interdisciplinary approach to the study of the peoples, cultures, societies and political systems of Latin America and the Caribbean. The curriculum allows students to develop an area of interest within Latin American studies.

Students have an opportunity to gain global awareness and cross-cultural communication skills that can be applied to many careers.

The program offers unique opportunities to study with outstanding faculty in the U.S. and in Latin America and the Caribbean.
Program name: Social and Cultural Analysis (Latin American Studies), BA

description:
The social and cultural analysis program at ASU provides students with the intellectual and practical tools for understanding and engaging with the major social and cultural issues of our time, in local, national and global contexts.

The program combines critical social theory, cultural studies, community-based research and engagement, and innovative curriculum to equip students with the necessary skills to analyze complex social problems and cultural phenomena and to become effective leaders of social change.

Students learn to ask pressing questions about the social world, such as how social inequalities are produced and reproduced, how social identities are created and contested, and how different cultural forms and practices shape our lives and the worlds we inhabit. They develop strong analytical, research, writing and public presentation skills to effectively communicate their ideas to a range of audiences.

The peace studies concentration teaches students to link theory with practice to address the major challenges to peace in the 21st century. The concentration draws from a range of fields, including:

conflict resolution
history
political science
psychology
religious studies
sociology

Students gain understanding of how to engage directly with conflict and its effects and to promote positive change through nonviolent and creative means.
Program name: Social and Cultural Analysis (Peace Studies), BA

description: The social and cultural analysis program offers a unique interdisciplinary curriculum that enables students to develop a sophisticated understanding of the complexities of our social world. The concentration in queer and sexuality studies allows students to engage in an interdisciplinary study of sexuality and its importance to human societies and lives in the past and present. The curriculum is composed of courses on gender and sexuality that are drawn from a variety of fields and disciplines, including: history, literature, philosophy, religion, theatre, film and media studies, sociology, anthropology, political science, psychology, art history, and women's and gender studies. The curriculum includes courses on a variety of subjects, such as: the history of sexuality, lesbian and gay history, queer theory, queer and transgender literature, gender and sexuality in the ancient world, gender and sexuality in American religion, gender and sexuality in film, and the sociology of sexualities. Students learn about the various ways in which sexuality has been organized, understood and experienced historically and cross-culturally, and they develop their abilities to think critically about sexual norms, the politics of sexuality and the historical construction of sexual identities.
Program name: Social and Cultural Analysis (Queer and Sexuality Studies), BA

description: The BA program in social and cultural analysis with a concentration in women and gender studies offers an interdisciplinary curriculum grounded in the humanities, social sciences and cultural studies. The program provides a unique opportunity to study how gender and other social categories of difference shape the lives of individuals and groups of people in a variety of cultural contexts. Students explore a wide array of topics such as gendered representations in media and literature, the social construction of gender and sexuality, queer studies, the history of feminist thought, and the relationship between gender and social justice. Throughout their course of study, students develop strong critical thinking, analytical, communication and research skills, graduating with a complex understanding of the significance of gender as a social and cultural construct.
Program name: Social and Cultural Analysis (Women and Gender Studies), BA

description:
The BA program in social justice and human rights, housed in the New College of Interdisciplinary Arts and Sciences, provides students with a deep understanding of the historical and contemporary struggles for social justice and human rights.

The program is interdisciplinary, drawing on a range of fields, including law, philosophy, political science, history, sociology and literature to provide students with the intellectual and practical skills necessary to be effective agents of social change and to promote social justice and human rights locally, nationally and globally.

The curriculum focuses on a range of social justice and human rights issues, including economic justice, racial justice, gender justice, environmental justice and LGBTQIA+ rights. Students are encouraged to develop a critical understanding of the social, economic, and political structures that perpetuate injustice and inequality, as well as the strategies and tactics that social movements and human rights organizations have used to challenge those structures.

Graduates are prepared for a variety of careers in fields such as advocacy, community organizing, education, law, nonprofit management, policy analysis and social services. The program can also provide a solid foundation for those interested in pursuing graduate studies in areas such as law, public policy, social work or human rights or as preparation for graduate school.
Program name: Social Justice and Human Rights, BA

description:
The Bachelor of Social Work program at ASU prepares students for entry-level professional social work practice to enhance human well-being and to help meet the needs of diverse individuals, families, groups, organizations and communities. Students learn to advocate for social, economic and environmental justice. Students gain real-world experience through internships at social service agencies.

Coursework and field education experiences are based on a competency model that prepares students to provide social work services in an ethical and effective manner.

The BSW program is available at the Downtown Phoenix, Tucson, West and ASU@Yuma campuses. Students at the ASU@Lake Havasu location can take social work courses as part of the social and behavioral sciences bachelor's degree program with a concentration in social work.

The School of Social Work is dedicated to creating a learning community that is diverse and inclusive, including among its faculty, staff and student body. The school acknowledges the historical and ongoing injustices and violence that Black, Indigenous and other people of color, and other marginalized groups, experience in the U.S. and globally. It recognizes that these injustices are reproduced in institutions of higher education and within the social work profession. Therefore, the school is committed to creating an anti-racist, anti-oppressive and inclusive culture in its classrooms, policies, and practices and in its engagement with the community.
Accreditation status: The Bachelor of Social Work program at Arizona State University is accredited by the Council on Social Work Education's Commission on Accreditation.

description:
The Bachelor of Science in sociology is the study of social life, social change, and the social causes and consequences of human behavior. Because all human behavior is social behavior, the subject matter of sociology ranges from the intimate family to the hostile mob, from organized crime to religious cults, from the divisions of race, gender and social class to the shared beliefs of a common culture, and from the sociology of work to the sociology of sport.

This program provides students with core knowledge of sociology, with a strong focus on social research methods and analytical skills.

The skills learned through the program are valuable in a wide variety of careers.

The Bachelor of Science in software engineering program is focused on the professional aspects of software engineering. It is an application-oriented program based on a core of computer science and mathematics, with an emphasis on working in teams to build and maintain large, complex and secure software systems for the real world.

Graduates are prepared for immediate employment and long-term professional growth in a range of organizations. They are prepared to lead teams of software engineers and to communicate effectively with stakeholders.

The BA program in Spanish with a concentration in literature offers students a wide range of courses in Spanish, Spanish American and U.S. Latino literatures and cultures, from the Middle Ages to the 21st century. Students gain insight into the diverse peoples, histories and cultures of the Spanish-speaking world. In addition to a set of core courses designed to solidify their language skills and critical vocabulary, students in the literature concentration can choose from a wide variety of advanced courses, including:
- Chicano and Chicana literature and culture
- film studies
- Latin American literature and culture
- Medieval and Golden Age Spanish literature and culture
- modern and contemporary Spanish literature and culture

Students also have the opportunity to take courses from a wide range of topics, such as gender studies, popular culture and post-colonial studies.

The curriculum encourages students to think critically about the world and their place in it. Students can enhance their experience through a variety of study abroad programs.

The bachelor's degree program in special education and elementary education leads to teacher certification in both special education (K-12) and elementary education (K-8). The program prepares highly qualified teachers who are equipped to meet the needs of all learners in today's diverse classrooms.
The program combines research-based practices with extensive field experiences in a variety of school settings. The first three years of coursework are identical to the coursework for the BAE in elementary education. Students apply for advancement to the final, professional year of the program when they have met specific requirements, including prerequisite coursework and a minimum GPA.
For the final year of the program, students are part of a cohort that completes a yearlong residency in a K-8 school. This residency includes student teaching and provides a rich clinical experience under the guidance of a highly qualified mentor teacher and a university supervisor.
The BAE in elementary education is also offered as a fast-track program. Students enrolled in this accelerated program complete the same high-quality courses and clinical experiences on an accelerated path, enabling them to graduate and enter the workforce sooner.
Accreditation status: Mary Lou Fulton Teachers College is accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation.
Program name: Special Education and Elementary Education, BAE

description: The bachelor's degree program in speech and hearing science provides students with a strong foundation in the processes and disorders of speech, language and hearing. Students learn the basic science of how humans produce and perceive speech and language as well as the nature of sound and how it is processed by the auditory system. The curriculum also introduces students to the various disorders of communication that affect people throughout their lives and to the methods used to assess and treat these disorders. The program offers outstanding academic and clinical preparation for graduate studies in either speech-language pathology or audiology.

The BA program in sport and media studies explores the symbiotic relationship between sports and various media forms, from traditional print and broadcast to emerging digital platforms. The program provides a comprehensive understanding of how sports are represented, consumed and influenced by media, as well as how media shapes public perception and the cultural significance of sports.

Students in this program delve into the historical, cultural, economic and political dimensions of sports media. They analyze media content, production practices and audience reception in relation to sports, and they examine the role of media in constructing narratives, creating stars and promoting sports as entertainment and a cultural spectacle.

The curriculum is interdisciplinary, drawing from fields such as media studies, cultural studies, sociology, history and communication. Students develop critical thinking, analytical and communication skills, which are essential for careers in sports journalism, broadcasting, public relations, marketing, and media production and management.

Graduates are prepared to critically engage with and contribute to the ever-evolving landscape of sports media, whether as practitioners, critics or scholars.

The BA program in sports business combines a strong business core with sports-specific curriculum and experiences to prepare students to pursue a career in the dynamic and competitive sports industry.

The sports business program is offered by the W. P. Carey School of Business, which has a worldwide reputation for quality and is accredited by AACSB International.

Students are educated on all facets of the business of sports, including topics such as sports analytics, marketing and promotions, sponsorship, facilities and event management, and sports law and ethics. An internship and applied learning opportunities provide students with invaluable real-world experience. Students learn from world-class faculty who bring research and practical industry experience to the classroom. Top sports executives and organizations from around the country partner with the program, offering students unique engagement opportunities and connections.

Upon graduation, students have a strong foundation in business principles and the specialized knowledge needed for a career in the sports industry.
Accreditation status: The W. P. Carey School of Business, which has a worldwide reputation for quality and is accredited by AACSB International.

description:
The BA program in sports journalism, in the Walter Cronkite School of Journalism and Mass Communication, prepares students for careers as sports journalists and communicators. The program teaches students the values of accuracy, fairness and diversity in reporting and editing, as well as the roles of journalists in a democracy and the importance of professional ethics.

Students learn to report and write for a variety of media, including broadcast, digital and print. They learn to produce in-depth stories and analysis on sports issues and events. They also learn how to create and edit visual content, such as photographs and videos, as well as how to use social media to engage with audiences and promote their work.

Students have the opportunity to cover professional and college sports for major media outlets through sports bureaus in Phoenix and Los Angeles. They gain hands-on experience in a variety of roles, such as play-by-play announcer, color commentator, sideline reporter, anchor, producer, director and videographer for professional and collegiate sporting events. They also learn how to produce content for digital and social media platforms, including websites, blogs and podcasts.

The Cronkite School has a national reputation for its sports journalism program, which is consistently ranked among the best in the country. The school has state-of-the-art facilities, including a dedicated sports broadcasting studio, and a faculty of experienced professionals who are committed to helping students succeed. Graduates of the program have gone on to work for major sports media outlets, such as ESPN, Fox Sports and the NFL Network.
Accreditation status: Accrediting Council on Education in Journalism and Mass Communications

description: The BS program in statistics provides students with a fundamental understanding of the concepts of probability and statistical inference, and a proficiency in the application of statistical methods and data analysis skills. This program covers the same core of statistics courses as the BA program but is supplemented with a greater emphasis on mathematics and the technical aspects of probability and statistical theory. It is designed to prepare students for graduate study in statistics or for a career as a practicing statistician in industry or government. Students learn to use modern statistical software for data analysis and gain experience in statistical consulting. Coursework includes a yearlong sequence in mathematical statistics, a yearlong sequence in applied statistics and a course in statistical computing.

The BS program in supply chain management provides students with a deep understanding of how to manage the flow of goods, services and information across the supply chain. The curriculum provides a solid foundation in business disciplines, as well as an extensive array of general education coursework to prepare students for the demands of the global marketplace. The supply chain management major provides students with the critical skills needed for a variety of careers in purchasing, logistics, operations and supply chain management in manufacturing, retailing and service organizations. Graduates are prepared for careers in a global environment that is increasingly dependent on the ability to move goods and services from raw material suppliers to final customers.
Accreditation status: The W. P. Carey School of Business is accredited by AACSB International --- The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business. The W. P. Carey School of Business is one of the top-ranked business schools in the country, and its undergraduate, graduate and doctoral programs are internationally recognized.

Concentration name: ['Ecosystems Sustainability', 'International Development and Sustainability', 'Policy and Governance in Sustainable Systems', 'Society and Sustainability', 'Sustainable Urban Dynamics']
description:
The Bachelor of Arts in sustainability is a liberal arts-oriented degree program that addresses the challenges of sustainability through the lenses of society, culture, economics and the environment. Students develop a solid foundation in sustainability principles and theory and learn to apply their knowledge to real-world situations.

The BA in sustainability requires a foreign language and is excellent preparation for careers in the nonprofit or governmental sectors or for graduate school.

Concentration name: ['Ecosystems Sustainability', 'Economics of Sustainability', 'Energy, Materials and Technology', 'International Development and Sustainability', 'Policy and Governance in Sustainable Systems', 'Society and Sustainability', 'Sustainable Food Systems', 'Sustainable Urban Dynamics', 'The Sustainability Commons']
description:
The BS in sustainability is a transdisciplinary degree program that provides a strong foundation for students interested in devising real-world solutions to society's most pressing environmental, economic and social challenges in local, national and global contexts.

The curriculum introduces students to the concept of sustainability in the context of real-world problems. It explores the interaction of environmental, economic and social systems and the complex trade-offs that must be considered when working to solve problems and create a more sustainable future. Students develop an understanding of the concepts and principles that are central to sustainability, as well as the analytical tools and problem-solving skills necessary to address a broad range of sustainability-related issues.

Students can customize their degree by selecting one of nine unique tracks based on their own interests or by taking a broader approach and following a more generalized track of study.

The BS program in sustainable food systems gives students an in-depth, interdisciplinary education about the complex social, economic and environmental factors that affect the sustainability of food systems at local, regional and global scales. The program focuses on the science of food and food production and the economic, social and cultural dimensions of sustainable food systems. The curriculum emphasizes real-world problem-solving, equipping students with the knowledge and practical skills needed for a variety of careers in the private, public and nonprofit sectors of the food industry.

The BS program in sustainable horticulture provides students with the scientific knowledge and technical skills to design, build and manage sustainable food and landscape systems in a variety of settings. Students learn about the science and art of cultivating plants and how they are used to enhance the human environment. Students in the program develop knowledge and skills to grow and use plants sustainably in a variety of contexts, including landscape design and management, parks and natural areas, green roofs and living walls, sports and golf turf, nursery and greenhouse operations, and food production. Students gain expertise in plant biology, soil science and sustainable horticultural practices and develop a holistic understanding of how plants connect people and the environment.

The BS program in technical communication with a concentration in user experience is a hands-on, project-based program that prepares students for the challenges of a rapidly changing, technologically-oriented workplace.

Students learn to effectively communicate complex technical information to a variety of audiences by focusing on a rhetorical or user-centered approach to communication. This program has an applied focus, emphasizing problem-solving and giving students skills in content strategy, information architecture, user research, usability and creating and editing a variety of technical and digital documents, including websites.

This program is available for students to complete fully online.

The program also offers a fast-track option for students to earn both their bachelor's and master's degrees in as little as five years.

The BS program in technical communication teaches students the skills necessary to bridge the gap between subject-matter experts and those who need to understand or use the information. Technical communicators are experts in communication: writing, editing, design and research. The program focuses on how to make the complex and technical understandable to a wide range of audiences.

Technical communication students become experts in analyzing audiences to understand their needs. They use that analysis to design, write and edit a variety of genres, from traditional print documents to complex, digital media. Students work individually and in collaborative teams on real-world projects, gaining expertise in the tools and technologies used in the field.

Students also have the opportunity to focus their studies in a particular area of interest. In the user experience concentration, students learn how to research user needs and apply their findings to the design and development of websites and other digital products and services. In technical editing and publishing, students hone their language and copyediting skills. In plain language, students become adept at creating clear and concise content for government agencies and regulated industries. In science and medical communication, students apply their knowledge to communicating complex information for both specialized and lay audiences. All students in the program gain experience in writing for the web, information architecture and content strategy, and creating content for a global audience.

The BS program in technology entrepreneurship and management provides students with a foundational understanding of entrepreneurship and the innovation process. The program focuses on creating, developing and launching new technology-based ventures, and it is also beneficial to students who would like to work in large organizations in an innovation or product development role.

Students learn how to validate their ideas, research a market, build a minimum viable product and launch a business. They also learn how to pivot, based on customer feedback. The program is specifically designed to provide students with the ability to navigate the process of opportunity recognition, resource acquisition and entrepreneurial management.

Because technology entrepreneurship is a primary driver of the global economy, this program provides students with the critical skills they will need to be part of this economy in the 21st century. Additionally, this program is suitable for students who wish to pursue a social entrepreneurship venture.

Students pursuing this degree can learn about and engage in technology entrepreneurship and management within a polytechnic context. The final semester provides an opportunity for students to launch their ventures in a capstone experience.

Through iProjects, students are given a unique opportunity to find a solution to a real-world challenge. Students gain experience working in a collaborative, team-based setting, and the results have an immediate impact. Recent iProjects have included a challenge to design a renewable energy solution for a small town's street lamps in order to address public safety concerns, an effort to create a social media and web presence for a local nonprofit and the development of a marketing plan for an advanced medical device.

The BA program in theatre with a concentration in acting provides students with a foundational understanding of theatre studies and acting in a liberal arts context.

The curriculum combines a core of theatre studies with a sequence of courses in acting, voice and movement and directing. The program is designed to provide aspiring actors with a solid foundation of theory and practice. The acting concentration offers small, studio-style classes and individual attention that enables students to acquire skills and develop their craft alongside a supportive ensemble of artists and scholars.

Students who graduate with a BA in theatre with a concentration in acting have a variety of career choices. Many go on to work as professional actors, while others may choose careers in education, public relations or law. This undergraduate program also provides an excellent foundation for graduate studies in theatre and other fields.

The BA program in theatre with a concentration in design and production provides students with a broad and comprehensive view of theatre that includes hands-on experience in every area of theatrical design and production. Students take core classes in acting, dramatic literature, playwriting and script analysis, directing, and history and theory in addition to intensive coursework in design and production. Coursework is based on an inclusive, process-based approach to theatre-making.

Students receive individual attention and work closely with faculty, staff and graduate students on an ambitious season of plays and projects. Opportunities are also available to work on student-produced projects, films, dance concerts and other ASU productions. The program values collaboration, creative problem-solving and professionalism and offers a rigorous, well-rounded and nurturing environment in which all students are challenged to become their best artist-selves.

Students are trained to enter a wide variety of roles in professional theatre and related entertainment industries, including: costuming, lighting, scenery, sound, technical direction, props, stage management, scenic art. The program also prepares students for continued study in graduate school.
Accreditation status: The theatre programs are accredited by the National Association of Schools of Theatre (NAST).

description:
The BA program in theatre with a concentration in theatre and performance studies is for students who want a broad-based education in theatre and performance. Students can customize their degree by choosing from a range of electives. The program trains students as artists, scholars and cultural leaders who can use their knowledge of theatre and performance to succeed in a variety of professions and to create a more just and equitable world.

Coursework in dramatic literature, theatre history and performance studies is balanced with studio classes and production experiences in acting, design, directing, playwriting, and technology and production.

Students benefit from the program's strong connections with the professional theatre locally, nationally and internationally through professional artist residencies, internship opportunities and faculty mentorship. Students also have the opportunity to participate in and create a variety of productions, including main stage shows, student-led productions, new work development, Theatre for Youth and Community projects and other performances.

In the BA in theatre program, students learn to use theatre and performance as tools to solve local and global challenges.
Accreditation status: The ASU School of Music, Dance and Theatre is an accredited member of the National Association of Schools of Theatre.

description:
The BA program in theatre offers a course of study for students who want a broad-based education in theatre within a liberal arts context. This flexible program is ideal for students who want to combine the study of theatre with another area of interest or who are interested in pursuing a career that requires an undergraduate degree with an emphasis on communication, collaboration and creativity.

The curriculum provides a foundation in the major areas of theatre: acting, directing, design and production, and history and literature. Students then pursue their interests by taking an additional 24 credit hours of theatre electives. Courses are available in all areas of theatre studies, and they are taught by a dedicated faculty of working artists and scholars.

Students complete their studies with a one-credit hour senior capstone experience.
Accreditation status: The School of Music, Dance and Theatre is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Theatre.

description:
The Bachelor of Science in therapeutic recreation prepares students to use recreation and other activity-based interventions to improve the health, well-being and quality of life for individuals with illnesses or disabling conditions. Students learn to use the therapeutic recreation process of assessment, planning, implementation and evaluation of services in a variety of settings such as hospitals, community recreation agencies and long-term care facilities.

The curriculum is based on the standards of the National Council for Therapeutic Recreation Certification. It meets the requirements for students to be eligible to take the NCTRC exam to become a Certified Therapeutic Recreation Specialist®, which is the national credential for therapeutic recreation professionals.

Graduates are prepared for a professional career as a recreational therapist and for a number of other careers that support the health and well-being of individuals and communities.

Recreational therapists help individuals of all ages and with a wide range of medical conditions improve their overall well-being through creative activity. What recreational therapists do: evaluate a client's specific needs and interests, plan goal-oriented treatment to improve physical, cognitive and emotional well-being, use a range of activities to help improve a client's functioning and independence, and help clients to integrate into their community through recreation.

According to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, overall employment of recreational therapists is projected to grow 4% from 2021 to 2031.
Accreditation status: The therapeutic recreation program is an NCTRC-approved program. The curriculum is based on the standards of the National Council for Therapeutic Recreation Certification and meets the requirements for students to be eligible to take the NCTRC exam to become a Certified Therapeutic Recreation Specialist®, the national credential for therapeutic recreation professionals.

description:
The BS program in tourism development and management with a concentration in meetings and events provides students with the management skills and knowledge needed to become a leader in one of the world's largest and most diverse industries: tourism.

Students learn how to create and manage exceptional tourism experiences and meetings and events for a wide range of organizations, from convention and visitor bureaus and destination marketing organizations to corporate meeting departments, from third-party event planning companies to conference centers, and from resorts and hotels to nonprofit agencies and government entities. The curriculum addresses the economic, sociocultural and environmental aspects of tourism, and it has an applied, industry-relevant focus.

Throughout the program, students gain the knowledge and skills necessary to succeed as professionals in the meetings and events industry. Classes are taught by a world-renowned faculty who bring extensive professional experience to the classroom. Coursework focuses on topics such as:

destination management
event operations
leadership
marketing and sales
meeting and convention planning and management
sustainable tourism
tourism planning
The curriculum culminates in a required internship, during which students earn academic credit while gaining valuable, real-world experience.
Program name: Tourism Development and Management (Meetings and Events), BS

description:
The BS program in tourism development and management with a concentration in resort and hotel leadership teaches students to create and manage exceptional tourism experiences in resort and hotel settings around the world.

This dynamic and engaging program provides a solid foundation of professional management practices and experiential learning in the fields of hospitality, lodging and tourism. Students develop leadership skills and a customer-centric focus through specialized coursework in rooms division management, food and beverage management, financial leadership, guest experience design and destination development.

Students also gain real-world experience during the program. The School of Community Resources and Development has strong relationships with leading domestic and international resort and hotel brands. Students take part in extensive paid internship and management-in-training opportunities, interacting with top industry executives who provide mentorship and career guidance.

Graduates are prepared to assume leadership positions with national and international hotel, resort and casino brands in functional areas including rooms, food and beverage, human resources, sales, marketing and revenue management.
Program name: Tourism Development and Management (Resort and Hotel Leadership), BS

description:
The BS program in tourism development and management with a concentration in sustainable tourism provides students with the management and practical skills necessary for a career in the tourism industry.

The curriculum is designed to be student-centric and provide flexibility. Core courses develop a strong foundation of tourism knowledge. Students then select from an extensive list of electives that align with their specific career interests.

Students in the sustainable tourism concentration focus on developing sustainable tourism practices, including policy, planning and management in natural and cultural heritage sites and in rural and urban settings. Students also examine tourism in the context of economic development, sociocultural and environmental sustainability, and quality of life for residents of the host community. This program prepares graduates who can help communities and businesses create responsible and impactful visitor experiences.
Accreditation status: The tourism development and management program is accredited by the Accreditation Commission for Programs in Hospitality Administration.
Program name: Tourism Development and Management (Sustainable Tourism), BS

Concentration name: Meetings and Events, Resort and Lodging Leadership, Sustainable Tourism
description:
The BS program in tourism development and management provides students with the knowledge and skills for a successful management career in one of the largest and most diverse industries in the world: tourism.

The program features a core of courses focused on business management principles, a series of specialty tourism courses focused on the operational sectors of the industry, and a choice of one of three concentration areas: meetings and events, resort and lodging leadership, or sustainable tourism.

The curriculum allows students to integrate a strong theoretical and methodological foundation with the professional skills needed to be successful in the industry. Students study the business of tourism, including tourism's role and impact in the local and global context. They learn principles for effectively managing tourism organizations, for developing new tourism products and services, and for assessing the social, economic and environmental impacts of tourism.

A required internship provides students with the opportunity to gain relevant professional experience and apply classroom learning to real-world situations, building their professional networks and preparing them for a career in the largest industry in the world.
Accreditation status: The BS program in tourism development and management is accredited by the Accreditation Commission for Programs in Hospitality Administration.

description: The Bachelor of Arts program in transborder Chicana/o and Latina/o studies with a concentration in social justice and human rights provides students with a deep understanding of Chicana/o and Latina/o communities in the U.S. and across the Americas. The program provides the intellectual and practical skills needed to critically analyze the histories, cultures, social justice and human rights issues of these communities. Students learn to address these complex issues through a curriculum that emphasizes a transborder perspective and is grounded in scholarly and community-based research and practices. Students develop their skills and passion in classes that span the humanities, social sciences and arts, and they have opportunities to engage in experiential learning activities that provide practical experience to move on to graduate programs, professional schools or a variety of careers in the public, private and nonprofit sectors.
Program name: Transborder Chicana/o and Latina/o Studies (Social Justice and Human Rights), BA

description: The Bachelor of Arts in transborder Chicana/o and Latina/o studies with a concentration in transborder media and expressive culture is a cutting-edge interdisciplinary program focusing on Chicana/o and Latina/o expressive arts (literature, film, music, performance, visual arts) and media in the context of the U.S.-Mexico transborder region. The program gives special attention to the ways Chicana/o and Latina/o populations use expressive arts and media as a means to respond to, critique and shape social life and cultural identities. Students learn about the production, circulation and consumption of Chicana/o and Latina/o media and expressive culture in a transborder context that recognizes the social, cultural and political influence of Mexico and Latin America in the United States and vice versa.
Program name: Transborder Chicana/o and Latina/o Studies (Transborder Media and Expressive Culture), BA

description:
The BA program in transborder Chicana/o and Latina/o studies with a concentration in U.S. and Mexico borderlands provides an interdisciplinary curriculum that focuses on the U.S.-Mexico border region, its history, its peoples and its cultures.

Students are given the theoretical and practical skills to analyze the social, political, cultural and economic contexts that shape and define the U.S.-Mexico transborder space. Through coursework, research and experiential learning, students gain a comprehensive and nuanced understanding of transborder social, cultural and institutional practices and their historical and contemporary significance for Chicana/o and Latina/o communities in the U.S. Southwest and beyond.

Students take courses in social sciences and humanities that provide them with the variety of skills and knowledge needed for a comparative and transnational understanding of the U.S.-Mexico borderlands.
Program name: Transborder Chicana/o and Latina/o Studies (US and Mexico Borderlands), BA

description:
The BS program in unmanned aerial systems focuses on the knowledge and skills necessary to prepare students for careers in the rapidly growing field of unmanned aerial systems. The program provides students with a strong foundation in aviation science, flight training, data collection and analysis, and aviation safety and management, as well as hands-on experience in the operation and maintenance of unmanned aerial vehicles.
