Students learn to design, build and fly UAVs; to collect and analyze data from various sensors; and to apply their knowledge to a variety of applications, such as agriculture, construction, environmental monitoring and public safety.

The curriculum is designed to provide students with a well-rounded education that prepares them for success in the dynamic and evolving field of unmanned aerial systems.

Graduates are prepared for careers as UAV pilots, sensor operators, data analysts and managers in a variety of industries. The program also provides a strong foundation for students who wish to pursue graduate studies in aviation, engineering or related fields.

The Bachelor of Science in Planning program in urban planning helps students understand the forces that shape the quality of life in neighborhoods, cities and regions around the world.

Students learn how cities and communities work and how urban planning practices and policies can improve people's lives. Urban planners connect knowledge from many fields to specific places and communities. Students learn to think critically about the places in which they live and work and to develop professional skills to help plan better communities for the future. They examine the social, economic, physical and political factors that affect urban environments, and they gain the analytical skills necessary to develop plans and policies to address contemporary challenges.

The degree program focuses on topics such as:

- environmental quality and resource management
- housing and community development
- land use and physical planning
- public policy
- sustainable urbanism
- transportation

Students can develop specific interests and skills by choosing courses and studios from a variety of offerings. They benefit from the program's strong connections to the planning profession and from an extensive alumni network. Graduates are prepared for careers in public, private and nonprofit organizations and for graduate studies in urban planning and related fields, such as architecture, landscape architecture, public policy and public administration, creating just and sustainable futures.
Accreditation status: The Bachelor of Science in Planning degree in urban planning is accredited by the Planning Accreditation Board. The school also is a member of the Association of Collegiate Schools of Planning.

description:
The BS program in user experience provides students with the skills to create and develop engaging, accessible and usable experiences for users.

The user experience program is a multidisciplinary field, bringing together aspects of computer science, engineering, psychology, design, and art. The program prepares students to work in this evolving field by focusing on the design and evaluation of systems for end users. The curriculum is focused on user research, user interface design, information architecture, usability, accessibility, and human factors.

Students learn to apply the user-centered design process to create useful and usable products and services, including websites, mobile applications, and other interactive systems. The degree program emphasizes a hands-on, project-based learning approach through which students apply theories and skills from their coursework to a real-world design challenge.

This program is offered by the College of Integrative Sciences and Arts.

Concentration name: Small Animal, Equine, Food and Fiber Animal
description: The Doctor of Veterinary Medicine program is a robust, four-year program that will prepare students for a successful career in veterinary medicine. Our innovative curriculum is built upon a student-centered, evidence-based and instructional-best-practices model. The program is designed to equip graduates with the knowledge and skills necessary to be day-one-ready veterinarians who will be competitive in the 21st century veterinary marketplace. Graduates will be prepared to excel in a variety of careers in private practice, industry, and government, and be leaders in the veterinary medical profession.
Accreditation status: The Arizona State University College of Veterinary Medicine is accredited by the American Veterinary Medical Association (AVMA) Council on Education (COE).

description:
The BA program in women and gender studies is a flexible, interdisciplinary program that focuses on the past and present of women and the role of gender in shaping lives, histories and cultures.

Students examine the ways in which sex and gender are socially constructed, and how these constructions intersect with other social identities such as race, ethnicity, class, nationality and sexuality. The curriculum reflects the latest scholarship in the humanities, social sciences and natural sciences, bringing to light women's contributions to culture and society and examining the operations of gender and power in people's lives.

Students examine and analyze a variety of political, historical, cultural and economic issues from a feminist perspective, including reproductive rights, violence against women and the gendered division of labor.

Courses offered are from a variety of fields, including:
- anthropology
- communication
- economics
- English
- history
- justice studies
- philosophy
- political science
- psychology
- religious studies
- social work
- sociology

Graduates of this program are especially well-prepared for graduate study as well as for careers in a wide range of fields in which knowledge of gender issues is important, such as education, counseling, social services, law, public policy and business. The program also fosters leadership skills, social consciousness and a commitment to social justice.

Concentration name: Creative Writing, Professional and Public Writing
description:
The Bachelor of Arts in writing, rhetorics and literacies explores the power of the written and spoken word across a range of genres and settings. The program helps students understand that writing is a creative and intellectual act achieved through a process of inquiry, discovery and revision. Students learn how to analyze and produce a wide range of texts and genres for different purposes and audiences in professional, public and creative contexts.

The curriculum emphasizes a deep understanding of audience, context, genre and persuasion and provides students with extensive practice developing their skills as writers, readers and thinkers in a variety of modes and media. In addition to a broad grounding in writing, rhetorical and literacy studies, students also pursue a concentration in either creative writing or professional and public writing.

Students who concentrate in creative writing study across the genres of fiction, nonfiction and poetry, developing their craft as writers and their critical understanding of the literary arts. Students who concentrate in professional and public writing study how writing works in professional settings (e.g., business, science, government) and public spaces (e.g., social media, community organizing, advocacy).

All students in the major complete a capstone course in which they work closely with faculty to develop a substantial, independent project that showcases their abilities as writers, readers and critical thinkers. Both concentrations provide an excellent foundation for any career that requires strong communication, writing and critical thinking skills, as well as for graduate study in a number of fields, from creative writing and composition and rhetoric to communication, law and the study of how texts work in the world.
